text:
I am submitting this complaint regarding a JPMCB Card account that is currently reporting on my credit file as a charge-off with a reported balance of approximately {$460.00}. I am formally stating that I do not own this account. I did not open this account, I did not authorize anyone to open it on my behalf, and I did not benefit from any credit extended under this account. This account is the result of identity theft.

I became aware of this JPMCB Card charge-off after reviewing my credit report and noticing a derogatory tradeline reflecting a balance of approximately {$460.00} that had been charged off. Although the balance is smaller compared to other fraudulent accounts discovered, the presence of any charge-off is extremely damaging to my credit profile. A charge-off indicates severe delinquency and default, and it creates the false impression that I failed to repay a legitimate debt. That is not accurate in this case.

I have never knowingly applied for or opened a JPMCB credit card account corresponding to the account being reported. I did not sign any credit application, cardmember agreement, or authorize any extension of credit in my name with JPMCB for this account. I did not make purchases, receive statements, or otherwise use the credit associated with this account.

Upon discovering this account, I immediately took steps to protect myself. I filed an Identity Theft Report with the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), formally documenting that this JPMCB Card account was opened fraudulently using my personal information. I also initiated disputes with the credit reporting agencies, clearly stating that this account does not belong to me and was the result of identity theft.

Despite filing the FTC Identity Theft Report and submitting formal disputes, this JPMCB Card charge-off continues to report on my credit file. The continued reporting of this fraudulent account is causing ongoing harm to my creditworthiness and financial stability.

The reporting reflects delinquency prior to charge-off. I did not make late payments on this account because I did not open it and was unaware of its existence. The negative payment history associated with this account does not reflect my financial behavior but instead reflects fraudulent activity carried out by an unknown third party.

After discovering the account, I requested that JPMCB provide documentation
proving that I personally opened and authorized this account. Specifically, I requested : A copy of the original signed credit application or cardmember agreement.

Documentation showing the identity verification procedures used at the time the account was opened.

Copies of any identification documents allegedly submitted.

Complete account statements from inception through charge-off.

Documentation showing how the {$460.00} balance was calculated.

To date, I have not received original signed documentation bearing my authorization. I have not received proof that I entered into a contractual relationship with JPMCB for this account. Any response stating that the account was verified is not sufficient to establish responsibility, especially after a formal identity theft report has been filed.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), both furnishers and credit reporting agencies are required to ensure maximum possible accuracy of the information
they report. Reporting an account as belonging to me when I did not open or authorize it violates this standard. Furthermore, under Section 605B of the FCRA, when a consumer submits a valid Identity Theft Report, the credit reporting agencies must block the reporting of fraudulent information unless they determine the report is false or based on misrepresentation.

I have complied with all necessary steps to assert my rights as a victim of identity theft. I filed the FTC Identity Theft Report and formally disputed the account. The continued reporting of this JPMCB charge-off suggests that proper blocking procedures were not followed or that a meaningful investigation was not
conducted.

It is concerning that this account progressed to charge-off status without me being aware of its existence. If the account was opened online or electronically, I request review of : IP address logs associated with the application.

Device identification data.

Email addresses and phone numbers used in the application.

Records of identity authentication steps taken at approval.

If the account was opened in person, I request copies of any identification documents presented at that time and records of identity verification performed by JPMCB.

The financial impact of even a relatively small charge-off is significant. Credit scoring models do not consider only the balance ; they heavily weigh the presence of charge-offs and derogatory tradelines. The reporting of this account lowers my credit score and negatively affects lending decisions.

In addition to financial harm, this situation has caused emotional distress. Discovering that my personal information was used to open unauthorized credit accounts is alarming. I have taken responsible and immediate action to correct this issue, but the burden of removing fraudulent information should not rest solely on the victim. If JPMCB believes that this account belongs to me, I request that they provide
detailed documentation demonstrating : The exact date the account was opened.

The method of application ( online, phone, in-branch ).

The identity verification procedures used.

Copies of any signed agreements bearing my signature.

Proof that I personally authorized charges associated with the account.

Without such documentation, there is no legitimate basis for continuing to report this account as mine. I also request clarification as to whether this account has been sold, transferred,
or assigned to any third-party collection agencies. If so, I request documentation of the chain of assignment and confirmation that the identity theft dispute was communicated to any third parties involved. Selling or transferring a fraudulent account without proper notice perpetuates harm.

The Fair Credit Reporting Act was enacted to protect consumers from inaccurate and fraudulent reporting. The continued reporting of this JPMCB charge-off undermines the purpose of the law and causes unjust harm.

I have acted responsibly by reviewing my credit report, filing an FTC Identity Theft Report, and submitting formal disputes. I am fully cooperating and willing to provide additional documentation to support my claim.

The dispute process must involve a meaningful investigation that includes review of original documentation and verification records. Simply confirming information with an automated system is not sufficient when identity theft has been reported.

If JPMCB can not produce documentation showing that I personally opened and authorized this account, the only appropriate resolution is permanent deletion from my credit file.

I am not attempting to avoid legitimate debt. If I had opened and used this JPMCB Card account, I would take responsibility for it. However, I can not and should not be held responsible for a debt incurred through identity theft.

The resolution I am seeking in this complaint is recognition that this JPMCB Card charge-off was opened fraudulently, correction of the inaccurate reporting, and restoration of accuracy to my credit profile.

I respectfully request that JPMCB conduct a thorough and meaningful investigation into this matter and take corrective action consistent with federal consumer protection laws.

I appreciate the opportunity to formally document this issue and request corrective action. I look forward to receiving a written response explaining the findings of the investigation and confirming that the fraudulent JPMCB Card charge-off has been removed.

text:
I am filing a second complaint against Citibank regarding a personal loan application that was formally approved and, after XXXX days of not being able to accept it due to an internal system failure, they let it expire. Now, I reapplied using exactly the same information that resulted in the previous approval, and Citi has denied my application. 

For context : Citibank approved my loan application and confirmed that, in their system, the loan was pending acceptance, and the credit line showed as available ( XXXX ). However, when I attempted to log in and accept the loan terms, their platform consistently fails and does not allow me to proceed, asking me to call them. This issue is entirely on Citibanks side and prevents me from accessing an already approved financial product. 

Over the past 22 days, I have contacted Citibank XXXX times through their customer service channels and personal bankers. Despite these repeated efforts : No representative has been able to resolve the issue. 
I have not received any meaningful update or estimated timeline. 
The only response I consistently receive is that I must wait for the Tech Department to fix the issue, '' since " it is clearly a Technical Issue on our side. '' They got extremely rude asking me to stop calling and wait XXXX hours for a representative to call me ( which has not happened ). 

This response is not acceptable. Citibank has failed to provide a functional mechanism to accept the loan, yet continued to treat the application as time-sensitive and finally it let it expire. 

Compounding the issue, Citibank conducted a hard inquiry on my credit report as part of the application process. I was informed that if I do not accept the loan within 21 days, they will require a new application and an additional hard credit inquiry. This of course has negatively impact my credit scoredespite the fact that I was absolutely unable to accept the loan, and no Citibank employee could fix the issue, solely due to Citibanks internal system malfunction. 

This situation creates an unfair and unreasonable outcome : 1. I had an approved loan that I can not access.

2. I faced credit harm due to circumstances entirely outside my control.

3. Citibank did not provid a workaround, escalation path, or resolution timeline.

4. Citibank let the approval expired.

5. Now Citibank has conducted a new credit inquiry and has rejected my new loan application, which had exactly the same information as the application that was previously approved.

This matter reflects a breakdown in Citibanks digital onboarding process and a complete failure to protect consumers from avoidable credit harm. 

After XXXX weeks and a first complaint filed, Citibank replied on XX/XX/year>. Frankly, Citis response was deeply unsatisfactory and fails to address the actual substance of my complaint. Rather than engaging with the factual background I provided, Citi issued a generic and conclusory response that ignores the operational reality I have been dealing with for nearly four weeks. At no point did I claim that my loan application was denied. The issue is precisely the opposite : Citi approved the loan, but I had repeatedly been unable to complete the acceptance process because Citis own system fails during the electronic bank account verification stage. This has occurred consistently and repeatedly despite numerous attempts over approximately 24 days. Several Citi employees have also tried to complete the loan application on the phone and in person in a New York branch, and the same error appeared. Most concerning, Citi now states in its CFPB response that it confirmed that there were no system errors or issues on Citibanks end. That assertion is directly contradicted by the facts and what multiple Citi representatives and supervisors told me during numerous phone calls. Throughout this process, Citi agents repeatedly acknowledged that the issue appeared to be technical in nature, that the application was stuck in the system, and that they were escalating the matter to technical support because they themselves could not resolve it. If, as Citi now claims, there was never any system issue, then I request that Citi explain : ( 1 ) why multiple representatives stated that the matter had to be escalated to technical support ; ( 2 ) why no representative was ever able to complete the electronic acceptance process despite repeated attempts ; ( 3 ) why I was repeatedly instructed to wait for the tech team ; ( 4 ) why the issue was unresolved after more than three weeks later ; and ( 5 ) why Citibank has now denied my new loan application under the exact same information they approved XXXX XXXX weeks ago. 

Citis response also entirely disregards the central concern raised in my complaint : that I was exposed to the risk of expiration of an approved loan offer, and now to a second hard credit inquiry, because Citis process was not functioning properly in practice regardless of whether Citi now labels it a system error.

Moreover, Citis proposed solution namely, requiring me after weeks of failed attempts to abandon the electronic process and instead complete a paper-check workaround only further demonstrates that Citi was unable to make the approved electronic acceptance process function properly. The CFPB should note that Citis response does not meaningfully address the repeated failed attempts, the contradictory information provided by Citi representatives, the lack of any effective escalation path, the substantial amount of time spent attempting to resolve an issue that Citi now broadly dismisses without explanation ; and the recent denial of the new application under the same circumstances I had been approved XXXX weeks ago.

This is not a duplicate complaint of any previously resolved complaint. 
Complaint Against Exeter Finance LLC Violations of the Dodd-Frank Act ( 12 U.S.C. 5531, UDAAP ) I am attempting to volunatrily surrender a vehicle securing an auto loan with Exeter Finance LLC. Exeter Finance LLC is refusing to provide a workable written process to complete the voluntary surrender unless I engage in telephone communication, resulting in ongoing financial harm due to continued accrual of interest, fees, and insurance costs. 

I am submitting this complaint against Exeter Finance LLC for engaging in what appear to be unfair and abusive acts or practices in violation of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, specifically 12 U.S.C. 5531, which prohibits Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ). Exeter Finance LLCs conduct meets the statutory definitions of both unfair and abusive practices under federal law.

This matter concerns Exeter Finance LLCs refusal to process my voluntary surrender of a vehicle securing my loan, despite multiple documented written requests and my consistent use of the companys own designated secure communication channel. 

The vehicle securing this loan is a XXXX XXXX XXXX, financed through Exeter Finance LLC since XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXX/XX/XXXX, I submitted my first written request through Exeters XXXX of the XXXX secure messaging portal to initiate a voluntary surrender and to obtain the required instructions and documentation. Rather than responding to the substance of this request, Exeter directed me to contact their customer service department by telephone. 

I continued to act in good faith and submitted additional written requests on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX through the same secure portal. These requests were not substantively addressed. In a response dated XX/XX/XXXX, provided to both myself and the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Exeter Finance LLC stated that I have the option to voluntarily surrender the vehicle. Despite this acknowledgment, the company failed to provide any written instructions or means to complete the surrender when requested to proceed with voluntary surrender. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted another written request. In its response to both myself and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Exeter Finance LLC stated that I may have the option to voluntarily surrender, while continuing to require that I engage in telephone communication as a condition of proceeding. 

At all times, I have used the same secure messaging platform that Exeter Finance LLC itself uses to communicate with me. I have also previously revoked consent for telephone communication. Despite this, Exeter has refused to process the voluntary surrender or provide written instructions unless I agree to communicate by phone. 

Additionally, I received a Right to Cure notice via Certified Mail from the XXXX. Postal Service from Exeter Finance LLC dated XX/XX/XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX This notice indicated that the account was in default status and provided a deadline to cure the alleged default before further collection or repossession actions may proceed. This escalation occurred while I had already made multiple documented good-faith written requests to voluntarily surrender the vehicle through Exeters secure messaging portal. 

Despite my ongoing efforts to resolve the matter through voluntary surrender, Exeter Finance LLC did not provide written instructions to complete the surrender process and instead continues to require telephone communication as a condition of proceeding. As a result, the account was simultaneously being escalated toward repossession while I have been actively attempting to voluntarily surrender the collateral in writing. This appears to further demonstrate unfairness, and abusiveness. This sequence of events shows the delay in processing the voluntary surrender request, and that it is not attributable to a lack of intent or cooperation on my part. To whom it may concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding Chase Autos handling of my refinance application ( XXXX ) submitted on or about XX/XX/XXXX. I am also filing a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). 
The facts outlined below demonstrate conduct that appears to violate the Dodd-Frank Acts prohibition against Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ), as well as applicable provisions of Regulation Z and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ). 

Chase repeatedly represented that I was approved for refinancing, provided specific loan terms, and communicated a clear validity window ( initially described as 60 days and later reflected as expiring XX/XX/XXXX ). I relied on those representations. To then deny the loan today on the basis that my vehicle aged or that mileage increased during the very timeframe Chase established is inherently contradictory. 

If vehicle aging or mileage fluctuation during the offer period was a material underwriting risk, that risk should have been accounted for when the approval window was set or clearly disclosed as a condition that could void the approval. A lender can not extend a defined acceptance period, repeatedly confirm approval, and then rescind based on predictable passage of time within that same period. That is the functional equivalent of a bait-and-switch : representing that credit is approved and available through a stated deadline, while internally reserving the ability to withdraw it for foreseeable and undisclosed reasons. 

Timeline of events : XX/XX/XXXX I applied for a Chase auto refinance and submitted all required personal and credit information, including my Social Security number and vehicle details.

US Bank, in partnership with XXXX , issues a branded XXXX credit card that advertises rewards points for every purchase made using the card. These rewards points are marketed as having a cash-equivalent value and can be redeemed accordingly. Under the program terms, points expire three years after they are earned. 
Up to approximately XXXX, the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX portal clearly displayed the number of reward points scheduled to expire, including the applicable expiration timeframe. This information was readily accessible to the cardholder without any additional effort. 
In XXXX, US Bank removed this information from the online portal. Instead, the number of points scheduled to expire was displayed only on the monthly credit card statement. 
By XXXX, US Bank further reduced transparency. Monthly statements no longer disclosed the number of points scheduled to expire. Instead, the statements contained only a generic notice stating that points expire by the end of the year, without providing any numerical point balance or identifying which points were at risk of expiration. 
At that point, the only way to obtain specific information about expiring points was to call the US Bank customer service XXXX number. The automated phone system is confusing, rigid, and highly resistant to routing callers to a live representative. The automated system does not provide information regarding expiring reward points and repeatedly blocks access to a human agent. It is extremely difficultborderline impossiblefor an average customer to obtain this information through automated means. 
After significant effort, I was eventually able to reach a live customer service representative. Only then was I able to obtain the specific details regarding my expiring rewards points. 

Based on this progression, it is clear that US Bank has intentionally removed meaningful access to information about expiring rewards points over time. As visibility has been reduced, customers are more likely to forget about expiring points, resulting in the forfeiture of cash-equivalent value. Those forfeited points are retained by the bank, effectively converting unredeemed customer rewards into bank profit. 

It is my opinion that these rewards points represent my property, earned through card usage as advertised by US Bank and XXXX XXXX As such, the bank has an obligation to clearly and proactively disclose what rewards belong to me and what portion of those rewards is at risk of expiration. I should not be required to navigate a hostile automated phone system or affirmatively request information in order to know what I own and what I stand to lose. 
The progressive removal of this informationfrom the web portal, to statements, to -total obscurityundermines transparency and deprives customers of a fair opportunity to redeem their earned rewards.

I have been a Navy Federal Credit Union ( NFCU ) member for more than 25 years. I am filing this complaint against NFCU regarding their gross mishandling of a fraudulent wire transfer recall, leading to a ( likely avoidable ) loss of more than {$120000.00}.

Their story seemed believable as I had been in contact with the actual NFCU Fraud Department earlier in the year due to possible fraudulent activity on my NFCU credit card. However the criminals had secretly transferred the money from my personal account to the joint account before directing me to send the fraudulent wire. 

I recognized the fraud the same day ( XX/XX/XXXX ) and reported it NFCU less than 12 hours after the transfer. Per subsequent conversations with XXXX  XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, the receiving institution ) the transfer was recognized as fraudulent, the transfer was rejected and the money never posted to the recipients account. I even escalated my concerns to the NFCU Executive Resolution Team ( who simply referred me back to the same Wire Fraud team. ) They continued to blame XXXX. It wasn't until I threatened to take the matter to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX that they reopened their investigation, resulting in the eventual recovery of less than 10 % of the wire transfer amount more than 3 months after the fraudulent transfer took place. text:
I am submitting this complaint regarding Scratchpays failure to clearly disclose material terms and consequences related to my loan and promotional interest waived offer, as well as confusing and inconsistent account documentation. 

In early XX/XX/year>, I was approved for a Scratchpay loan under XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. The loan documents dated XX/XX/year> show an amount financed of {$9900.00}, an APR of 32.90 %, and a 6 month interest waived promotional offer, under which the interest would effectively be waived if I made the required payments on time and paid the balance within the promotional period. 

In XX/XX/year>, I began experiencing financial hardship and needed a little extra time to make my XX/XX/XXXX payment. Before the situation got worse, I contacted Scratchpay on XX/XX/XXXX through their system and requested a short extension. I had been making my payments before this issue, and I was trying to be proactive and communicate my circumstances. 

Scratchpay responded to my request and advised that they could not change the due date unless the account was current. In that same communication, they stated they would waive the late fee as a one time courtesy. They also included several notes and warnings about the account, including that reminders would continue, that the account had a 2 day grace period before a late fee was generated, and that a due date change would remain as the new due date going forward. 

However, Scratchpay did not clearly tell me in that communication that failure to make the payment by the required deadline would cause me to lose eligibility for the 6 month interest waived promotional offer. This was the most important consequence, and it was never disclosed to me in response to my hardship inquiry, despite the fact that Scratchpay knew I was specifically asking for help because I needed more time. 

I later made the XXXX payment on XX/XX/year>. After doing so, I logged into my account and discovered that my monthly payment had increased substantially and that my balance had increased by more than {$2000.00}. This was the first time I realized that I had lost the promotional benefit and that interest had been applied in a way I was not expecting. 

On XX/XX/year>, I called Scratchpay to dispute what happened. During that call, I explained that I had proactively reached out, disclosed hardship, and requested help before things escalated, but was never told that I could lose the promotional offer if payment was not made by a certain date. During that call, a supervisor told me that my account had been dropped from the promotional offer on XX/XX/year> due to nonpayment. That specific deadline had never been clearly disclosed to me beforehand. Had Scratchpay simply told me that I needed to make the payment by XX/XX/year> in order to preserve the promotion, I would have done everything possible to make that happen. 

I understand that Scratchpay may point to language in the loan documents regarding the conditions of the promotional offer, which is still vague in terms of what is considered an on-time payment. My complaint is that when I directly contacted Scratchpay to explain hardship and ask for help, they gave me written account specific guidance, waived the late fee, and listed other warnings, but still failed to clearly disclose the single most material consequence, which was that I was about to lose the interest waived promotion entirely. That omission caused substantial financial harm. 

Separately, and only recently discovered by me, I also found that my Scratchpay account documents reflect a second plan ID, XXXX XXXXXXXX, along with an Adverse Action Notice dated XX/XX/year>. That notice states that records show I applied for a Scratchpay plan on XX/XX/year> and was not approved for the amount requested at that time. This is confusing because my funded loan appears to be the XX/XX/year> loan under XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. I did not discuss this separate adverse action notice with Scratchpay during my prior calls because I only realized this issue later when reviewing my account documents. Scratchpay has not clearly explained why there are two separate plan IDs, whether the XX/XX/XXXX notice related to a second application, a request for a different amount, or some other credit decision. This creates further confusion and reflects poor and inconsistent disclosure practices.

Despite formally acknowledging Complainants status as a confirmed successor in interest to the property at XXXX XXXX XXXX, SPS and XXXX XXXX proceeded with a foreclosure, denied Complainant all federally mandated protections, and made misrepresentations in multiple court proceedings. 

Factual Background : XXXX. Property Acquisition and Loan History : Complainant acquired title to the property at _XXXX XXXX XXXX, via a quitclaim deed dated XX/XX/XXXX, and recorded on XX/XX/XXXX. The original borrower obtained the mortgage on XX/XX/XXXX. The original Borrower 's personal liability on the mortgage note was discharged in a XXXX XXXX bankruptcy proceeding, with the discharge order entered on XX/XX/XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Bankruptcy Court, XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. SPS has been the loan XXXXervicer since XX/XX/XXXX. Complainant has made payments on this loan totaling approximately {$10000.00}. 

XXXX. Confirmation as Successor in Interest : On XX/XX/XXXX, after Complainant provided documentation of ownership interest, SPS sent formal written correspondence explicitly confirming Complainants status. The letter states : SPS has added " Complainant '' as an authorized third party to the above-referenced account. As an authorized third party, they will be granted access to all account information and are authorized to make any changes to the account. This written confirmation legally established Complainant as a confirmed successor in interest under RESPA ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.31 ), entitling Complainant to the same rights and protections as the original borrower. 

XXXX. Foreclosure and Denial of RESPA Rights : Despite this written confirmation, SPS and XXXX XXXX proceeded with a foreclosure sale on XX/XX/XXXX, and recorded a Sheriffs Deed on XX/XX/XXXX. Complainant was not treated as a confirmed successor ; instead, SPS sent generic occupant notices, in violation of their duty to provide specific notice to a known successor. 

XXXX. Defective Foreclosure : The foreclosure contained procedural defects. The Notice of Default was issued on XX/XX/XXXX, purportedly on behalf of XXXX XXXX. However, XXXX XXXX did not acquire any recorded interest in the mortgage until XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX than XXXX months after the default was declared. SPS initiated foreclosure as an attorney-in-fact for a principal ( XXXX XXXX ) that had no recorded interest in the property at that time. 

XXXX. Settlement Agreement : On XX/XX/XXXX, a Settlement Agreement was executed between the original borrower, SPS, and XXXX XXXX, which released all claims related to the foreclosure. Pursuant to this agreement, SPS issued a XXXX Settlement payment to the original Borrower. A logical outcome of this Settlement was the discharge of the underlying mortgage Lien. However, SPS and XXXX XXXX have not recorded a discharge of the Lien, leaving a cloud on the Title. 

XXXX. Misrepresentations in Litigation : In multiple court proceedings, including the current Quiet Title action ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ), counsel for SPS and XXXX XXXX have represented that Complainant is a stranger to the mortgage to deny standing, despite their own XX/XX/XXXX, letter confirming Complainants status. Furthermore, at a hearing on XX/XX/XXXX, their counsel stated that Complainant had failed to make a Court-ordered Escrow paymenta statement immediately proven false by the court docket. 


IV. SPECIFIC VIOLATIONS OF FEDERAL LAW XXXX. RESPA Violation Failure to Recognize Confirmed Successor Status ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.38 ) SPS violated RESPA by failing to treat Complainant as a borrower after confirming successor-in-interest status in writing on XX/XX/XXXX. Under 12 C.F.R. 1024.38 ( b ) ( 1 ) ( vi ), a servicer must facilitate communication with successors. SPS had an affirmative duty to provide Complainant with borrower-level notices and protections but instead proceeded with foreclosure. 

XXXX. RESPA Violation Inadequate Successor Notice ( 12 U.S.C. 2605 ; 12 C.F.R. 1024.38 ) SPS knew Complainant was the confirmed successor in interest. Yet they provided only generic occupant notices regarding foreclosure. A confirmed successor is entitled to the same specific notices as the original borrower. This failure to provide adequate notice deprived Complainant of the ability to exercise established rights. 

XXXX. RESPA Violation Failure to Provide Loss Mitigation & Dual Tracking ( CFPB Mortgage Servicing Rules ) As a confirmed successor in interest, Complainant is considered a borrower for purposes of loss mitigation under 12 C.F.R. 1024.41. SPS did not provide an opportunity to apply for loss mitigation options or conduct any required review. By proceeding with foreclosure sale while Complainant was communicating with them about rights, SPS engaged in prohibited dual tracking. 

XXXX. FDCPA Violations Debt Collection Abuses by SPS ( 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. ) SPS has acted as a debt collector throughout this process. Their counsel admitted this in a XX/XX/XXXX, email stating, This firm is a debt collector attempting to collect a debt. SPS violated the FDCPA by : - Attempting to collect on a debt for which personal liability was extinguished by XXXX XXXX XXXX bankruptcy discharge ( 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ) ). 
- Using misrepresentations to collect a debt by misrepresenting the validity of the debt and their legal authority to foreclose ( 1692e ( 10 ) ). 

XXXX. Pattern of Misrepresentation and Servicer Misconduct The actions of SPS and XXXX XXXX suggest a pattern of non-compliance. This includes : - Misrepresenting Complainants legal status in court proceedings after confirming successor status in writing. 
- Initiating foreclosure with a chain of Title that appears defective, using a notice of default that predates their recorded interest.

I am filing this follow-up complaint regarding my XXXX XXXX issued by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) and serviced by Continental Finance Company ( XXXX  ). 

The companys response failed to address the core issue of my complaint : the excessive and predatory nature of the fees being charged on this account and the lack of any meaningful accommodation despite financial hardship. 

XXXX claims a Change in Terms notice was sent on XX/XX/year>, adding a {$12.00} monthly maintenance fee. However, merely stating that a notice was mailed does not resolve whether the disclosure was clear, conspicuous, reasonable, or compliant with consumer protection standards. I do not recall receiving adequate notice that such significant recurring fees would be imposed on an already high-fee account.

The account already carries substantial costs, including annual fees and interest charges. Adding a recurring monthly maintenance fee creates an unfair and abusive financial burden that disproportionately impacts consumers already experiencing hardship. The company further stated that the only available option to reduce fees and interest is to permanently close the account. This is not a reasonable accommodation and effectively forces consumers into account closure to escape excessive charges.

I believe these practices may violate the spirit and intent of the Truth in Lending Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ), which requires meaningful and transparent disclosure of credit terms, as well as prohibitions against unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices under the Consumer Financial Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. 5531.

Additionally, under Arizona consumer protection principles, consumers are entitled to fair dealing and truthful business practices. Imposing layered maintenance fees on subprime credit products while refusing reasonable hardship relief appears excessive and unconscionable.

The companys response also failed to provide : * Proof that the Change in Terms notice was actually delivered ; * Evidence that I affirmatively agreed to the additional monthly maintenance fee ; * Any reasonable hardship assistance while keeping the account open; * Any explanation as to why such excessive fees are justified.

Desired Resolution : * Removal or permanent waiver of the monthly maintenance fee ; * Waiver or reduction of the annual fee as a hardship accommodation ; * Refund of any recently assessed maintenance fees; * Written confirmation that no additional maintenance fees will be added while the account remains in good standing; * A good-faith review of the account for fair consumer treatment.

I respectfully request the CFPB review whether these fee practices are unfair, deceptive, and abusive toward consumers.
label: Credit card

text:
Risk Management That Creates Risk : Barclays Credit Limit Reduction Experience Ive had a deeply disappointing experience with Barclays US Consumer Bank and their handling of my JetBlue Plus Card account.

Without prior warning, Barclays reduced my credit limit from {$23000.00} to {$8000.00}. This action instantly drove my utilization on the account to 100 %, materially impacting my credit profile, not due to new behavior, but due to their unilateral decision. 

When I contacted them, I was informed the decision was based in part on : A single ~ {$800.00} collections account currently under active dispute with TransUnion, for which I have supporting documentation Elevated utilization across accounts ( which their own action significantly worsened ) I approached the conversation professionally and in good faith. I requested a modest adjustment, restoring the limit to even {$10000.00}, to bring utilization to a more reasonable level while I finalize repayment of balances ( which I am in a position to do imminently due to an upcoming liquidity event ), and citing my perfect payment history over the years that I have done business with them. 

That request was declined without meaningful consideration or flexibility. 

Whats most concerning is not the existence of risk controls, those are expected, but the lack of proportionality and communication. A sudden, drastic limit reduction that directly worsens a customers credit standing, combined with a refusal to engage constructively when the customer demonstrates both intent and capacity to resolve the issue, reflects poorly on Barclays approach to customer management. 

I would caution prospective customers ; especially those who value stability and predictability in their credit relationships, to consider this risk when choosing a card issuer. 

Based on this experience, I do not plan to continue my relationship with Barclays once my balances are resolved. 

This approach creates a feedback loop where customers are penalized in ways that increase risk metrics rather than reduce them. Thats not risk management ; its risk amplification.

text:
I. BACKGROUND AND SUMMARY I am writing in connection with a formal billing dispute I opened regarding a payment of {$680.00} made via United States Postal Service ( USPS ) Money Order No. XXXX, submitted to the Citi payment address on file specifically, Citi Cards, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, PA XXXX which was confirmed by XXXX as XXXX on XX/XX/year>. 

Despite repeated attempts to resolve this matter including multiple phone calls, two written submissions ( first via regular mail, then via email and fax on XX/XX/year>XXXX   and XX/XX/year>XXXX   ), and clear documentary evidence Citi has : failed to apply the payment to my account ; closed and/or denied my dispute without providing any written explanation or evidence supporting its findings; reported my account as delinquent for two missed payments to credit reporting agencies ; assessed late fees and interest charges as a direct result of its own failure to apply this payment ; and failed to conduct a proper, timely, or lawful investigation of this billing error. 

I am writing this letter as a formal, legally-noticed dispute under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666 et seq., and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., to demand immediate corrective action. 

II. DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE SUBMITTED The following evidence has been provided to Citi twice and is referenced in this letter : 1. USPS Money Order No. XXXX, dated XX/XX/year>, in the amount of {$680.00}, made payable to Citi Cards at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, PA XXXX the Citi-designated payment address. This is the address printed on the money order itself. 
2. USPS Letter dated XX/XX/year>, confirming receipt of my PS Form-6401 Money Order Inquiry and providing a copy of the cashed money order showing the endorsement and payee information. 
3. USPS General Accounting Branch letter dated XX/XX/year>XXXX  ( Inquiry ID : XXXX ), confirming that Money Order No. XXXX was cashed on XX/XX/year>, and that no replacement check will be issued because the money order was in fact cashed. 
4. USPS receipt dated XX/XX/year>, showing the {$21.00} fee paid to file a Money Order Inquiry ( PS Form-6401 ) at the XXXX XXXX XXXX NJ Post Office . 
5. Citi Case Number XXXX stamped on the original USPS letter, confirming Citi had already received and associated this evidence with my prior dispute and then failed to act on it. 

III. THE CRITICAL FACTS CITI HAS IGNORED The evidence is unambiguous and raises a critical question that Citi has yet to answer : who cashed this money order?

The money order was addressed to and delivered to a Citi-controlled XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, PA ) XXXX This is not a public or shared address it is a locked USPS XXXX XXXX that can only be accessed by an individual or entity with a key issued by USPS. This was confirmed by USPS guidance provided to me at the time of my inquiry. 

The money order was cashed. USPS confirmed this. The image of the cashed money order including the endorsement was retrieved from the Federal Reserve Bank and sent to me by the USPS General Accounting Branch. The person who endorsed and cashed this money order had access to Citi 's PO Box and presented a valid form of identification. 

There are only two logical conclusions : either ( 1 ) a Citi employee or authorized party cashed this money order and failed to apply it to my account, or ( 2 ) there was a serious internal control failure at Citi. In either case, I am not responsible for the non-application of this payment, and Citi must credit my account immediately.

IV. CITI 'S VIOLATIONS OF FEDERAL LAW A. Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666 Under the FCBA, upon receipt of a written billing error notice, a creditor must : ( 1 ) acknowledge receipt within 30 days ; ( 2 ) resolve the dispute within two billing cycles ( not to exceed 90 days ) ; and ( 3 ) not take adverse action on the account ( including reporting delinquency or charging interest/late fees ) on the disputed amount during the investigation. 

Citi has violated all three obligations. My dispute has been pending for months. Citi has reported my account delinquent, charged late fees and interest on the disputed amount, and prematurely closed the dispute allegedly referring the case internally to the wrong department, as Citi representatives admitted to me by phone. 

B. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 Citi, as a furnisher of information, is prohibited from reporting information it knows or has reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate. Reporting my account as having two missed payments when the payment in question was confirmed by USPS as having been cashed by a party with access to Citi 's own PO Box is the reporting of inaccurate information in violation of the FCRA.

I am submitting a complaint regarding Credit Acceptance Corporation ( Account XXXX. XXXX ) based on ongoing and newly discovered issues following my prior CFPB complaint ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ). This matter involves continued misrepresentation, improper notice, and inaccurate information regarding the status and recoverability of my vehicle. 

In my prior CFPB complaint, I clearly expressed my intent to resolve the account, reinstate the loan, and regain possession of the vehicle. I specifically requested a pause of any sale activity and the opportunity to cure the account and redeem the vehicle.

Despite this, Credit Acceptance continued to represent to me that I would be able to regain possession of the vehicle through payment arrangements. These representations occurred multiple times, including last week and again this week, leading me to believe that recovery or redemption remained a viable option. 

The vehicle was sold on XX/XX/year>. 

Despite the sale, I continued to receive information indicating that recovery of the vehicle was still possible. In Credit Acceptances formal response to my prior CFPB complaint, they instructed me to contact them to discuss redeeming the vehicle. Relying on that instruction, I contacted the company and was told to log into my account and pay the balance in order to redeem the vehicle. 

However, because the vehicle had already been sold on XX/XX/year>, redemption was no longer legally possible under XXXX XXXX. Directing me to log in and pay to redeem the vehicle after the sale constitutes materially inaccurate and misleading information. 

On the following day, I contacted Credit Acceptance again and was instructed to call back three separate times. During those calls, I received inconsistent and incomplete information regarding recovery or resolution. On the final call, I was informed that there was nothing I could do. This sequence demonstrates that multiple representatives continued to communicate recovery-related options even after the vehicle had already been sold, followed by a complete reversal within the same day. Additionally, the companys prior investigation failed to account for this. The in
vestigator should have had access to the vehicles sale status, yet recovery and redemption were still communicated to me multiple times. This raises concerns regarding internal controls, record accuracy, and compliance oversight.

Separately, Credit Acceptance failed to provide proper notice as required under XXXX XXXX and XXXX. All notices were sent to an outdated address ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ), while my correct address is XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, Tennessee. As a result, I did not receive notice of repossession or my right to redeem prior to sale. 

The repossession itself also raises concerns. The vehicle was taken from within a locked and enclosed area under my carport without my consent, and the incident was captured on video. Under XXXX XXXX, repossession must occur without breach of the peace. 

In addition, personal property was left inside the vehicle at the time of repossession and has not been returned. I was not provided a meaningful opportunity to retrieve my belongings, nor was I given clear instructions on how to recover those items. The loss of personal property represents an additional harm resulting from the repossession and subsequent handling of the vehicle. 

These actions have caused financial harm and hardship. I relied on the companys repeated representations when making financial decisions. Funds that could have been used for essential expenses were instead directed based on inaccurate information. In addition, the loss of the vehicle has impacted my ability to travel to work and maintain income stability. This hardship was worsened by the company continuing to suggest that recovery remained possible, delaying my ability to make alternative arrangements. 

Overall, Credit Acceptances conduct reflects repeated misrepresentation, inconsistent communication, defective notice, potential breach of peace, and failure to address personal property recovery, raising concerns under XXXX provisions, federal law ( including 15 U.S.C. 1692e and 1692f ), and the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act.

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received an initial collection notice from IQ Data International , Inc. ( reference # XXXX ) for an alleged debt of {$770.00} originating from XXXX XXXX XXXX ( operated by XXXX Residential ) in XXXXXXXX XXXX. The alleged debt consists of three move-out charges from a Move-Out Statement dated XX/XX/XXXX : Cleaning ( {$200.00} ), Full Paint ( {$160.00} ), and Carpet Replacement ( {$350.00} ). 

On XX/XX/XXXX, well within the 30-day validation window under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( a ), I sent IQ Data a written dispute requesting verification of the debt, including third-party invoices, proof of payment, documentation of damage beyond normal wear and tear, and an Inventory and Condition Form comparing move-in and move-out conditions. 

IQ Data did not respond for over six months. On XX/XX/XXXX, they finally responded with only two documents : the original creditor 's own billing statement and a copy of the move-out inspection. No third-party invoices, no proof of payment, no photographs, no condition reports, and no move-in documentation were provided. They also added {$28.00} in interest, bringing the alleged balance to {$800.00}. They then reported this disputed tradeline to consumer reporting agencies. 

I consider none of the three charges lawful : ( 1 ) Cleaning ( {$200.00} ) Under Paragraph 26.1 of my TAA lease, a tenant is liable for cleaning charges only when cleaning is inadequate beyond normal wear that is, soiling occurring without negligence, carelessness, accident, or abuse. IQ Data has not provided any photographs, cleaning vendor invoices, receipts, or any other objective documentation establishing that any condition in the unit exceeded normal wear and tear. A flat {$200.00} line-item on a landlord-generated statement, without supporting documentation, does not satisfy the verification standard of 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) or establish a valid charge under the lease.

( 2 ) Full Paint ( {$160.00} ) My lease does not obligate a tenant to repaint the unit at move-out. A " Full Paint '' charge is recoverable only if the walls exhibited damage beyond normal wear and tear attributable to the tenant. IQ Data has provided no photographs, painter 's invoices, receipts, or condition documentation demonstrating any such damage. Under Paragraph 26.1, normal wear including routine scuffs, minor marks, and fading over a 15-month tenancy is not chargeable to the tenant. 

( 3 ) Carpet Replacement ( {$350.00} ) This charge is factually false. I currently reside in the same apartment complex ( XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, TX ) one floor above the unit in question. My wife, at my request and on my behalf, personally inspected Apartment XXXX with the current tenant, XXXX XXXX, in XX/XX/XXXX. There is no carpet in the apartment a different type of hard-surface flooring is installed. No carpet replacement was ever performed. Attached photographs and a written statement from the current tenant confirm this. 

Once one charge in a single document is proven factually false ( the {$350.00} carpet replacement ), the remaining charges in the same document can not be treated as reliable. All three charges originate from the same Move-Out Statement prepared by the same party on the same date, with no independent corroboration for any of them. The demonstrated falsity of one line item compromises the credibility of the entire document. 

Additionally, no one ever explained on what objective basis " wear beyond normal '' was determined for any of these charges. No move-in Inventory and Condition Form was referenced or produced. No photographs of the unit 's condition at move-out ( aside from the inspection form ) were shown. Without a move-in to move-out comparison, there is no factual basis to attribute any alleged condition to me rather than to pre-existing conditions or normal wear over the 15-month tenancy ( XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX ). 

IQ Data 's " verification '' response fails the standard of 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ). Continuing to report and collect a debt that contains a demonstrably false charge violates 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ), 1692e ( 8 ), and 1692f ( 1 ).

The inaccurate tradeline has already caused me quantifiable credit harm. I submitted two separate disputes to Experian ( resulting in reports # XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX and # XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX ), both of which were " verified '' by IQ Data through automated responses without any actual reinvestigation of the underlying facts. 

I do not seek partial balance adjustment or settlement my sole objective is complete deletion of this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies to which it has been reported, as the debt is both procedurally unverified and substantively inaccurate.

I am submitting this complaint against Portfolio Recovery Associates , LLC ( PRA, LLC ) for repeated violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) in connection with an alleged debt that has not been properly validated and appears to be time-barred.

I first discovered PRA, LLC reporting on my credit file in or about XX/XX/XXXX, where it was inaccurately identified as the original creditor. On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent PRA, LLC a written debt validation request and cease-and-desist via USPS Certified Mail, delivered XX/XX/XXXX. PRA, LLC responded with a XX/XX/XXXXXXXX  letter using a standardized XXXX template. This response failed to provide proper validation under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ). It included an unsigned Notice of Intent to Sell, and account statements that were internally inconsistent and mathematically irreconcilable, including a charge-off statement that explicitly stated, Statement not provided to customer. 

Beginning in XX/XX/XXXX, PRA, LLC initiated repeated telephone calls identified as PORTFOLIO RECOV. Calls were brief, often disconnecting after one ring, and included at least one instance ( XX/XX/XXXXXXXX  ) where the call was answered and immediately dropped, consistent with predictive dialer or automated call behavior. These calls occurred without meaningful disclosure and appear to violate 15 U.S.C. 1692d and 1692e. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent PRA, LLC a second written dispute, including : ( 1 ) a renewed demand for validation under 1692g ( b ), ( 2 ) a notice of violations, and ( 3 ) a formal cease-and-desist pursuant to 1692c ( c ). Delivery was confirmed on XX/XX/XXXX. Despite this, PRA, LLC continued collection activity, including calls on XXXX XXXX  and XXXX XXXX XXXX, in violation of 1692c ( c ). 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received another call from PRA, LLC and immediately returned the call. A representative identified as XXXX answered. At the beginning of the call, I requested consent to record, and the representative expressly consented. I provided my first and last name to identify myself. The representative then attempted to obtain additional personal identifiers, including my address and partial Social Security number, which I refused to provide. At that point, the representative attempted to end the call. I then referenced my prior written disputes and the formal cease-and-desist previously sent. Upon doing so, the representatives tone changed, and she instead offered to place a cease-and-desist on future calls associated with my number. This interaction demonstrates that PRA, LLC continued collection activity without first providing proper validation and only acknowledged cease-and-desist obligations after being directly confronted. 

During the XX/XX/XXXX, call, the representative attempted to obtain additional personal identifiers without first providing validation or confirming the legitimacy of the alleged debt, further supporting deceptive practices under 1692e. 

PRA, LLC also failed to disclose that the alleged debt was time-barred during its collection attempts. Prior attempts to collect without this disclosure constitute misleading representations in violation of 1692e.

On XX/XX/XXXX, PRA, LLC added dispute remarks and closed investigations within approximately one day, indicating a cursory or automated review process rather than a reasonable investigation. 

PRA, LLCs conduct demonstrates : ( 1 ) Failure to provide proper validation ( 1692g ( b ) ) ; ( 2 ) Continued collection after cease-and-desist ( 1692c ( c ) ) ; ( 3 ) Use of deceptive and misleading representations ( 1692e ) ; ( 4 ) Harassing or abusive call practices ( 1692d ) ; ( 5 ) Failure to disclose time-barred status prior to collection ( 1692e ) ; and ( 6 ) Failure to conduct reasonable investigations and improper credit reporting ( FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ) ). 

These violations are willful and consistent with patterns previously identified in the XX/XX/XXXX, CFPB stipulated order against PRA, LLC - CFPB v. Portfolio Recovery Associates , LLC, Case No. XXXX ( XXXX. XXXX XXXX. XXXX, XXXX  ) ( CFPB Consent Order ). Complaint Title : Department of Education and Servicer Attempting to Collect on Loans That Were Never Legally Originated -- - What Happened : I am filing a complaint because the Department of Education ( XXXX ) and its contracted servicer are attempting to collect on federal student loans that were never legally originated, were not supported by required federal documentation, and were included in my bankruptcy case. 

The school I attended was in teachout/closure status, and XXXX has never produced the federal records required for lawful Title IV loan origination. Despite multiple requests, neither XXXX nor the servicer has provided the documents that federal law requires for a school to originate or certify federal student loans. 

Because these documents are missing, the loans were never valid, and all collection activity must cease. 

-- - Documents I Am Requesting the Department of Education to Produce : These are the mandatory federal records required for lawful Title IV origination. I am requesting that XXXX produce all of the following : ECAR ( Eligibility and Certification Approval Report ) showing my program existed PPA ( Program Participation Agreement ) in effect at the time CIP code assigned to my program Program eligibility approval Accreditation approval for the program Cost of Attendance ( COA ) used to originate the loan Enrollment certification submitted to XXXX Disbursement authorization records Teachout or closure authorization Financial responsibility documentation for the school If XXXX can not produce these documents, then the loans were never legally originated. 

-- - Why This Is a Serious Compliance Issue : 1. Illegal Origination Without ECAR, CIP, COA, enrollment certification, and program approval, XXXX can not legally originate or disburse Title IV loans. 
If these documents do not exist, the loans are invalid. 

2. False Certification / Borrower Defense If the school lacked program approval, accreditation approval, or CIP codes, then the school falsely certified eligibility, and XXXX continued servicing loans based on nonexistent approvals.

I am feeling incredibly violated, XXXX, and embarrassed. 2 years ago, I received a phone call from someone named XXXX, who worked with/on behalf of Elite DMS ( Elite Document Management Solutions ), claiming that Elite DMS was a " financial restoration program '' and was told that if I stopped paying my credit card bills, to the point that each account/debt were to go into collections, that they ( Elite DMS ) would work dispute those debts for 30-40 % of the total amount of my debts. I was, of course, very skeptical of this, and remember doing some research at the time ( with no legal expertise or background ) and all I can really remember about my findings at the time is that they were positive, and that they had had rave reviews on various websites. The woman I spoke with, who claimed to be named XXXX, sounded to me, at the time, incredibly kind, informative, helpful, sweet, understanding, etc. I had many, many concerns at the time, and had been receiving a number of letters/offers for various " debt relief '' programs that very clearly seemed to be scams, but for some reason, this one seemed different to me. 

I had around ~ {$15000.00} in debts total across 6 different credit cards. I had been paying those credit cards on a timely manner, and would have continued to do so had I not signed up for this program. 

I ended up agreeing to pay $ XXXX over the course of 2 years, receiving monthly phone call/appointments with XXXX to go over any new documentation I had received from debt collectors. I was told that if Elite DMS were unable to successfully dispute any of the accounts in question, I was A. Be entitled to reimbursement, or B. Be provided with legal representation at no extra cost. 

I was already in a desperate financial situation, and though I was not looking for any shortcuts or easy ways out of it ( as I stated before, I would have simply continued to pay off my debts as normal over a long period of time ), XXXX & Elite DMS were incredibly convincing, and I ended up signing up for ( what I thought to be ) an honest program that existed to protect consumers, despite it being a for profit company/institution ( as I was told ). 

Fast forward to 2 years later, this past XX/XX/2023, I received a court summons from a debt collector/law firm that had bought the debt from one of my accounts. My fiance was actually the one to have been served, not me directly, as I was working that day, so I didn't get a chance to look at the documents until after business hours. Once I had realized that what I received was, in fact, a court summons, and that clearly, at least 1 of my 6 accounts had not been successfully disputed, I googled Elite DMS to find their phone number so I could get back in touch with them and get some guidance as to how to move forward/how to respond to the summons/etc. 

To my utter dismay, shock, horror & disbelief, I saw a torrent of 1 star reviews of dozens and dozens of people crying " SCAM!!! STAY FAR AWAY FROM ELITE DMS!!! ". I couldn't believe it. 

The next day ( Tuesday, XX/XX/XXXX ), and each following business day that week ( excluding Friday of that week ), I called every phone number I could find that was associated with Elite DMS. I got a call back on the 1st day from someone claiming to be named XXXX, who told me not to worry, and that someone from their legal team would be getting back to me shortly. Tuesday passed, I made a number of calls to Elite DMS, left voicemails, etc. Waited on hold with what I now assume to be a " dummy '' " dead end '' " hold '', where a voice at the beginning says " Our representatives are currently busy. Someone from Elite DMS will be with you shortly '' and waited 30 minutes in silence to no avail. Repeat same thing on Wednesday, and Thursday. 

Finally, on Thursday, I received a call from Elite DMS, but not from their legal team. I do not recall this person 's name, but they told me they would send me a form for reimbursement for the account that was not successfully disputed. I did not sign this form ( as I worry it would relieve them of accountability ). 

I have since revisited the contracts I had signed and I fear I have made a grave mistake. I have no idea what I got myself into, but I fear I have paid this company $ XXXX for what appears to be absolutely nothing, and it seems that several dozen other people have also fallen victim to what I presume to be a scam, that I *HOPE* to XXXX is breaking some sort of law here, so that I might have some sort of legal recourse or course of retaliation. 

Today is XX/XX/2023, and I repeated my same calling routine, trying to get in touch with SOMEONE at Elite DMS, to no avail. I will continue to do so the rest of the week. 


I had initially attached 6 documents to this, but then upon seeing that Elite DMS would see that it was me filing this complaint, I removed them out of fear of retaliation. text:
In XX/XX/XXXX, I received a phone call from my loan lender stating that my student loans were nearing repayment status and that my monthly payments would increase. I informed the representative that I was still in my fifth year of college and was assured that my payments would not change. I received no additional phone calls or emails between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX regarding any change to my loan repayment terms. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received an email stating that my student loan payments were increasing, without advance notice. At that time, I did not fully understand the total balance of my loans, as I had been led to believe by a family member that the loans were being managed and paid. During this period, I took over full financial responsibility for these loans and have remained prompt and diligent with all required payments. As I began managing the loans independently, I reasonably relied on information provided directly by representatives of the loan lender when making significant financial decisions. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I made a large payment of approximately {$39000.00} toward my student loans. Before making this payment, I spoke with a loan lender representative who explained that once XXXX loan was paid off, my remaining loans would be eligible for reamortization. During this same call, the representative explicitly stated that my loans would be automatically reamortized as a result of this payment and that the new payment amount would be reflected within approximately XXXX days. I was instructed to call back only if I did not see the change. The reamortization did not occur. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted the loan lender to follow up. I was informed that the previous representative had provided incorrect information, but I was told that reamortization could still be processed upon request and that it would reduce my monthly payment. I specifically asked when the change would take effect and was told to make my normal XXXX payment, with the new payment reflecting in XX/XX/XXXX. 

As of the XX/XX/XXXX billing cycle, no reamortization had occurred, and my monthly payment remained unchanged. 

I made multiple attempts to resolve this issue : On XX/XX/XXXX, I was told the loan lender could not reamortize my loans because I had only paid off XXXX loan, and that payments across all XXXX loans were required, a criterion that had never previously been disclosed. I requested that a formal case be opened, that prior calls be reviewed, and that corrective adjustments be applied. A case number was issued. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, my case was escalated due to no response. 

On XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, I followed up again and received no update. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, A manager confirmed that call reviews showed representatives had provided incorrect information. I was offered a reduced payment but was not informed that doing so would significantly increase the total interest accrued. This material information was disclosed only after I questioned it directly. The manager also stated that the loan lender does not reamortize student loans at all, contradicting previous representations. 

I also requested access to call recordings and was informed that they could only be obtained through a subpoena. 

As a result of this situation, I have experienced significant financial burden and mental distress. I took over full financial responsibility for these loans in good faith and have remained current and prompt on my payments. However, I made a {$39000.00} payment in reliance on explicit representations that my loans would be reamortized and that my monthly payment would decrease. Instead, I have faced prolonged uncertainty, repeated misinformation, ongoing higher monthly payments, and continued interest accrual. This has materially impacted my ability to responsibly manage my finances and move forward with my life, including delaying my ability to refinance and achieve financial stability. I can not reasonably continue absorbing financial harm caused by inaccurate information while remaining compliant with my repayment obligations.
label: Student loan

2. HOW I AGREE TO THE TERMS OF THIS LOAN. Upon receipt of each Disclosure Statement, I will review it and notify you in writing if I have any questions. If I am not satisfied with the terms of my loan as disclosed in a Disclosure Statement that covers my entire loan amount, I may cancel my loan by giving you a written cancellation notice within ten ( 10 ) days after I receive the Disclosure Statement. If I am not satisfied with the terms of my loan as disclosed in a Disclosure Statement that covers only one of multiple disbursements of my loan, to cancel the disbursement covered by that Disclosure Statement, I will give you a written cancellation notice within ten ( 10 ) days after I receive the Disclosure Statement and I understand that unless I withdraw from the School or I or my School specifies otherwise, the cancellation of any disbursement will not cancel any future disbursements. Previous disbursements may not be canceled under any circumstances. I understand that I must repay, in accordance with the terms of this Credit Agreement, all amounts disbursed but not canceled. If loan proceeds have been disbursed, I agree that I will immediately return the canceled disbursement to you, will not endorse any check that disburses the loan proceeds to be canceled, and will instruct the School to return the canceled disbursement to you. If I give notice of cancellation but do not cause the return of the disbursement as stated above, the disbursement will not be canceled and I will be in default of this Credit Agreement. ( See Paragraph I. ) C. DEFINITIONS : 1. Disbursement Date means the date or dates on which you lend money to me in consideration for my Credit Agreement and will be the date ( s ) shown on any loan check you prepare or the date ( s ) you initiate any electronic funds transfer.

2. The Deferment Period will begin on the first Disbursement Date and end on the Deferment End Date.

3. Deferment End Date means the date specified below for the applicable loan program ( the applicable loan program is stated on the first page of this Credit Agreement ).

( a ) Undergraduate Alternative Loan Program : If I have elected the Immediate Repayment option ( the applicable repayment option is stated on the first page of this Credit Agreement ), there is no Deferment Period, and my first payment will be 30-60 days after the final disbursement of my loan. In any event, if I have elected the Interest Only repayment option, the Deferment End Date will be no more than 5 years after the first Disbursement Date. If I have elected the Full Deferral repayment option ( the applicable repayment option is stated on the first page of this Credit Agreement ), then the Deferment End Date will be 180 days after the date the student Borrower first graduates or ceases to be enrolled at least half-time in the School ( or another school participating in this Loan Program ). In any event, if I have elected the Full Deferral repayment option, the Deferment End Date will be no more than 5 years after the first Disbursement Date. For borrowers who chose the Interest Only or full Deferral repayment options, joint and serial ( associates to bachelors ) degree recipients may continue in-school deferment while completing their second degree, up to the 5-year or 5 -year maximum. Regardless of the repayment option I chose and after the Deferment End Date, this loan may be eligible upon written request for deferment periods of up to five ( 5 ) years total ( Additional Deferment ) as long as the student Borrower is enrolled at least half time to complete an undergraduate or graduate degree ( at a school participating in this loan program ) or begins a medical internship or residency program. The Servicer may treat any notice of a revised graduation date or of new enrollment as my written request for Additional Deferment. You will capitalize ( see Paragraph D.3 ) accrued and unpaid interest as of the end of each deferment period. All such capitalized interest shall be repaid with the principal balance.

( b ) Graduate Professional Education Loan Program : The Deferment End Date will be 180 days after the student Borrower graduates or ceases for any other reason to be enrolled at least half-time in the School ( or another school participating in this Loan Program ), but no more than 4 years after the first Disbursement Date ; provided, however, that if the student Borrower begins a medical residency or internship during the Deferment Period, then the Deferment Period will end 180 days after the day the residency or internship ends, but no more than 8 years after the first Disbursement Date.

( c ) Health Professions Education Loan Program : The Deferment End Date will be 270 days after the student Borrower graduates or ceases for any other reason to be enrolled at least half-time in the School ( or another school participating in this Loan Program ), but no more than 6 years after the first Disbursement Date ; provided, however, that if the student Borrower begins a medical residency or internship during the Deferment Period, then the Deferment Period will end 270 days after the day the residency or internship ends, but no more than 10 years after the first Disbursement Date.

( d ) Residency Loan Program : The Deferment End Date will be 270 days after the student Borrower ceases for any reason to be enrolled in a medical residency or internship, but no more than 4 years after the Disbursement Date.

4. The Repayment Period begins the day after the Deferment Period ends. If there is no Deferment Period for my loan, the Repayment Period will begin when my loan is fully disbursed. The Repayment Period is 20 years ( 25 years for loans with a Principal Sum of {$40000.00} or more ) unless monthly payments equal to the minimum monthly payment amount ( See Paragraph E.2 ) will repay all amounts owed in less than 20 years, in which case the Repayment Period will be the number of months necessary to pay in full the amount I owe at the minimum payment. D. INTEREST : 1. Accrual Beginning on the first Disbursement Date, interest will be calculated at the Variable Rate ( Paragraph D.2 ) and charged on the Principal Sum, and on any unpaid interest later added to the Principal Sum according to Paragraph D.3 . During the Repayment Period, interest will be calculated at the Variable Rate and charged on the outstanding balance of this Credit Agreement until all amounts are paid in full.

Interest will be calculated on a daily simple interest basis. The daily interest rate will be equal to the annual interest rate in effect on that day, divided by the number of days in that calendar year.

2. Variable Rate The Variable Rate is equal to the Current Index plus a Margin.

The Margins for both the Deferment Period and the Repayment Period are shown on the first page of this Credit Agreement. In no event will the Variable Rate exceed the maximum interest rate allowed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. 
The Variable Rate will change quarterly on the first day of each XXXX, XXXX, XXXX and XXXX ( the Change Date ( s ) ) if the Current Index changes. The Current Index for any calendar quarter beginning on a Change Date ( or for any shorter period beginning on any Disbursement Date and ending on the last day of a calendar quarter ) is based on the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate ( LIBOR ) as published in the Money Rates section of The XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ). The index for each calendar quarter ( or for any shorter period beginning on a Disbursement Date and ending on the last day of a calendar quarter ) will equal the average of the LIBOR rates published on the first business day of each of the three ( XXXX ) immediately preceding calendar months, rounded to the nearest one-hundredth of one percent ( 0.01 % ). If The XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ) is not published or the Current Index is not given on any of these dates, then the Current Index will be determined by using the immediately preceding published Current Index for such date. If the Current Index is no longer available, you will choose a comparable index. 
XXXX. Capitalization If I have elected the Full Deferral repayment option, I understand that you will add all accrued and unpaid interest to the principal balance of my loan ( capitalize interest ) as of the last day of the Deferment Period. In addition, if my loan will be disbursed in multiple disbursements and if I have elected the Immediate Repayment option, you will capitalize interest that accrues between the first disbursement of my loan and the final disbursement of my loan. I understand that regardless of the repayment option I chose, you will capitalize interest at the end of any forbearance period. { XXXX } XXXX XXXX of XXXX XXXX TERMS OF REPAYMENT : XXXX. Deferment Period If I have elected either the Interest Only repayment option or the Full Deferral repayment option ( the applicable repayment option is stated on the first page of this Credit Agreement ), you will send statements during the Deferment Period ( showing the total outstanding principal balance of my loan and the interest that has accrued on my loan ).
