You will add any interest that I do not pay during the Deferment Period to the principal balance, as described in Paragraph D.3.

2. Repayment Period The amount of my monthly payment ( Monthly Payment Amount ) will be established based on the rules in this Credit Agreement when my Repayment Period begins. During the Repayment Period, you will send me monthly statements that show the Monthly Payment Amount and the payment due dates, and I will pay the Monthly Payment Amount shown on my monthly statement, which amount will in no event be less than {$25.00} or the unpaid balance, whichever is less. I understand that the Monthly Payment Amount is due each month. I may pay more than my Monthly Payment Amount at any time without penalty or charge. If my loan is in paidahead status, I may, but will not be required to make monthly payments. You reserve the right to send monthly statements to the Borrower and/or the Cosigner. Even if I do not receive monthly statements, I will make consecutive monthly payments in amounts at least equal to the Monthly Payment Amount by the applicable payment due dates until I have paid all of the principal and interest and any other charges I may owe under this Credit Agreement.

3. Repayment Terms- My Monthly Payment Amount will be calculated as of the day the Repayment Period begins ( Repayment Date ). It will be recalculated ( a ) once each year prior to the anniversary of the Repayment Date, ( b ) if the Variable Rate changes between anniversaries of the Repayment Date to the extent that the Monthly Payment Amount would not pay in full the accrued monthly interest on my loan, ( c ) following any subsequent deferment or forbearance period or ( d ) following any request by the Borrower to the servicer to change the monthly payment due date ( each of which events is a new Repayment Date ). As of any Repayment Date, my Monthly Payment Amount will be recalculated. My new Monthly Payment Amount will be disclosed to me by the servicer. The new Monthly Payment Amount will equal the amount necessary to pay in full, over the number of months remaining in the Repayment Period, the amount I owe in equal monthly installments of principal and interest at the Variable Rate in effect at the time of the calculation. I understand that this may result in a reduction or increase in my monthly payment as calculated as of each Repayment Date. I understand that during the Repayment Period ( and, if I have elected the Interest Only repayment option, during the period of interest payments ) the servicer may change the monthly payment due date of future payments to a later date for the convenience of the servicer in processing payments or in order to coordinate the due dates of all of my loans processed by the servicer.

4. Amounts Owing at the End of the Repayment Period Since interest accrues daily upon the unpaid principal balance of my loan, if I make payments after my payment due dates, I may owe additional interest. If I have not paid my late fees, I will also owe additional amounts for those late fees. In such cases you will increase the amount of my last monthly payment to the amount necessary to repay my loan in full.

5. Payments Payments will be applied first to late fees, other fees and charges, accrued interest, and the remainder to principal.

6. Other Charges - If any part of a monthly payment remains unpaid for a period of more than 15 days after the payment due date, I will pay a late fee not exceeding {$5.00} or 5 % of the overdue payment amount, whichever is less. To the extent permitted by law, I agree to pay you all amounts you incur in enforcing the terms of this Credit Agreement, including reasonable collection agency and attorney 's fees and court costs and other collection costs.

F. LOAN ORIGINATION FEE : If you charge me, I will pay you a Loan Origination Fee at the time my loan is disbursed. The dollar amount of any Loan Origination Fee will be determined by multiplying the Principal Sum times the Loan Origination Fee Percentage shown on the first page of this Credit Agreement. The percentage would be higher if computed only on the amount advanced rather than on the entire Principal Sum ( Loan Origination Fee plus the loan Amount advanced ). For example, a nominal Loan Origination Fee of 6.5 % on the entire principal amount would equal 6.9519 % of the amount advanced. The Loan Origination Fee I will pay, if any, will be shown on my Disclosure Statement and included with the Principal Sum. To the extent permitted by law, and unless I timely cancel a disbursement ( see Paragraph B.2 ), I will not be entitled to a refund of any Loan Origination Fee relating to that disbursement.

G. RIGHT TO PREPAY : I have the right to prepay all or any part of my loan at any time without penalty.

H. FORBEARANCE : If I am unable to repay my loan in accordance with the terms established under this Credit Agreement because of a hardship such as financial or medical difficulty, I may request that you modify these terms. If I default, I will be required to pay interest on this loan accruing after default. The interest rate after default will be subject to adjustment in the same manner as before default.

To the extent permitted by applicable law, upon default, you may also capitalize any interest and fees ( i.e., add accrued and unpaid interest and fees to the principal balance ), and increase the Margin used to compute the Variable Rate by two percentage points ( 2 % ).

CONSEQUENTLY, THE PROVISIONS OF THIS CREDIT AGREEMENT WILL BE GOVERNED BY FEDERAL LAW AND THE LAWS OF THE COMMONWEALTH OF PENNSYLVANIA, WITHOUT REGARD TO CONFLICT OF LAW RULES.

3. My responsibility for paying the loan evidenced by this Credit Agreement is unaffected by the liability of any other person to me or by your failure to notify me that a required payment has not been made. 4. I may not assign this Credit Agreement or any of its benefits or obligations. You may assign this Credit Agreement at any time.

5. The terms and conditions set forth in this Credit Agreement and the Disclosure Statement constitute the entire agreement between you and me.

6. If any provision of this Credit Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, that provision shall be considered omitted from this Credit Agreement without affecting the validity or enforceability of the remainder of this Credit Agreement.

7. A provision of this Credit Agreement may only be modified if jointly agreed upon in writing by you and me. Any modification will not affect the validity or enforceability of the remainder of this Credit Agreement.

8. To the extent permitted by law, you have the right to apply money from any of my deposit account ( s ) with you to pay all or a portion of any amount overdue under this Credit Agreement. On XX/XX/XXXX, I notified the servicer in writing of the deaths of both the borrower and co-borrower and provided the documentation I was instructed to submit, including death certificates, a petition for Letters of Administration, and identification. I received no response. 

In XX/XX/XXXX, I was finally contacted by a representative and again provided the prior documentation, along with the Letters of Administration issued by the probate court on XX/XX/XXXX. I requested assistance with a forbearance or other options to prevent foreclosure. I was told I needed to record the Letters of Administration on title before further action could be taken. This requirement was completed on XX/XX/XXXX. 

Despite these efforts, the loan proceeded further into default. In XX/XX/XXXX, after obtaining life insurance proceeds, I tendered payment in the amount of {$16000.00} to bring the loan current and reinstate the mortgage. 

Since making that payment : The servicer has not provided written confirmation that the loan has been reinstated. 
The servicer has not provided updated statements or billing information to allow me to keep the loan current.

The servicer has refused to communicate with me directly, despite my status as the court-appointed Administrator, and despite repeated attempts to resolve the issue. 

Additionally, on XX/XX/XXXX, the servicer issued a letter stating that the XX/XX/XXXX payment was past due. This correspondence was not sent to me, but instead mailed to a third-party address and was not received until XX/XX/XXXX. This has further impaired my ability to keep the loan current and raises concerns regarding the servicers handling of account communications. 

A Notice of Default was also recorded, which included a certification that the servicer exercised due diligence to contact the borrower as required under California Civil Code 2923.55. This is concerning, as the servicer was notified of the borrowers death and had my contact information and documentation as early as XX/XX/XXXX, yet failed to meaningfully engage for several months. 

I am attempting in good faith to resolve the delinquency, maintain the loan in good standing, and prevent foreclosure while the property is being prepared for sale. However, the servicers lack of communication, failure to provide confirmation of reinstatement, and failure to provide ongoing billing statements are preventing me from doing so.

text:
I am filing this complaint against Bridgecrest/XXXX for inaccurate, inconsistent, and unverifiable credit reporting in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

This account is being reported with multiple errors, including inaccurate late payments, conflicting account information, and an unverifiable remaining balance. Due to these issues, the tradeline is materially misleading and can not be considered reliable. 

1. Inaccurate Late Payment Reporting The account reflects multiple 30-, 60-, and 90-day late payments, including recent severe delinquency. However, I made documented payments during the same time period, including payments in early 2025. 

Despite these payments, the account continues to report escalating delinquency without accurately reflecting how those payments were applied or how the account remained in a delinquent status after receipt of payment. 

Reporting late payments under these circumstances, without providing a clear and accurate accounting of how payments were applied or how delinquency was determined, is unsupported, misleading, and unverifiable. 

The company has not provided any documentation or accounting demonstrating how the reported late payments were calculated or how the account remained in a delinquent status after receiving payments. 
This violates : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) furnishing inaccurate information 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) failure to ensure maximum possible accuracy 2. Conflicting and Materially Misleading Information This account contains internal contradictions, including : A drastic balance reduction from approximately {$26000.00} to around {$3000.00} A notation stating the debt is being paid through insurance Continued reporting of severe delinquency and past due status These elements can not logically coexist without proper adjustment to the account status. The combination of payments, insurance activity, and continued delinquency reporting creates a materially misleading tradeline that does not reflect the true condition of the account. 

3. Unverifiable Deficiency Balance Based on the balance reduction and insurance involvement, it appears that the collateral may have been repossessed, surrendered, or otherwise disposed of. 

However, the company has failed to provide : Documentation of repossession or voluntary surrender Sale or disposition records of the vehicle Application of insurance proceeds A complete and accurate deficiency balance calculation Without this documentation, the remaining balance is unverifiable and can not be reported accurately. 

4. Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation I previously disputed this account, and it was marked as updated, yet the inaccuracies remain unchanged. This indicates that no reasonable investigation was conducted and that relevant information was not properly reviewed. 

This violates : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) 5. XXXX XXXX Noncompliance The account reflects inconsistencies between account status, payment history, balance, and insurance activity. Under XXXX XXXX reporting standards, these data fields must be internally consistent. 

The current reporting fails to meet these standards and is therefore inaccurate and misleading. 

Requested Resolution DELETION ONLY Due to the inaccurate, conflicting, and unverifiable nature of this account, I am requesting : Immediate deletion of this tradeline from all credit reporting agencies This account can not be corrected without speculation, as the underlying data is inconsistent and unsupported by documentation. 

Notice of Liability Continued reporting of inaccurate or unverifiable information after notice may constitute willful or negligent noncompliance under : 15 U.S.C. 1681n 15 U.S.C. 1681o I am seeking complete removal of this account due to its failure to meet federal reporting standards.

The presence of contradictory data points strongly indicates that the information has not been properly verified with the original source and may be the result of unreliable or automated furnishing practices.

Republic Finance is the appropriate company for this complaint. After I applied for a loan, I was contacted directly by Republic Finance regarding my application. During that interaction, I clearly stated that I did not want a vehicle-secured loan. I was told that another loan structure could be arranged, but the only option ultimately presented was a vehicle-secured loan. This complaint concerns the representations made by Republic Finance during the application process and how loan options were communicated to me, not simply a denial of credit. Republic Finance directly handled my application and communication, and therefore is responsible for this issue. They marked my previous complaint as not belonging to them.

I am filing this complaint regarding the handling of a recent loan application with Republic Bank. Before allowing a hard credit inquiry to proceed, I had a detailed conversation with a representative at Republic Finance who contacted me, regarding the type of loan I was willing to consider. She mentioned that it was for a secured loan, and I immediately told her I do not want to do a secured loan and if theres any small chance that I would be approved for only a secured loan then lets not proceed. During that conversation, And prior to finishing the application, I clearly stated the following : XXXX. I did not want a loan secured by a vehicle, XXXX. My current vehicle is in the process of being bought back by the manufacturer, so it can not be used as collateral XXXX. I would not place a replacement vehicle as collateral for a loan. XXXX. I was concerned about allowing a hard inquiry on my credit report unless there was a very realistic possibility of approval for the type of loan I was requesting. The representative acknowledged these concerns and stated that the loan could be structured as a personal property secured loan, instead of a vehicle-secured loan. She expressed confidence that this type of structure could be possible and indicated she had seen situations where the final approval amount differed, or even increased, from the initial pre-approval. On XX/XX/XXXX, when I answered her call I told her that I did not want to go through with it because I did not feel like the pre-approval amount was worth it. At that time, is when she then told me that she has seen scenarios where people get approved for more than the pre-approval amount, and I wouldnt not have to put a vehicle up as collateral. The confidence that she displayed in getting me a loan that was not tied to a vehicle is what convinced me to move forward. At the end of our phone call, she said I will have an approval for you by tomorrow morning. And this was after we discussed my concerns and that I did not want to move forward if there was even a small chance of any of my concerns being valid. Because of those assurances she gave me, after 3 days of hesitance, I agreed to proceed with the application and allowed a hard inquiry to be placed on my credit report. The following day, when I had not heard anything from her after she stated she would be calling back in the morning, I contacted the bank for an update, at XXXX. I was informed by another male representative that I was only approved for a loan secured by a vehicle, which would pay my vehicle off, which is the exact type of loan I had clearly declined from the beginning. At that point I had told him that I had already discussed with the previous representative that I did not want to do that type of loan and this car is being bought back by the manufacturer. He then started to come up with several excuses as to why their sales tactic was not unethical. During that conversation, the representative focused on the fact that I had received a pre-approval, and stated that underwriting ultimately determines the final decision. However, this response does not address the actual issue. My complaint is not about the underwriting decision itself. I understand that lenders ultimately determine approval terms. The issue is that I communicated very clearly that I would not accept a vehicle-secured loan, and the representative still encouraged me to proceed with a full application and hard credit inquiry based on the suggestion that a different loan structure was likely possible. It is their responsibility as the professionals in this industry to advise against applying, especially when someone has concerns as I did. I also brought up that I was ready to leave it because the initial preapproval was for a secured loan. It wasnt until she said, it doesnt have to be a vehicle that I even continued to entertain the conversation. That shouldve never happened. She shouldve advised against me moving forward with this loan because of my concerns and the circumstances. The male representative I spoke to continue to argue with me that there was no problem with what happened. He also cut me off initially while I was speaking ; and several times after. When I asked him to let me finish speaking, so he could hear what I was saying, he said so its your way or the highway?. Lets be clear ; this man cut me off when I was in the middle of speaking. There was no reason to start cutting me off. I continued to try and explain to him why Im frustrated and he continued to defend their actions. He kept focusing on the pre-approval, and not the fact that I was convinced into completing this application. At that point, I hung up. Given the information I provided up front about my credit concerns, credit report history, collateral limitations, and loan preferences, I truly believe a reasonable and responsible course of action would have been to advise me that the pre-approval appeared to be tied specifically to a vehicle-secured loan and that proceeding with the application could result in exactly the outcome that occurred. Instead, I relied on the representatives assurances that a different loan structure was possible, which led me to authorize the application and incur a hard inquiry on my credit report. This has nothing to do with underwriting and everything to do with the fact that they are responsible for providing guidance in these situations, and they provided me with guidance that completely changed the course of this application, as I did not want to pursue it. As someone working to rebuild my credit, I was very transparent about my concerns regarding unnecessary credit inquiries. Had I been advised that a vehicle-secured loan was the most likely outcome, I would not have proceeded with the application. I believe consumers should be able to rely on clear and responsible guidance before authorizing a credit inquiry that can impact their credit profile. After this conversation with the Republic Finance representative, they send a letter a few weeks later " denying '' my loan request. The timing of this, is very odd.
label: Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan

text:
Unfair and Deceptive Payment Allocation Practices by Synchrony Bank I am filing this complaint to formally report an unfair, deceptive, and systematically abusive payment allocation practice by Synchrony Bank regarding their credit card accounts with multiple deferred-interest promotional balances.

I currently hold a Synchrony credit card account that has multiple overlapping promotional purchases on it ( e.g., an older, higher-amount equal-payment promotion and multiple newer XXXX deferred interest promotions ). The newer promotions are for smaller amounts and will expire a year earlier than the older promotion.

Synchrony 's payment system defaults to an internal allocation algorithm. Crucially, Synchrony deliberately provides no online tool or interface that allows consumers to manually route their excess payments to the promotional balance that will incur retroactive interest the soonest.

To avoid thousands of dollars in retroactive interest, I am forced to call Synchrony Bank 's customer service every single month to manually override their system and direct my payment to the correct balance. To make matters worse, if a consumer does not get through to a representative soon enough after making a payment, Synchrony claims it will take 1 to 2 billing cycles for the re-allocation to take effect. This artificial delay further complicates a consumer 's ability to pay balances off in time and acts as another trap to ensure the promotion expires before the corrected payments are applied. 

This practice is inherently anti-consumer. The bank has the technological capability to calculate complex retroactive interest across multiple balances, yet chooses not to provide a simple online option for payment allocation. By designing an online portal that hides this functionality and forcing customers to navigate monthly phone calls ( complete with arbitrary processing delays ) to avoid penalties, Synchrony is intentionally creating an unreasonable barrier to success. This relies on consumer fatigue, mathematical errors, or simply forgetting to call, ensuring the bank profits from predatory retroactive interest.

I am asking the regulatory body reviewing this complaint to investigate Synchrony Banks deliberate lack of transparent, consumer-facing online allocation tools and predatory default allocation logic, as it constitutes an unfair practice designed to trap consumers.

Since Synchrony specializes in these sorts of promotions, they absolutely know how to allocate payments to best avoid interest. Payments should be applied first toward minimum payments, and then any additional amount should automatically be allocated toward the promotion that ends the soonest.

Just this simple change would make it easier for consumers to increase payment amounts for additional purchases and remain on track for all promotions. It would be even better if they provided an online tool to choose how payments are allocated, but simply changing the auto-allocation algorithm to prioritize the earliest expiring promotion would solve this problem. It is also obviously the ethical thing to do for a bank specializing in deferred-interest promotional purchases.

In XX/XX/year>, a salesperson from XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX came to my home to sell a solar system that would be financed through Dividend Finance. During the inhome sales presentation, the salesperson made several statements that turned out to be false. He told both me and my fianc that we were guaranteed to receive the federal solar tax credit, that the credit amount would be {$7100.00}, and that this guaranteed credit would be applied to the loan to keep our monthly payment at {$91.00} per month. He also stated that we would not have to worry about higher payments later. These statements were presented as facts, not estimates or possibilities. 

After signing the loan, I reviewed the loan documents and discovered that the written disclosures directly contradict what the salesperson told us. The documents state that Dividend Finance does not guarantee that a borrower will qualify for the tax credit, that eligibility depends on individual tax liability, and that the incentive payment amount may be higher than any tax credit received. The documents also state that if the incentive payment is not made, the monthly payment will increase. 

Because the salespersons statements were false, we relied on incorrect information when agreeing to the loan. This was a doortodoor, inhome solicitation, which is regulated under Pennsylvanias Home Improvement Consumer Protection Act and the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law. Both prohibit deceptive or misleading statements used to induce a homeowner to sign a contract. 

As a result of the misrepresentation, we now face a required incentive payment of {$7100.00} at month XXXX and a payment increase from {$90.00} to {$120.00} if we can not make that payment. We would not have agreed to this loan if the salesperson had provided accurate information.

To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to formally dispute the handling, validity, and reporting of the above-referenced auto loan account in which I am listed as a co-signer. 

This dispute is based on multiple deficiencies in required notices, improper handling of address records, and inaccurate credit reporting. 

-- - * * Failure to Provide Required Notices * * XXXX XXXX failed to provide legally required notices in connection with the repossession and subsequent sale of the vehicle. 

Specifically : * No * * Notice of Intent to Sell ( Notice of Disposition ) * * was provided to the primary borrower. 
* No * * deficiency balance notice or post-sale explanation * * was provided to the primary borrower. 
* Required notices were not consistently or properly sent to all obligated parties on the account. 

Under UCC Article 9, these notices are required to be sent to all obligated parties and must be sent to the correct last known address. Failure to provide such notices calls into question the enforceability of any claimed deficiency balance. 

-- - * * Address Discrepancies and Improper Notice * * I have updated my address with XXXX XXXX multiple times. Despite this : * The vehicle was repossessed from my correct and current address. 
* XXXX successfully sent correspondence regarding the repossession to this correct address ( see attached documentation ). 
* However, required notices related to the sale and deficiency were not sent consistently to the correct address, nor were they sent to the primary borrower. 

This demonstrates that XXXX had access to and knowledge of the correct address but failed to use it for all legally required notifications, depriving the obligated parties of the right to redeem the vehicle and participate in the sale process. 

-- - * * Commercial Reasonableness of Sale * * The vehicle appears to have been sold for a significantly low amount, raising concerns that the sale was not conducted in a commercially reasonable manner as required under applicable law. 

Without proper notice and an opportunity to redeem or monitor the sale, the resulting deficiency balance is questionable and potentially invalid. 

-- - * * Inaccurate and Inconsistent Credit Reporting * * There are discrepancies in how this account is being reported across the three major credit bureaus.

XXXX has stated that they are not responsible for these discrepancies ; however, as the data furnisher, XXXX is responsible under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) for ensuring that all reported information is accurate and consistent. 

Failure to ensure accurate reporting constitutes a violation of federal law. 

-- - * * Request for Resolution * * Based on the above, I am requesting the following : 1. Full documentation of : * Notice of Disposition ( including address used and proof of mailing ) * Post-sale deficiency balance and complete accounting * Details of the sale, including date, method, and sale price 2. Correction or removal of any inaccurate or unverifiable information reported to the credit bureaus 4. If proper notice and commercially reasonable sale can not be substantiated, I request that the deficiency balance be deemed unenforceable and that the account be updated or removed accordingly from all credit reporting agencies.

text:
To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding Wells Fargos handling of my business credit account and a recent setoff of {$36000.00} from my account. 

At the time of this withdrawal, I was actively enrolled in a hardship payment plan with a monthly obligation of {$700.00}. This plan was established due to financial hardship, including the impact of the recent California fires, which caused displacement and ongoing disruption to my business and personal finances. 

Despite these circumstances, I made consistent good-faith efforts to comply with the plan and continued making payments, even during months when I was unable to meet the full amount. 

Without prior notice, Wells Fargo withdrew {$36000.00} from my account through a setoff. This action has caused significant financial harm, severely impacting my ability to operate my business and maintain financial stability. It also appears to undermine the purpose of the hardship payment plan, which was intended to provide a sustainable path toward repayment during a period of financial difficulty. 

Additionally, a substantial portion of the funds that were withdrawn originated from a loan through XXXX involving my spouse. My spouse is not obligated on the Wells Fargo account and is not a guarantor of the debt. While these funds were deposited into a joint account, they were not solely attributable to me. I am concerned that Wells Fargo may have improperly applied a setoff to funds that belong, at least in part, to a non-obligated party.

I understand that financial institutions may have contractual rights of setoff ; however, such rights are generally expected to be applied in a fair and equitable manner, particularly where a borrower is actively participating in a hardship repayment plan. In this instance, the setoff appears inconsistent with the purpose of the hardship arrangement and has created significant hardship.

I am seeking the following resolution : A full reversal of the {$36000.00} setoff, or at minimum a substantial partial reversal Confirmation and reinstatement of my hardship payment plan Assurance that no further setoffs will occur while I remain in an agreed repayment arrangement I am committed to resolving this obligation responsibly and continuing payments under a structured plan. However, the current situation has made it extremely difficult to do so.

I respectfully request a thorough review of this matter and a fair resolution that reflects the hardship circumstances and the involvement of funds not solely attributable to the obligated party.
label: Debt collection

On XX/XX/year>, I deposited {$1000.00} with XXXX. After placing and winning my bets, I attempted to withdraw my funds. XXXX then required me to send identification, including my drivers license. Soon after, they denied my withdrawal and claimed there was an issue tied to rollback and play-through requirements.

The original play-through requirement I understood was 1x, which I met after winning a XXXX XXXX. However, XXXX  later claimed that bonus credits provided by one of their agents changed the requirement to an extremely high play-through amount, which was never clearly disclosed to me before the transaction or before I accepted the funds. This made withdrawal practically impossible after I had already deposited and played under different expectations.

In addition, although my deposit was {$1000.00}, my Wells Fargo card was charged {$1100.00}. A XXXX  representative stated that the charge should have been corrected/refunded back to the proper amount of {$1000.00} after my withdrawal was denied. However, that did not resolve the issue, and I was still left with a charge that did not match the amount I authorized. 

Another major concern is that the billing descriptor did not clearly show XXXX or a gambling/sportsbook-related merchant. Instead, the transaction appeared under a clothing-related merchant description. I believe this billing descriptor was misleading and prevented the transaction from being accurately identified and investigated.

I reported this issue to Wells Fargo and explained that the dispute was not simply a duplicate charge. The issue involved an incorrect transaction amount, misleading merchant billing information, failure to provide the service/funds as represented, and a merchant refund/correction that was not properly completed. Despite my attempts to explain the situation to multiple Wells Fargo representatives, Wells Fargo mislabeled or mishandled the claim as a duplicate-charge issue, which did not match the facts of my dispute.

Because Wells Fargo did not correctly classify the dispute, I do not believe a reasonable investigation was completed. I am requesting that Wells Fargo reopen and properly investigate this matter as an incorrect and misleading card transaction, not merely as a duplicate charge.

It has become apparent to me that, rather than extending funds as a traditional loan, the bank may have utilized my promissory note as a form of deposit to facilitate transactions with third parties, such as my seller.

However, despite my repeated requests and demands, the bank has failed to comply with legal obligations to produce relevant documentation for verification. 

Now, regarding the contract in question, I've learned that for a contract to be enforced, it needs five key ingredients. These include : 1. **Offer and Acceptance : ** Clearly defined terms and an agreement between parties. 

2. **Legal Purpose : ** The contract must have a lawful purpose and can not involve any illegal activities. 

3. **Competent Parties : ** Both parties must be of legal age and mentally capable of understanding the contract. 

4. **Mutual Assent : ** Both parties must fully understand and agree to the terms of the contract. 

5. **Consideration : ** There must be an exchange of something valuable between the parties.

2. Wheres the XXXX Report? 

3. Wheres the proof of funds receipt to show that Ive received funds for this particular loan? 

If you give a bank a promissory note, they are required to give you a cash receipt. They owe you that money under a RE-COUPMENT or asset. If you take the receipt back, they should give you some money. They call it an offset in accounting, but in the UCC it is called a RE-COUPMENT. Under Title 12 USC 1813 ( L ) ( 1 ) when you deposit a promissory note, it becomes a cash item. They have come out with an affidavit of a lost note or destroyed instrument. Under UCC 3-309 you have to show four elements to claim a lost instrument : 1 ) you were in possession at the that the obligor on the note is indemnified by you against and future claims ; 4 ) the loss was not due to a transfer.

The mortgage company is not applying the correct accounting entries under GAAP. They're treating the account as a trade receivable through securitization as an off balance sheet financing technique. Since they accepted the instrument that I have tendered, I have a claim or possessionary right in the instrument and its proceeds under 3-306 of the UCC. Any defense and any claim in RE-COUPMENT under section 3-305 of the UCC, which I shall exercise at my option, if they do not credit my account. By depositing the Note ( an asset of the originators/ makers of the note ) by the XXXX. XXXX, the loan, which had not yet been advanced to mortgagors by the mortgage company, was paid therefore there can not be a " holder-in-due- course '' of the Note if it has already been paid. To be a " holder-in-due- course '' of the note, the note must be held by the lender until the note is paid off by the borrower and returned to the borrower. Depositing the note, in effect, cancels the note because the lender has just been paid ( cash receipts for the deposit ) and no " receipt '' for the deposit was ever given to the borrower. The XXXX. XXXX must follow GAAP, as do all banks, and show a corresponding " liability '' for the " asset '' ( note ) they deposited. That liability is money the bank OWES to borrowers for their asset that was deposited. 

As soon as the Note was deposited, the balance due on the Note was XXXX. However, the assignee, thinking that they are the " holder-in-due- course '' of the note, file a foreclosure on the mortgagors when the mortgagors fail to make the payments. The transferee/assignee is not aware and does not see the " liability '' owed by the original " lender '' who deposited the note because it was entered onto another entities balance sheet. This " off-balance- sheet '' financing is illegal and a fraud but common with banks who sell mortgages and notes to investors as securities. 

The Assignee, or new possessor of the Note, has no security interest in the note and can not claim foreclosure on the note because it is not the " holder-in-due- course ''. I am a XXXX U.S. military veteran and single mother of XXXX. On XX/XX/year>, I entered into a home improvement financing agreement through PowerPay LLC and XXXX Bank ( Loan # XXXX XXXX ) to fund a roof replacement by XXXX XXXX ( Georgia License # XXXX ) at my property. 

I am filing this complaint for the following reasons : 1. FUNDS DISBURSED OR AT RISK OF DISBURSEMENT WITHOUT PROJECT COMPLETION AUTHORIZATION The Borrower Payment Authorization ( Exhibit A of the Loan and Security Agreement ) contains two parts. Part I was signed by me on XX/XX/year> as an initial authorization. Part II the Project Completion Authorization has NOT been signed by me. The agreement explicitly states that funds are to be disbursed to the Authorized Service Provider upon completion of the project, as evidenced by the borrower 's signature on Part II. 

The roofing project was NOT completed satisfactorily. Independent inspections on XX/XX/year> and XX/XX/year> identified multiple critical deficiencies including improper drip edge installation, raised starter shingles creating wind-uplift risk, improperly cut gable rake drip edges that will cause leaks, incorrect step flashing with visible open penetrations, and soft spots indicating potential structural damage. A forensic inspection is currently underway. 

Despite the project being defective and incomplete, I am concerned that PowerPay may attempt to disburse funds to XXXX XXXX based on Part I alone, or that XXXX XXXX may fraudulently represent that the project has been completed. I have formally notified both PowerPay and XXXX Bank in writing not to disburse funds without my Part II signature. 

2. POTENTIAL MILITARY LENDING ACT VIOLATION I am a XXXX U.S. military veteran. The Loan and Security Agreement ( Section 14 ) contains explicit Military Lending Act ( MLA ) language acknowledging that the arbitration provision " does not apply '' to covered borrowers. Under 32 C.F.R. 232.8 ( c ), mandatory arbitration clauses in consumer credit contracts are void and unenforceable as applied to covered borrowers under the MLA.

I am concerned that PowerPay and/or XXXX Bank may attempt to compel arbitration of any dispute related to this loan, in potential violation of the MLA. I am requesting that the CFPB review whether the lender properly verified my status as a covered borrower under the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) database as required by 32 C.F.R. 232.5 ( b ) prior to executing this agreement, and whether the arbitration clause as written and applied complies with MLA requirements.

3. DECEPTIVE PRACTICES BY AUTHORIZED SERVICE PROVIDER PowerPay and XXXX Bank have a financial relationship with XXXX XXXX as an Authorized Service Provider ( # XXXX ). XXXX XXXX : Misrepresented the quality of materials that would be installed. 
Installed a defective roof under conditions I explicitly objected to ( heavy rain ). 
Failed to provide a certificate of insurance. 
Performed partial repairs while refusing to address critical deficiencies. 
Has not fulfilled the terms of the contract. 

As the financing entity that entered into a program sponsor relationship with XXXX XXXX, PowerPay has responsibility for ensuring that its Authorized Service Providers fulfill their contractual obligations before funds are released. Disbursing funds to a contractor that has not completed work satisfactorily and whose work has been found critically deficient by independent inspectors would constitute an unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice ( UDAAP ) under the Consumer Financial Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. 5531.

4. RISK OF ADVERSE CREDIT REPORTING I am concerned that if PowerPay or XXXX Bank disburses funds to XXXX XXXX and I refuse to begin payments on a loan for work that was never satisfactorily completed, this dispute will result in adverse credit reporting against me. As a XXXX veteran who has not received the services financed, any adverse credit reporting during the pendency of this active dispute would be unfair and potentially unlawful. 

DESIRED RESOLUTION : 1. PowerPay and XXXX Bank must NOT disburse any funds to XXXX XXXX under Loan # XXXX without my signed Part II Project Completion Authorization. 
2. The loan account must be placed in formal dispute status with no adverse credit reporting during the dispute period.

3. The CFPB should review whether PowerPay properly complied with MLA requirements, including XXXX database verification, prior to executing this loan agreement. 
4. XXXX XXXX should be required to arrange a full roof replacement by a reputable, licensed, and insured contractor at no cost to me, after which I will sign the Project Completion Authorization and honor the loan in full.

5. The arbitration clause in Section 15 of the Loan and Security Agreement should be confirmed as void and unenforceable as to me as a covered borrower under the MLA. 

SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION AVAILABLE : Signed Loan and Security Agreement ( PowerPayXXXX Bank , dated XX/XX/year> ) Borrower Payment Authorization ( Part II unsigned ) XXXX XXXX XXXX contract ( Contract # XXXX ) Independent inspection report ( XX/XX/year> ) Second independent inspection findings ( XX/XX/year> ) Forensic inspection ordered ( findings forthcoming ) XXXX  complaint filed XX/XX/year> Photographic evidence : XXXX : XXXX Formal demand letters sent to PowerPay, XXXX Bank, and XXXX XXXX XXXX XX/XX/year> ) XXXX outreach to XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XX/XX/year> ) I am a XXXX veteran and single mother who trusted XXXX XXXX and PowerPay with a nearly {$35000.00} investment in my home. I am submitting this complaint regarding a private student loan issued by Sallie Mae, which I believe involved unfair and deceptive lending practices, compounded by a lack of adequate guidance during my college enrollment process. 

I am a first-generation college student from a single-parent household. Neither my parent nor I had any prior experience navigating higher education financing. Throughout early XXXX, after applying to the XXXX XXXX XXXX, I made repeated attempts to contact the universitys financial aid office to understand my options for scholarships, grants, or other financial assistance. Despite multiple calls, I was unable to obtain clear or actionable information and was frequently redirected without meaningful support. 

It was not until I attended in-person orientation ( after incurring travel expenses we could not afford ) that I was informed that my full out-of-state tuition balance would be due and that I had not qualified for institutional financial aid. At that point, I was told that my only remaining option to attend was to take out private student loans. This created a situation of significant stress, pressure and urgency, as I had already committed time, money, and effort toward attending the university. 

Under these circumstances, I applied for and was immediately approved for a large private loan through Sallie Mae, despite having limited financial experience and no meaningful understanding of complex loan terms. I reasonably relied on the assumption that such a loan would be structured in a way that was manageable and appropriate for a student borrower. 

Critically, I did not understand nor was it clearly explained to me in a way I could reasonably comprehend, that the loan was structured in a manner that would result in negative amortization. I believed that my required monthly payments of {$25.00} would at least cover accruing interest or reduce my balance. Instead, the loan allowed substantial unpaid interest to accrue and capitalize over time. 

As disclosed in the loan documents, more than {$19000.00} in unpaid interest was expected to accrue during the initial repayment period alone. As a result, despite making all required payments on time and never missing a payment, my loan balance has increased significantly from approximately {$41000.00} to nearly {$60000.00}. While I am still enrolled in school. 

Additionally, the loan carries a high, variable interest rate ( over 11 % at origination, with the potential to rise substantially ), further exacerbating the financial burden. The structure and terms of this loan were not adequately explained in a way that accounted for my lack of financial sophistication as a first-generation student borrower. 

Due to the financial strain and the realization that I would need to take out similarly large private loans for each remaining year of my education, I was ultimately forced to transfer to a different institution. Continuing at the XXXX XXXX XXXX would have required me to incur an unsustainable level of debt over multiple years. This decision significantly altered my educational path and was not based on academic preference, but rather on the financial hardship and risk created by the loan structure and lack of adequate guidance. 

I believe this loan was issued without proper consideration of my ability to repay and was structured in a way that is inherently harmful to borrowers, particularly those in vulnerable or inexperienced positions. I further believe that the combination of inadequate institutional guidance and the lenders approval of a high-risk loan contributed to my current financial hardship. 

I am requesting that this loan be reviewed for potential relief, including but not limited to interest reduction, balance adjustment, or discharge, based on unfair, deceptive, or predatory lending practices. 

I am prepared to provide supporting documentation, including the loan disclosure showing the accrual of unpaid interest and the resulting increase in loan balance despite consistent, on-time payments.
label: Student loan

I am filing a complaint versus : Beyond Finance XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, Texas XXXX XXXX utilized Beyond Finance to settle a debt. In short, the debt balance was circa $ XXXXThe " debt settlement '' was XXXX  {$17000.00}. 

My complaint is in connection with adequate disclosures, or lack thereof. Today, XXXX, I called the Beyond Finance Call Center. From viewing my dashboard, I could see my " Special Purpose Account '' balance, versus what is remaining to be paid to this creditor, was nearing an equal amount. 

I asked when my Special Purpose Account deposits would cease. I was told by the representative that scheduled payments would continue up to and including XXXX. However, the Special Purpose Account balance, after approximately two more monthly payments, would be equal to what the debt settlement amount is equal to. However, I was informed that there is an owed " fee '' of approximately {$5000.00}, which is equal to at least 9-10 more monthly payments of {$530.00}.

Had I known " the fee '' amounted to such a large percentage of the settlement ( AT THE TIME OF SETTLEMENT ), I would not have proceeded further. As such, I feel that this practice was deceptive, and is itself creating an undo hardship.

I am writing to formally document and report concerns regarding my experience as a student and student-athlete at XXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX to XXXX. 

I enrolled as a XXXX major with the intention of pursuing medical school and was recruited with the promise of strong academic support, close faculty relationships, and a quality educational environment. I was also offered a partial athletic scholarship as a member of the volleyball team. Unfortunately, my experience did not align with these representations in several significant ways. 

1. Financial Aid and Administrative Support During orientation, my parent and I spent several hours in the financial aid office seeking guidance on loans and related processes. We received minimal assistance, were instructed to complete complex forms independently, and encountered staff who were unable or unwilling to answer questions. This lack of support created confusion and left us without a clear understanding of financial obligations. 

2. XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX As a member of the volleyball team, I experienced what I believe to be unsafe training practices and inadequate medical oversight. Over two years, I sustained five injuries despite having no prior injuries in XXXX years of playing volleyball. Concerns about injuries were frequently dismissed, and I was encouraged to continue training despite ongoing pain. 

After leaving the university, I was diagnosed with a torn labrum, which ultimately ended my volleyball career. I believe earlier evaluation and proper medical attention may have prevented further damage. 

Additionally, I was subjected to an ice bath that I believe was conducted at an unsafe temperature and/or duration. Following this, I became physically ill. When I raised concerns even during the treatment, they were not taken seriously. I am concerned that this reflects a broader lack of attention to XXXX safety. 

3. Academic Quality and Resources The academic experience within the Biology program did not meet expectations. Laboratory facilities were limited and, in my experience, not adequately maintained or equipped. Coursework, including Organic Chemistry, lacked depth and rigor appropriate for students preparing for professional school. Much of the instruction consisted of repetitive tasks rather than comprehensive learning. 

4. Facilities and Program Development The volleyball program appeared underdeveloped during my time at the university. Basic resources, such as a team locker room, were not available until my second year. The overall structure and support for the program did not reflect what was presented during recruitment. 

5. Overall Concerns Based on my experience, I believe there was a significant gap between what was promised to prospective students and what was actually delivered. This includes academic preparation, student support services, and XXXX care. Given the financial investment required to attend the university, these discrepancies are deeply concerning. 

I am submitting this complaint in the interest of accountability and to help ensure that future students are provided with accurate information, adequate support, and a safe environment. 

I would appreciate acknowledgment of this complaint and information regarding any steps the university may take to review or address these concerns.

This complaint is not duplicative. My earlier complaint addressed the underlying fraudulent / unauthorized charges on the credit-card account. This complaint addresses Chases separate conduct in furnishing inaccurate information to consumer reporting agencies, including reporting the account as delinquent, maxed out, or over limit based on charges I dispute as fraudulent. The legal and factual issue here is inaccurate credit reporting and failure to correct furnished information after notice, not merely the underlying transaction dispute. 


I am submitting this complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . / JPMCB Card Services regarding a credit-card account that is being reported as delinquent even though the balance is the result of fraudulent / unauthorized charges that I do not owe. 

The account is showing on my credit report as JPMCB Card Services with an approximately {$10000.00} balance on a {$10000.00} credit limit, along with derogatory payment history and maxed-out or over-limit utilization. This is causing ongoing harm to my credit report and credit standing. However, this balance is not valid debt that I am responsible for because it resulted from fraud / unauthorized use. 

Under the Truth in Lending Act, the Fair Credit Billing Act, and Regulation Z, liability for unauthorized use of a credit card is limited, and unauthorized charges are billing errors that must be reasonably investigated and resolved. See 15 U.S.C. 1643 and 12 C.F.R. 1026.12 ( b ) and 1026.13. A use is unauthorized when it is made by a person without actual, implied, or apparent authority and from which the cardholder receives no benefit.

Regulation Zs official interpretation also states that, during the billing-error process, a creditor must not make an adverse credit report concerning the disputed amount because the consumer does not pay that disputed amount, although the creditor may report that the amount is disputed. To the extent Chase reported this account as delinquent based on disputed fraudulent charges, that reporting is improper. In addition, under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, a
furnisher may not furnish information to a consumer reporting agency if it knows or has reasonable cause to believe the information is inaccurate. Furnishers also must maintain reasonable policies and procedures regarding the accuracy and integrity of information furnished and must investigate direct disputes concerning a consumers liability for a debt. See 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 and 12 C.F.R. 1022.42 and 1022.43. 

Despite notice of fraud / unauthorized use, Chase has continued to report this balance and derogatory account history as if I am responsible for the debt. This has resulted in inaccurate balance reporting, inaccurate delinquency reporting, and serious damage to my credit profile. If Chase failed to conduct a reasonable investigation, failed to correct the balance, or continued furnishing inaccurate information after notice, that conduct also raises concerns under the prohibition on unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices under 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536.

I am requesting immediate correction. This fraudulent balance should not be treated as my debt, and the negative reporting associated with it should be removed from my credit reports. If Chase contends that I am liable for any portion of this balance, then I request a complete written explanation and all documents Chase relied on to conclude that the charges were authorized and legally my responsibility.

The restriction was imposed within hours of a PayPal agent confirming in writing that my account was " fully usable. '' During the chat session in which the restriction was delivered, I disclosed twice that I am a terminally ill, end-stage XXXX XXXX patient on continuous IV life support medication and that the {$64.00} was the difference between eating or not eating. The agent acknowledged the disclosure, took no escalation action, and returned to script. PayPal has refused to identify any specific policy, term of service, or legal basis for the restriction. 

A. ACCOUNT BACKGROUND AND PAYPAL 'S INITIAL INSTRUCTION On or about XX/XX/XXXX or XXXX, 2026, I applied for a PayPal XXXX XXXX through my existing PayPal account. The application was rejected on the basis that my Social Security XXXX was allegedly associated with another account. I contacted PayPal support, and an agent instructed me to close and reopen my account to " reset '' the issue. I followed that instruction. 

B. AGENT XXXX 'S " FULLY USABLE '' REPRESENTATION ( XX/XX/year> ) On XX/XX/year>, I attempted to reapply for the Debit Card and was directed to contact support again. I disclosed to the agent that I had previously operated a business that XXXX have used PayPal. XXXX XXXX informed me I was not eligible for the card at this time, but stated clearly and in writing that my account was " fully usable '' and that I could " send and receive payments, shop online wherever PayPal is accepted, and move funds using your linked bank account or card. '' This representation was unambiguous. It confirmed that my account was in good standing and that I could transact freely, including receiving deposits and moving funds to my linked bank account. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX AND IMMEDIATE RESTRICTION ( XX/XX/year> ) On XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXX AM CT, a {$64.00} deposit from XXXX posted to my PayPal balance. XXXX is a legitimate gift card resale platform. I had sold a XXXX XXXX gift card I had received. This is a legal transaction with a legal company. I attempted to transfer the funds to my linked checking account. Within hours of the deposit posting, PayPal flagged my account and presented me with a set of XXXX steps it described as necessary " to secure my account. '' The window between XXXX XXXX 's written confirmation that the account was " fully usable '' ( XX/XX/XXXX ) and the account restriction ( XX/XX/XXXX ) was approximately XXXX hours. The only intervening variable was the XXXX deposit. 

XXXX THE 8-STEP PROCESS I completed all 8 steps. Four were identity verification measures : email verification ( already completed ), facial recognition using my driver 's license, verification of two linked card transactions with 4-digit codes, and providing the full number of my new XXXX XXXX debit card. Step XXXX required me to photograph my driver 's license again for address verification, duplicating the document already provided during facial recognition. Steps XXXX and XXXX are the most significant. PayPal required me to provide a written synopsis of the {$64.00} XXXX transaction, including copies of all transaction-related emails between myself and XXXX, and the same for an earlier XXXX deposit. These steps had nothing to do with identity verification. They compelled me to explain what XXXX is as a business, describe how the transaction worked, and surrender my private correspondence with a third-party company. PayPal conditioned my access to my own funds on the production of this information. I complied because I needed the {$64.00} to buy groceries. 

XXXX PAYPAL 'S OWN PROMOTION OF CARDCASH ( XXXX ) PayPal 's own help documentation actively directs its users to XXXX. PayPal XXXX XXXX XXXX, currently live at XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, states in plain language that users can " exchange unwanted gift cards for cash in your PayPal balance via XXXX. '' The page provides step-by-step instructions : go to XXXX, enter the merchant 's name and balance amount, click GET OFFER, connect with PayPal, and receive XXXX PayPal balance. I followed this exact process. PayPal is marketing XXXX as a feature of its platform while simultaneously restricting accounts that use it and compelling consumers to justify the very transactions PayPal promoted. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX 'S CONDUCT : THE DUAL-FRAMING CONTRADICTION ( XX/XX/year> ) PayPal XXXX XXXX delivered XXXX account restriction via live chat on XX/XX/year>, beginning at approximately XXXX AM CT. I have preserved timestamped screenshots. XXXX XXXX XXXX contradictory framings of the same restriction within the same conversation. 

XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) : XXXX stated : " Your account is temporarily blocked. We noticed a new PayPal account has been created using your name. We understand this might be concerning, and we want to make sure you're aware of it. For now, some of your account features are temporarily blocked. '' She further stated : " To protect your account, some of your account features have been blocked. Although you can still receive money, you are blocked from the following ... '' This framing presents the restriction as a protective measure, as though PayPal were safeguarding me from identity theft. 

XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) : Later in the same conversation, after I disclosed my medical condition, XXXX delivered a fundamentally different characterization : " After a thorough review of your account, we've determined that it presents a risk to our platform. We regularly review all accounts on our platform, and if we identify any potential risk to PayPal, our customers, or our banking partners, an email is sent to notify you that you can no longer use our services. To help protect our security systems, we're unable to disclose the specific details of the risk identified. Any funds in this account will be held for 120 days to help minimize the risk to PayPal from customers who may file disputes or chargebacks. '' These are opposite characterizations delivered by the same agent in the same session. One says PayPal is protecting me ; the other says PayPal is protecting itself from me. The only variable that changed between the XXXX framings was my disclosure of my terminal medical condition and the urgency of my need for funds. The phrase " presents a risk to our platform '' accuses me, as a person, of being a threat to PayPal. The refusal to " disclose the specific details of the risk identified '' removes any ability to contest the characterization. 

XXXX MEDICAL DISCLOSURES ABSORBED WITHOUT ESCALATION During the XX/XX/XXXX chat session with XXXX, I disclosed my medical condition twice and offered to provide documentation. 

XXXX XXXX : I stated : " What is the address of your XXXX XXXX? I am a endstage XXXX XXXX patient currently at a Status XXXX and on a continuous IV life support medication. These funds are the difference between me eating or not today. '' XXXX 's XXXX : " I understand this is a critical situation, and I want to help you with your account. However, I can not provide the address of our XXXX XXXX. '' She did not escalate, did not flag it for supervisory review, and did not offer any accommodation. 

XXXX XXXX : I stated : " When will I have access to my balance? I am terminal. '' I offered : " If you would like a photo of the iv pump as proof, I am happy to provide it. '' XXXX 's XXXX : " I'm looking into your issue and will update you shortly. Please stay connected. '' A terminally ill person on IV life support disclosed twice, offered photographic documentation, and received a hold-pattern response identical to what would be delivered for a routine login issue. 

I had to rephrase my request from " General Counsel '' to " mailing address for legal correspondence '' before XXXX would provide : PayPal, Attn : Legal Dept./Civil, XXXX North XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX CA XXXX. This information is required to be provided upon request under Wisconsin law. Its initial refusal created an additional barrier to the exercise of my rights during an interaction in which the agent had full knowledge of my medical condition. 

H. MY MEDICAL CONDITION I am an end-stage XXXX XXXX patient, currently classified at Status XXXX on the transplant waiting list at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, Wisconsin. I receive continuous intravenous life support medication. I recorded a video during this experience documenting my medical condition and the circumstances under which PayPal 's restriction was imposed. This video is available upon request.

REQUESTED RELIEF 1. Immediate release of all funds held in my PayPal account, including the {$64.00} XXXX deposit and any other balance. 
XXXX. Written confirmation that no adverse information has been or will be reported to any consumer reporting agency, banking database, or partner institution. 
XXXX. Written explanation identifying the specific policy, term of service, or legal basis for the restriction, which PayPal has refused to provide.

4. Deletion or return of all information collected during Steps 5 and 6 of the 8-step process, including my written narratives about XXXX and my private email correspondence, compelled under duress of a fund hold.

5. Review of PayPal 's practice of restricting accounts for transactions promoted by its own help documentation ( XXXX ). 
6. Review of PayPal 's agent protocols regarding medical disclosures and whether a terminally ill consumer disclosing an immediate food-access emergency warrants escalation rather than scripted responses.

SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION 1. Chat transcript, XX/XX/year> ( XXXX XXXX, " fully usable '' representation ) XXXX. Chat transcript, XX/XX/year> ( XXXX XXXX, dual-framing restriction, medical disclosures, General Counsel refusal ) XXXX. Timestamped screenshots of XX/XX/XXXX chat session XXXX. XXXX transaction confirmation ( {$64.00} ) XXXX. XXXX account security process records ( On Request ) XXXX. Video recording of medical condition during restriction event ( On Request ) XXXX. PayPal XXXX XXXX XXXX ( archived ) XXXX. PayPal XXXX record ( NMLS ID XXXX, Wisconsin License # XXXX ) ( On request )

text:
I am submitting this complaint regarding inaccurate credit reporting tied to my student loan account after it was transferred to a new servicer, CRI.

At no point prior to the account being reported as late did I receive any communication, notice, or correspondence from CRI indicating that they had taken over my loan, that payments were due, or where payments should be directed. As a result, I was unaware that my loan had been transferred or that any action was required on my part. 

As soon as I became aware of who was servicing my loan, I immediately brought the account current and ensured that all payments were made. Upon identifying the correct loan servicer, I paid a lump sum of {$780.00} to bring the account current and have since enrolled in automatic payments to prevent any future issues. This demonstrates my consistent intent to remain in good standing.

Despite this, CRI reported late payments to the credit bureaus. This reporting is inaccurate and unfair, as I was never provided proper notice or an opportunity to make timely payments before being marked delinquent. 

This situation has caused significant harm. My credit score dropped from approximately XXXX to XXXX as a direct result of this reporting. Additionally, long-standing credit accounts have reduced my credit limits due to this sudden and inaccurate negative activity. I have maintained a history of on-time payments across all accounts for over 10 years, and this is the first instance of any negative reporting. 

I made every reasonable effort to resolve this directly with the company by requesting information about the loan transfer, payment expectations, and the basis for the reported late payments. However, I did not receive adequate resolution or correction. 

I am requesting that all inaccurately reported late payments related to this account be removed from my credit reports and that my account history be corrected to reflect accurate, timely payment behavior. I am further requesting that these corrections be applied to all tradelines associated with this account, not just a single loan segment, to ensure my credit report is fully and accurately updated. 
I also request that CRI ensure proper communication practices are followed for future account transfers so that consumers are not placed in similar situations. 

This issue is not due to a failure to pay, but rather a failure in communication and proper notification by the servicer, which has resulted in unjust credit damage.
label: Student loan

The account in question ( LoanCare LLC, account ending in XXXX ) is being reported with conflicting and inaccurate information, including : - The account is reported as " Current '' while simultaneously reflecting a 30-day delinquency, which is a direct contradiction and violates the requirement for maximum possible accuracy under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ).

- Dispute remarks are inconsistent across TransUnion, Experian, and Equifax, indicating that the furnisher has failed to maintain consistent and accurate reporting. 
- The account continues to reflect dispute resolved consumer disagrees, suggesting that no reasonable investigation was conducted, and the dispute was processed through automated systems such as e-Oscar.

Under FCRA 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ) and 12 CFR 1022.43, both the furnisher and the credit reporting agencies are required to conduct a reasonable investigation of disputed information.

Additionally, CFPB Circular 2022-07 clarifies that furnishers must not rely solely on automated dispute responses and must review all relevant information provided by the consumer.

LoanCares reporting also appears to violate CDIA Metro 2 standards, as account status, payment history, and delinquency codes must be internally consistent and accurately reflect the true status of the account. 


Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

text:
On XX/XX/XXXX a check for {$4700.00} was written from the XXXX XXXX  as an inheritance disbursement to my ex-husband. He lives in XXXX and was in the XXXX for 12 days for his mother 's funeral. I paid for his flight and he wanted to use some of the money to reimburse me and also to have access to it during his 2 week stay. The check was signed by his half-brother who was one of the Trustees on his mother 's Trust.

We decided to put the check into my Wells Fargo bank account, and thought that he would be able to access the money more quickly, so he endorsed the check and I countersigned it. I made a mobile check deposit via the Wells Fargo app on XX/XX/XXXX not realizing that a third-party check wouldn't be accepted in that way. 

Later that day, the transaction was flagged by Wells Fargo as a 3rd party credit, which they deemed as fraudulent activity, and a notification stating such was sent to me. I was also notified ( in the same message ) that my account was going to be closed in due course as a result of the alleged fraudulent activity. 

However, the next day ( on XX/XX/XXXX ), I received a second message from Wells Fargo which said that they were delaying the availability of the funds from the deposited check, and that the funds would be available on XX/XX/XXXX. 

This was confusing. I didn't know whether the account would actually be closed or not, or whether it would be closed after the money was made available. 

After that second message, we both went into the local Wells Fargo branch in an effort to show our ID and prove that the transaction was legitimate and try to stop the closing of my account, or at least get the funds released earlier because my ex-husband was returning to XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, one day before the funds were supposed to be released. 

However, there wasnt a banker available in the branch to verify the documents on that day. I tried to make an appointment to see a manager at a different branch before he had to go back, but there was no one available. 

In due course, my Wells Fargo account was indeed closed, as per the initial notification, and I was told that the funds would be sent back to XXXX XXXX  7-10 days after my account was closed. It was closed on XX/XX/XXXX, but 15 months later, we still have not received anything. 

All this time, we have been seeking to get the money released, in various ways, in connection with multiple communications with Wells Fargo and XXXX XXXX. I have spoken to my local Wells Fargo branch manager and loss prevention phone assistants repeatedly for over a year. During these many conversations, I have been told a variety of different stories on how to get the funds released and have followed their instructions, but to no avail. 

My brother in law ( who is a Trustee on the account ) called the XXXX XXXX  branch where the XXXX was set up to request a letter of indemnity. This request was made following the instructions from Wells Fargo to facilitate the release of the funds, but was told that they dont know which letter to send or what it needs to say to get the money released because its not fraud. 

Another brother-in-law ( who wrote the check ) had also been to a different branch of the XXXX Bank to request that Wells Fargo return the funds , but was told that it needs to be done by Wells Fargo.

In the most recent contact with Wells Fargo customer service, I was told that the only way for the money to be released was for the writer of the check ( my brother-in-law ) to go into any branch of XXXX XXXX, and tell them that the funds from the said check to the amount of {$4700.00}, had been placed and held in suspense by Wells Fargo, that the recipient hasnt received the funds and that XXXX Bank needs to file a letter of XXXX with Wells Fargo to recall the funds back to the said US Bank account. I was assured that US Bank would understand how to proceed from there and whom to contact at Wells Fargo, etc. 

So, with a letter explaining the whole situation, he again went to XXXX XXXX. While he was there, an employee of XXXX  Bank called me and said they can't do that because it is Wells Fargos responsibility to distribute the funds to me.

I then went back to my local Wells Fargo branch manager in frustration and updated her on the situation. She actually called the US Bank Customer Service line to ask what their procedure was in cases like this and was told that XXXX XXXX  should indeed file a letter of XXXX with Wells Fargo to recall the funds, but they won't do it! She also told me that if my ex-husband can't fly over here from XXXX in the next few days, the funds will most likely go to XXXX XXXX! 

I called Wells Fargo again and was told that banks only keep the money for 3-4 months and that the funds went to Utah XXXX XXXX in XX/XX/XXXX, which was only a few weeks after the check had been deposited! If that was the case, why wasn't I told that a year ago? 

I called Utah XXXX XXXX. They said they don't have it under any of the names on the check and told me to contact Wells Fargo again for a reference number and date it was sent. I did that and was told that the reference number was my account number. XXXX XXXX said it wasn't that. 

I again called Wells Fargo, got a different person and was told that the funds were sent on a different date, XX/XX/XXXX, but XXXX XXXX still could not find anything. 

I called Wells Fargo a third time and was told that the funds were still held in " suspense '' at Wells Fargo and the only way to get the money was for my ex-husband to fly over here from XXXX and go to a Wells Fargo branch with XXXX forms of ID connected to the case. 

At this point, I finally gave up and started looking for a third party to try and help resolve the situation! 

Thank you for your anticipated help.

THIS IS A SECOND COMPLAINT FILED BECAUSE GM FINANCIAL 'S RESPONSE TO CASE NUMBER XXXX FAILED TO ADDRESS ANY VIOLATION ALLEGED, AND BECAUSE GM FINANCIAL HAS CONTINUED AND ESCALATED ITS UNLAWFUL CONDUCT AFTER THAT COMPLAINT WAS FILED AND CLOSED. 
This complaint is related to prior CFPB complaint Case Number XXXX, filed XX/XX/XXXX and XXXX filed on or about XXXX, XXXX, which all were closed without an inadequate response from GM Financial dated XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a formal complaint with the CFPB against GM Financial, assigned Case Number XXXX. That complaint alleged fraudulent loan origination, misassignment of buyer and cosigner roles, violation of the FTC Holder Rule, unlawful post-rescission credit reporting, and wrongful repossession of a motor vehicle. 
GM Financial responded on XX/XX/XXXX through their Compliance Department, signed by XXXX XXXX Their response consisted of XXXX paragraphs that : ( 1 ) recited the contract terms, ( 2 ) disclaimed responsibility for XXXX XXXX XXXX conduct, ( 3 ) stated that the credit reporting was accurate, and ( 4 ) directed me to contact their customer service line. Their response did not address a single violation alleged in the original complaint. 

Specifically, GM Financial 's XX/XX/XXXX response failed entirely to address : The fraudulent misassignment of buyer and cosigner roles at signing The FTC Holder Rule, 16 C.F.R. 433, which is printed in bold capital letters on page 5 of the very contract GM Financial attached to their response The wrongful repossession of the vehicle on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX days before their response was even written The {$500.00} repossession fee assessed on a rescinded contract The legal invalidity of reporting delinquency on a contract rescinded before the first payment was ever due The XXXX formal written rescission notices received by GM Financial on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX I submitted consumer feedback to the CFPB disputing GM Financial 's response in its entirety. The complaint was closed without resolution. This second complaint is filed because GM Financial 's conduct has continued and escalated since the prior complaint was filed. 

NEW AND CONTINUING VIOLATIONS SINCE THE PRIOR COMPLAINT A. The Wrongful Repossession - XX/XX/XXXX GM Financial 's own payment history, submitted as part of their CFPB response to Case Number XXXX, confirms the following critical timeline : XX/XX/XXXX : Contract signed XX/XX/XXXX : GM Financial received and signed for formal Rescission of Contract via certified mail, XXXX days before the first payment was ever due XX/XX/XXXX : First payment due date under the contract XX/XX/XXXX : GM Financial received Final Demand for Immediate Rescission via XXXX XX/XX/XXXX : GM Financial received Notice of Fair Debt Collection Practices Act Violations, Notice of Dispute and Demand for Validation Cease and Desist Demand, Notice of Fair Credit Reporting Act Violations XX/XX/XXXX : GM Financial initiated repossession setup confirmed by their own payment history XX/XX/XXXX : GM Financial assessed a {$500.00} miscellaneous repossession fee confirmed by their own payment history XX/XX/XXXX : First CFPB complaint filed XX/XX/XXXX : GM Financial responded to CFPB complaint without addressing the repossession along. 
The first payment under this contract was not due until XX/XX/XXXX. My rescission was received by GM Financial on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX days before any payment was ever owed. No valid payment obligation ever legally arose under this contract. GM Financial repossessed the vehicle on XX/XX/XXXX, nearly XXXX weeks after receiving the first rescission notice and XXXX weeks after receiving the Final Demand. This is a wrongful repossession as a matter of law. The vehicle has not been returned as of the date of this complaint. GM Financial repossessed the vehicle while simultaneously preparing a response to a federal consumer complaint alleging fraud. They did not disclose the repossession in their XX/XX/XXXX CFPB response. The CFPB was not informed that GM Financial had taken the vehicle XXXX days before filing their response. 
XXXX GM Financial 's Own Contract Prohibits Their Defense GM Financial 's XX/XX/XXXX response states they were not present during contract negotiations and bear no responsibility for XXXX XXXX 's conduct. This position is directly and completely foreclosed by page XXXX of the Motor Vehicle Retail Installment Sales Contract that GM Financial itself attached to its CFPB response.
