This is the FTC Holder Rule, 16 C.F.R. 433. By purchasing this contract from XXXX XXXX, GM Financial assumed legal responsibility for all claims and defenses arising from its fraudulent origination. GM Financial submitted this language to the CFPB as part of their defense and appears to have either not read it or hoped the CFPB would not. This is itself an unfair and deceptive act in connection with a consumer complaint response. 
C. Continued Unlawful Credit Reporting As of the date of this complaint, GM Financial continues to report this account as delinquent on all three major consumer reporting agencies, Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. These derogatory entries reflect payment obligations that never legally arose because the contract was rescinded before the first payment was ever due.

VIOLATIONS ALLEGED The following federal violations have occurred and are documented : 1. Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), Willful furnishing of inaccurate derogatory information to consumer reporting agencies after receiving written notice of rescission on XX/XX/XXXX and Final Demand on XX/XX/XXXX. text:
I am filing this complaint regarding an unauthorized electronic fund transfer and the improper storage and use of a debit card issued through my health insurance incentive program. 

On XXXX XXXX XXXX a charge for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX was processed through Google Play using this debit card. This card is intended for restricted, health-related purchases only and was never intended to be used for digital subscriptions or app-based transactions. 

I did not authorize this payment method to be added to my Google account, nor did I authorize its storage or use for any transactions. I have never used this card for any purchases through Google Play or any mobile applications.

Upon reviewing my account, I found that the card appears in my Google payment methods with a status indicating incomplete information and can not be used. Despite this, a successful charge was processed. A payment method that is incomplete and flagged as unusable should not be capable of processing a transaction. 

Additionally, there is no record of prior failed transactions or billing attempts involving this card, and I did not receive any notification of attempted charges. I routinely receive payment failure notifications from other services, but no such notification was provided in this case. 

The timing of the transaction is also concerning. The charge occurred within approximately 50 minutes of a deposit being made to this cardbefore I was aware that funds had been added. There was no prior indication that this card was associated with any billing activity.

Based on these facts, I am disputing this as an unauthorized electronic fund transfer under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( Regulation E ).

This situation raises concerns regarding : - Unauthorized storage of payment credentials - Lack of consumer authorization for payment method use - Failure of controls preventing transactions on incomplete or unusable payment methods - Lack of notification regarding attempted or completed transactions I am requesting the following resolution : 1. A full refund of the unauthorized transaction 2. Removal of this payment method from all associated systems 3. A complete audit trail showing when and how this payment method was added, including any authorization records 4. A technical explanation of how a payment method marked as incomplete and unusable was able to process a successful charge 5. Confirmation of corrective actions to prevent unauthorized storage and use of payment methods in the future This matter involves the unauthorized use of a financial instrument and requires a formal investigation. 

I expect a timely and substantive response addressing these concerns. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

Complaint Regarding Excessive NSF Fees and Unfair Practices During XX/XX/year> Ice Storm To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding my banking experience with Wells Fargo and the excessive non-sufficient funds ( NSF ) fees that were charged to my account during and after the XX/XX/year> ice storm in XXXX, Tennessee. 

I am a XXXX  XXXX working in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. My income is project-based and depends heavily on XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. During the XX/XX/year> ice storm, the city of XXXX experienced a major shutdown. Over XXXX residents lost powersome for up to XXXX weeksand many businesses were forced to close. This disruption lasted well beyond the initial storm and affected income opportunities across the city for at least a month. 

As a direct result of this crisis, I incurred multiple NSF fees due to interrupted income and delayed payments. These were not the result of negligence, but of a citywide emergency that significantly impacted my ability to earn and maintain financial stability. 

To date, I have counted nine ( 9 ) NSF fees. While Wells Fargo reversed other fees, 11 charges from the ice storm until mid XXXX, they cited this as their maximum allowable per year was 2 and no relief under current policy. However, the remaining fees continue to place an ongoing financial burden on me. I am effectively paying down these fees as an additional bill, which has made it increasingly difficult to keep up with my other financial obligations. I will likely incur more after this complaint. 

What is especially concerning is that many of these NSF fees are higher than the transaction amounts themselves. This creates a cycle of hardship that feels disproportionate and exploitative, particularly during a time of crisis. I made multiple attempts to resolve this issue directly with Wells Fargo by filing complaints and speaking with representatives. Despite explaining the circumstances, the bank declined to recognize the ice storm as a qualifying hardship event and did not offer meaningful resolution. 

It is my belief that Wells Fargo failed to act in good faith during a known regional emergency. Their policies appear rigid and disconnected from real-world hardships, allowing them to continue profiting from customers during times of crisis. This has created what feels like a one-sided relationship, especially as a customer of over XXXX  years. 

I respectfully request that this matter be reviewed and that appropriate action be taken. Specifically, I am seeking : A full review and reversal of the remaining NSF fees incurred during the XX/XX/year> ice storm period Consideration of policy changes that limit the number of NSF fees charged, particularly during emergencies Greater accountability from financial institutions in supporting customers during community-wide crises No customer should face repeated penalty fees during a disaster, especially when those fees exceed the original transaction amounts. A limit of one NSF fee in such circumstances would be far more reasonable and humane. 

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter. I appreciate your role in protecting consumers and ensuring fairness within the financial system. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXXXXXX

We were given name tags and taken up an elevator where we were checked in again and placed in a waiting room with several other couples. I believe we received a cruise voucher at that time. 

We were then moved to another room where they played a video that was very emotional and focused on the importance of family vacations. During the video, man spoke about how he had immigrated from another country and how owning a XXXX timeshare allowed him to spend meaningful time with his family. 

After the video, we were introduced to a person named XXXX who us on a tour across the street to a hotel that she said was used exclusively by XXXX timeshare members. During the tour she asked about our employment, our financial situation, and how we typically vacation. While we were touring the property, we encountered an older couple in the elevator who told us that they loved their timeshare. This interaction appeared to reinforce the positive message about the program. 

After the tour we returned to the original building where XXXX began discussing different packages and the XXXX points system. She explained that points could be used for vacations and flights with major airlines. At that point, a manager named XXXX began hovering near the conversation and eventually took over the presentation. 

XXXX began presenting multiple pricing options and repeatedly stated that the numbers looked good. The explanation of the points system was confusing and involved a large amount of information presented very quickly. XXXX said that the points could be used for travel anywhere and even for first-class airline tickets. He also said that we could use the program whenever we wanted and that booking would generally only require a few weeks or months of advance notice. 

We told XXXX several times that we needed time to think about the decision. At that point another woman entered the room and talked about how much she loved the program. She told a story about a friend who had died and how she was able to immediately book travel to attend the funeral because she owned the XXXX program. 

XXXX then returned and continued presenting numbers. He told us that the package he was offering had originally been purchased by another family for approximately {$120000.00} but that XXXX had taken it back and would sell it to us that day for {$60000.00}. Although both me and my fianc are on the XXXX contract, only I was made responsible for the loan and I subsequently found out that the interest rate is XXXX  %.

Before any finalized purchase agreement or clear credit offer was extended, the dealership ran my credit and initiated a hard inquiry. 

A permissible purpose under the FCRA requires a bona fide credit transaction or firm offer of credit. In this case, the credit pull occurred without a finalized agreement and without a clearly disclosed or consummated credit offer, raising concerns under FCRA permissible purpose requirements and adverse impact obligations. 
Misrepresentation of Credit Approval Status ( ECOA / XXXX 15 U.S.C. XXXX ; XXXX XXXX ) I was told at different points that I was both : not approved for the vehicle I selected despite an XXXX FICO score, and XXXX credit score later effectively approved under alternative conditions involving a different vehicle and significantly altered terms. 

These contradictory representations create confusion regarding actual credit determination and appear to be inconsistent with XX/XX/XXXX requirements for fair, consistent, and nondiscriminatory credit evaluation. 

Under XXXX, creditors must provide consistent, nondiscriminatory treatment and must not misrepresent credit decisions or conditions of approval. The shifting narrative regarding approval status and qualification terms suggests potential XXXX violations due to deceptive credit representation. 

The dealership attempted to structure the transaction in a manner that improperly blended credit-based financing terms with cash-down requirements in a way that was not clearly separated or consistently disclosed. 

Under Regulation XXXX ( Truth in Lending Act ), credit terms must be clearly disclosed, and financing conditions must be presented in a transparent and non-misleading manner. Credit and cash components of a transaction must be properly itemized and can not be used in a way that obscures the true cost of credit or the actual loan terms being offered. 

The shifting requirement of : {$25000.00} down payment, later increased to {$30000.00}, and claims of a {$200000.00} down requirement on a ~ {$220000.00} vehicle reflects a lack of consistent underwriting disclosure and raises concerns under XX/XX/XXXX requirement for clear and accurate credit terms and APR disclosure integrity. 

After initially engaging in a transaction for a specific vehicle, I was redirected to a different vehicle I did not select. 

I was told I needed to crawl before I walk, implying I was not permitted to purchase the originally selected vehicle despite strong creditworthiness. This constitutes a classic bait-and-switch pattern, which is prohibited under Section XXXX of the Federal Trade Commission Act and qualifies as a XXXX deceptive practice when a consumer is induced toward XXXX product and then steered to another under pressure. 

The transaction included multiple fees ( documentation, dealer, electronic filing ) and additional warranty products that were not clearly disclosed or itemized. 

Under TILA and Regulation XXXX, all financed charges and optional add-ons must be clearly disclosed, voluntary, and separately agreed upon. Failure to clearly itemize discretionary versus mandatory charges constitutes a material disclosure failure and potential deceptive practice under UDAAP. 

I was instructed to sign documents electronically and was told this process was mandatory. I was not informed that I had the right to request paper documents executed with wet ink signatures. 

Under the E-SIGN Act, electronic signatures are only valid where the consumer provides informed consent to electronic delivery and execution. Misrepresenting electronic signing as mandatory when it is not, or failing to provide meaningful disclosure of alternatives, raises concerns under both E-SIGN compliance requirements and UDAAP standards for deceptive conduct. 

Additionally, the documents were presented in a rushed manner, limiting meaningful review or informed consent. 

As a result of the dealerships conduct : My credit report was accessed via hard inquiry without a clearly consummated transaction. 
I received inconsistent and contradictory representations of credit approval. 
I was subjected to shifting and excessive down payment demands. 
I was steered away from my selected vehicle toward an alternative. 
I was presented with undisclosed or improperly disclosed fees and add-ons. 
I was misled regarding electronic signature requirements and execution rights. 

I was encouraged by dealership personnel to apply for financing under my business profile rather than my personal credit profile, with the representation that doing so would result in a better approval outcome. 

This conduct implicates the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( XXXX ), 15 U.S.C. XXXX et seq., and Regulation XX/XX/XXXX ( XXXXXX/XX/XXXX Part XXXX ), which govern fair access to credit and prohibit discriminatory or misleading credit application practices. 

Under ECOA and Regulation XXXX : A creditor or its agents may not engage in practices that discourage or steer an applicant between credit channels in a manner that is misleading or not based on legitimate underwriting criteria. 
Credit decisions and application channels must be presented in a clear, transparent, and nondiscriminatory manner, without implying that alternative application types are required absent objective underwriting necessity. 

Here, I was directed away from a personal credit applicationdespite a strong personal credit profile ( XXXX FICO ) and encouraged to proceed under a business credit application as a strategy to improve approval likelihood. This created ambiguity regarding : the actual basis of credit evaluation and underwriting pathway, whether different or less favorable underwriting standards were being applied without disclosure, and whether the application process was being structured to influence approval conditions rather than evaluate credit uniformly. 

This conduct also raises concerns under CFPB UDAAP standards ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX, XXXX ) to the extent that a reasonable consumer could be led to believe that switching from personal to business credit was necessary or materially advantageous for approval, without clear disclosure of the underwriting differences, risks, or necessity for such a change.

CFPB COMPLAINT BRIDGECREST, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX : XXXX, XXXX  Summary of the problem I am filing this complaint because Bridgecrest continued collections, allowed repossession, and reported a deficiency balance on a vehicle that had a documented mechanical defect, a failed warranty repair, and an active dispute that I attempted to resolve through a formal XXXX request in XX/XX/XXXX. The defect existed early, was verified by an authorized repair facility, and was never properly repaired. XXXX denied the second repair using mileage as a technicality, despite the defect being pre-existing and the first repair failing. Bridgecrest continued collections and repossession activity despite being aware of the dispute, the failed repair, and my hardship as a XXXX veteran on limited income. 

Detailed timeline of events XX/XX/XXXX : I purchased the vehicle from XXXX. 
XX/XX/XXXX : I reported a transmission defect to XXXX. 
XXXX XXXX # XXXX : XXXX verified the transmission defect and performed a transmission replacement and programming under warranty. 
XX/XX/XXXX : The defect returned, including drivability issues and fluid leakage. 
XXXX denied the second repair due to mileage, even though the defect existed before the mileage limit and the first repair failed. 
XX/XX/XXXX : I submitted a formal ADR request to XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. I received no meaningful response. 
XXXX : Bridgecrest reported a repossession balance and deficiency despite the unresolved mechanical defect and active dispute. 

Documents supporting the defect and failed repair I am providing the following documents upon request : XXXX XXXX documents, including the XXXX XXXX Inspection, Cosmetic Inspection, Controls and Features Inspection, and Plastic Inspection. These documents show XXXX represented the vehicle as mechanically sound, with no drivability issues, no transmission issues, and no abnormal noises or vibrations. 
XXXX XXXX # XXXX documenting the verified transmission defect, the transmission fluid replacement, and the programming performed. 
XXXX XXXX # XXXX documenting my out-of-pocket payment and the continued mechanical issues after the first repair. 
Warranty document showing XXXX coverage for defects in materials or workmanship, including labor. 
My ADR letter from XX/XX/XXXX showing early notice, good-faith dispute resolution attempts, and the companies failure to respond. 
Statements from XXXX personnel, including the regional manager ( XXXX XXXX and the shop owner, acknowledging that a failed transmission after installation is rare, that the mileage denial was a technicality, and that they contacted XXXX regarding the issue.

Why this violates federal law Bridgecrests actions constitute Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) under 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 12 U.S.C. 5536.

Unfair practices : Continuing collections despite a known mechanical defect. 
Allowing repossession during an active dispute. 
Ignoring my hardship as a XXXX veteran. 
Deceptive practices : Failing to provide call logs, account notes, repossession documents, or deficiency calculations. 
Misrepresenting the status of the account while a dispute was active. 
Abusive practices : Taking advantage of my lack of transportation and financial vulnerability. 
Ignoring a failed warranty repair and documented defect. 

Why the repossession and deficiency balance are improper The defect existed before the mileage limit. 
The first repair failed. 
XXXX denied the second repair using a technicality. 
I submitted a formal ADR request in XXXX. 
Bridgecrest continued collections despite the dispute. 
Bridgecrest allowed repossession despite the dispute. 
Bridgecrest reported a deficiency balance despite the dispute. 
These actions violate UDAAP standards and constitute improper repossession activity. 

What I am requesting I request that the CFPB require Bridgecrest to : Provide all call logs, account notes, and internal communications. 
Provide all repossession documents and deficiency balance calculations. 
Provide all communications with XXXX and XXXX regarding my account. 
Investigate the improper repossession and deficiency balance. 
Remove the deficiency balance and correct all negative credit reporting. 

Hardship statement I am a XXXX veteran on limited income. The mechanical defect, failed repair, and denial of warranty coverage left me without reliable transportation and caused significant financial strain. Bridge crest 's actions worsened this hardship by continuing collections and allowing repossession despite a legitimate dispute.

I am submitting this complaint as a follow-up to a previous CFPB complaint ( Case # XXXX ) that was closed without resolution after XXXX provided an inadequate and misleading response.

I was recently prompted to complete an identity verification step when attempting to make an online purchase through XXXX, a retailer I have used with XXXX on multiple prior occasions. When I submitted my information including my name, date of birth, residential address, and Social Security Number XXXX 's system returned an error stating : " These details are already used by another profile. Please review and try again. '' This is my only XXXX account. I did not create any additional profiles. This error indicates that my personal identifying information, including my Social Security Number, may be associated with a fraudulent or unauthorized account. 

In response to my original CFPB complaint, XXXX claimed they were unable to locate my account using the information I provided. This is misleading. Subject : XXXX furnished false and materially misleading account information, falsely claimed adverse marks were removed, and then issued a cease-and-desist after evidence-backed disputes I am submitting this complaint against World Omni Financial Corp. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) regarding account ending XXXX. 

XXXX sent written CFPB response letters to me and my husband XXXX XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX, stating that : ( 1 ) it properly obtained a Relief from Bankruptcy Stay, ( 2 ) the vehicle was subsequently traded-in and paid off by a dealership, ( 3 ) it had previously submitted an update to the consumer reporting agencies to remove such credit marks, and ( 4 ) it was properly reporting the status of the account as paid in full/closed with a {$0.00} balance as of XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX also stated it would not make changes or take further action regarding any future disputes and considered the matter fully resolved. 

Those representations are contradicted by the actual XXXX reporting I reviewed after XXXX made those statements. The tradeline still displays Paid, Closed ; was 30 days past due, with Date Updated XX/XX/XXXX, Last Payment Made XX/XX/XXXX, Payment Received {$19000.00}, Date Closed XX/XX/XXXX, Balance {$0.00}, and an XX/XX/XXXX payment-history rating of XXXX. The tradeline also shows Account previously in dispute-now resolved. reported by credit grant ; CLOSED. In other words, XXXX told CFPB and both consumers that adverse marks had already been removed, yet the derogatory XXXX delinquency remained embedded in the tradeline at the exact closure/payoff event. 

That is not a minor display issue. It is materially misleading furnishing. If XXXX position is that the account was paid off by a dealership, closed with a XXXX balance on XX/XX/XXXX, and adverse marks were removed, then XXXX must explain what specific missed payment and what specific billing cycle allegedly caused a XXXX delinquency to appear at the same moment the account was closed and paid. text:
CFPB COMPLAINT INCOMPLETE INVESTIGATION, CONTRADICTORY RESPONSE, AND REFUSAL TO CORRECT OR FULLY REVIEW REPOSSESSION AND CREDIT REPORTING ISSUES I submit this complaint because Southeast Toyota Finance / World Omni Financial Corp. did not meaningfully investigate the issues raised and instead issued a conclusory XX/XX/year> response stating that it found no evidence of repossession-related communications during bankruptcy, had already updated reporting, and would take no further action on future disputes. That response is not an actual investigation. It is a refusal letter dressed up as one. 

In its XX/XX/year> CFPB response, the company made several key assertions : 1. It properly adhered to the Bankruptcy-related laws during the bankruptcy proceeding.

2. It found no evidence in its records that it communicated with or pressured me regarding repossession during the active bankruptcy period.

3. It claims it previously submitted updates to remove adverse credit marks.

4. It states it will not make changes or take further action regarding future disputes.

5. It claims the matter is fully resolved.

Those assertions remain disputed and appear to be based on an incomplete review. 

First, the companys statement that there was no evidence of repossession-related contact during bankruptcy is not sufficient unless it specifically reviewed third-party vendor records, repossession assignment logs, call records, bankruptcy forwarding activity, recovery notes, dialer records, and any communications made by agents or contractors acting on its behalf. A company can not truthfully say there was no evidence if it only checked its own narrow internal notes and failed to review vendor or third-party records. That is not a negative finding. That is an incomplete investigation. 

Second, the companys response does not identify what records were actually reviewed. It does not say whether it reviewed : any repossession vendor assignments, third-party contractor communications, skip-trace records, outbound call logs, vendor account notes, bankruptcy communication restrictions applied to the account, or internal escalation records concerning the vehicle before payoff.

Without that information, its conclusion is unsubstantiated.

Third, the company attempts to avoid responsibility for the continuing credit reporting harm by stating that it furnished accurate information and does not control how consumer reporting agencies display the data. That is not a complete answer. If a furnisher knows its reporting has produced inaccurate, misleading, incomplete, or contradictory information across bureaus, it still has a duty to investigate disputes reasonably and correct or clarify what it furnished. Saying we sent something, blame the bureaus does not resolve whether the companys own furnishing, coding, timing, bankruptcy notation, payment status, or post-bankruptcy account characterization was inaccurate or misleading. 

Fourth, the companys declaration that it will not make further changes or take further action regarding future disputes is itself troubling because it suggests it has predetermined the outcome of disputes regardless of new evidence. That is not a good-faith dispute investigation process. It is a blanket shutdown position. 

The company must now answer the following specific questions : 1. What exact records did it review before stating there was no evidence of repossession-related contact during bankruptcy?

2. Did that review include third-party repossession vendors, agents, contractors, dialer systems, outbound call logs, and assignment history?

3. Did it review whether any person or entity acting on its behalf contacted me or attempted to direct me regarding repossession while the bankruptcy case was active?

4. What updates, exactly, were furnished to each consumer reporting agency, on what dates, and with what status codes or bankruptcy/account condition codes?

5. If the account was updated to paid in full/closed with zero balance, why has the dispute process not produced a full written explanation with supporting furnishing details and documentary verification?

6. On what basis does the company claim the matter is fully resolved while refusing further action and failing to describe the scope of its investigation? 

Requested relief : I request that CFPB require Southeast Toyota Finance / World Omni Financial Corp. to : 1. Conduct a documented reinvestigation that includes all internal and third-party vendor records, including repossession-related assignments, communications, call logs, dialer history, and bankruptcy restriction logs. 
2. Produce a detailed written statement identifying every record category reviewed and every entity searched before making the no evidence claim.

3. Provide a complete Metro 2 or equivalent furnishing history showing exactly what was reported to each bureau, when it was reported, and what bankruptcy/account status codes were used.

4. Correct, delete, or clarify any inaccurate, misleading, or incomplete credit reporting associated with this account.

5. Explain in writing why it stated it would take no further action regarding future disputes, and whether that means it is refusing to consider new evidence.

6. Cease relying on conclusory statements that a matter is resolved where the actual investigation scope has not been disclosed.

This complaint is not resolved. The companys XX/XX/XXXX response is conclusory, incomplete, and evasive. It does not explain the investigation steps taken, does not identify the records reviewed, does not address third-party repossession-related activity adequately, and does not provide the detailed furnishing information necessary to test the accuracy of its reporting. The CFPB should require a substantive response rather than allowing the company to close the matter with unsupported assurances.

To Whom It May Concern, I am filing this formal complaint under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., regarding the inaccurate and misleading reporting of the following account. 

This account is being reported in a manner that is not consistent with the requirements set forth under federal law. The current reporting reflects a derogatory settlement accepted status despite the account having a XXXX balance and no ongoing obligation. This creates a misleading and damaging impression of my creditworthiness. 

Under FCRA 1681e ( b ), all information furnished to consumer reporting agencies must be accurate and reflect the maximum possible accuracy. The continued reporting of a settled account in a derogatory manner fails this requirement and presents an incomplete and unfair representation of the account. 

Additionally, pursuant to FCRA 1681s-2 ( a ), furnishers of information are required to provide accurate and complete information at all times. Reporting a paid and closed account with a negative designation, without properly reflecting its resolved status, is a violation of this obligation.

Furthermore, under FCRA 1681i, upon receipt of a dispute, there is a duty to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of the information being reported. If the information can not be verified as accurate, complete, and compliant with federal standards, it must be promptly deleted. 

Given these violations, I am formally demanding the immediate deletion of this account from all consumer reporting agencies. If deletion is not performed, then all derogatory language, including any reference to settlement accepted, must be removed and the account must be updated to reflect a neutral, non-damaging status. 

Failure to comply with these federal requirements will constitute a willful violation of the FCRA, and I am prepared to pursue all available remedies to protect my rights as a consumer. 

Please complete your investigation and provide confirmation of the deletion. 

Thank you

I am submitting this complaint regarding debt collection and credit furnishing activity by IQ Data XXXX related to a rental account originating from XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

Following move-out, I received charges supported primarily by vendor invoices rather than unit condition documentation. Property management indicated that no photographic documentation of the unit condition was available and could not confirm pet presence despite pet-related charges appearing on the account. 

The account was assigned to IQ Data and furnished to credit bureaus in XXXX of 2024. I disputed the account multiple times and requested validation. ( the " FCRA '' ), to formally dispute the credit reporting associated with the above-referenced account and to challenge the legal conclusions set forth in Cherry Technologies XXXX CFPB response dated on or about XX/XX/XXXX. Cherry 's response misapplies the law, relies on conclusory assertions in place of substantive analysis, and disregards multiple independent grounds upon which the credit reporting of this account is inaccurate, incomplete, and legally defective. This letter constitutes a final demand prior to litigation. 

I. CHERRY TECHNOLOGIES IS A FURNISHER SUBJECT TO 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) AND CAN NOT HIDE BEHIND ITS " SERVICER '' DESIGNATION Cherry Technologies characterizes itself as merely a " servicer and program administrator '' for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX This characterization does not insulate Cherry from direct FCRA liability as a furnisher of credit information. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), any entity that furnishes information to a consumer reporting agency -- regardless of whether it is the originating creditor -- bears independent legal obligations to investigate disputes and ensure the accuracy of reported information. 

See : XXXX v. XXXX & XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX Cir. XXXX ) ( holding that servicers and entities that furnish information to CRAs are subject to 1681s-2 ( b ) regardless of their role as originator or servicer ) ; SimmsParris v. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ) ( loan servicer qualifies as a furnisher under the FCRA and bears full investigatory obligations upon receipt of consumer dispute ). 

Cherry can not deflect responsibility to XXXX XXXX Bank. Both entities are co-obligors under the FCRA with respect to the accuracy of the information being reported. 

II. CHERRY 'S RESPONSE CONFIRMS A CHARGE-OFF -- WHICH ITSELF CREATES REPORTING OBLIGATIONS CHERRY IS VIOLATING Cherry confirms that this account was charged off on XX/XX/XXXX, with a net charge-off amount of {$2300.00}. Cherry then asserts that because no Form 1099-C was issued, the debt has not been cancelled and credit reporting may continue. This analysis is incomplete and legally flawed for the following reasons. 

A. The Charge-Off Must Be Reported Accurately and Completely A charge-off is not simply an " internal accounting classification, '' as Cherry characterizes it. Under the FCRA and Metro 2 credit reporting standards, when an account is charged off, specific data fields must be reported with precision : the charge-off date, the charge-off amount, the current balance ( if any ), and the account status code. Any inaccuracy in any one of these fields -- including misreporting the charge-off amount, the delinquency dates, or the account status -- constitutes a violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). 

See : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ) ( inaccurate reporting of charge-off status and account history gives rise to FCRA XXXX XXXX ) ; XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Bank XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ) ( furnisher liable where reported information, though technically accurate in isolation, creates a misleading impression of the consumer 's credit history ). 

B. A Charged-Off Account With a Zero Obligation Must Reflect That Status Cherry 's response acknowledges a net charge-off of {$2300.00} yet simultaneously states the debt remains outstanding. Cherry can not have it both ways. If the account has been charged off -- meaning Cherry and/or XXXX XXXX XXXX  has recognized the debt as uncollectible for accounting purposes -- the reporting of a continuing balance owed, combined with ongoing derogatory payment history notations, creates a materially misleading picture of the account status. The FCRA requires that credit reporting be not only technically accurate but also not misleading in context. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ) ( furnisher violated FCRA where reported information, while literally accurate, was incomplete and misleading ; accuracy requires both technical correctness and contextual completeness ) ; XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ) ( a report is " inaccurate '' under the FCRA if it is misleading in such a way and to such an extent that it can be expected to adversely affect credit decisions ). 

III. THE DELINQUENCY HISTORY CHERRY REPORTS IS DISPUTED AS INACCURATE Cherry 's response sets forth the following alleged delinquency timeline : 30 days late ( XX/XX/XXXX ), 60 days late ( XX/XX/XXXX ), 90 days late ( XX/XX/XXXX ), and charge-off ( XX/XX/XXXX ). I dispute this payment history in its entirety and demand that Cherry provide the following original account-level documentation to substantiate each data point : ( a ) Copies of monthly billing statements issued for each payment cycle from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX ; ( b ) Bank-level confirmation ( not servicer records ) of each payment received and each payment missed ; ( c ) Copies of any notices of delinquency or default sent to me at my address of record ; ( d ) Documentation confirming the date and amount of the XX/XX/XXXX payment Cherry acknowledges as the last successful payment. 

A furnisher 's own internal servicing records are not independently sufficient to verify disputed payment history. The FCRA requires that a furnisher review " all relevant information '' provided by the consumer and conduct a genuine investigation -- not merely confirm what its own system already shows. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX & XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX at XXXX ( " XXXX XXXX can not fulfill its 1681s-2 ( b ) obligations by simply reviewing the information it previously submitted to the CRA and confirming its accuracy. The investigation must go beyond the furnisher 's own records. " ) ; XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ) ( furnisher that reviewed only its own computer records without examining original loan documents did not conduct a reasonable investigation ). 

IV. THE ABSENCE OF A FORM 1099-C DOES NOT RESOLVE THE DISPUTE Cherry 's central argument -- that because no Form 1099-C was issued, reporting may continue unchanged -- is a non sequitur. Whether a 1099-C has been issued speaks to the tax treatment of cancelled debt under 26 U.S.C. 6050P. It says nothing about whether the credit reporting of this account is accurate under the FCRA. These are two entirely separate legal frameworks. 

The FCRA does not condition a consumer 's dispute rights on whether a 1099-C has been issued. The question under the FCRA is whether the reported information is accurate, complete, and not misleading. A charge-off combined with continued adverse payment history reporting can be inaccurate under the FCRA regardless of the tax treatment of the underlying debt.

Sadly, I learned over the next several months that nearly all the information given to me by XXXX XXXX to induce me into signing up for their program was false : # 1 ) I was told after 6 months in their program I could apply for their consolidation loan ; After spending 9 months in their program, they never made me an offer for such a loan - when I brought this to their attention, their response was : Oops, sorry you were told that, but that's not how it works here. 

# 2 ) I was told they would negotiate settlements with my creditors, but they did not. Over the course of 9 months I provided them with every correspondence I received from every creditor ( many of which asked me to contact them to discuss either alternative payment arrangements or even to discuss lowering my balances ) ; after 9 months in the program, Americor only communicated with 2 out of 14 listed creditors - and I learned this by contacting the actual creditors themselves, who told me no one from Americor had ever contacted them to discuss my account/debt with any of them # 3 ) Americor provides zero ability to contact, chat, communicate or email with their settlement negotiators who are working on your behalf. There is no way to verify what exactly is being communicated to my creditors, why they were not contacting 12 of my 14 creditors to even commence negotiations, or to learn how I could help them expedite their process. There is no way to actually communicate with their team responsible for executing the terms of their agreement with me. 

# 4 ) After having enough of their nonsense, on XX/XX/XXXX I cancelled their program. This required both an email notification AND a live phone conversation with one of their agents ( they make it extremely difficult to know exactly how to cancel ). Their agent repeatedly tried to convince me to remain in their program, but I was adamant and ultimately he agreed to let me cancel, sending me an email that as of XX/XX/XXXX I was cancelled from the program and they would refund me the existing balance in my trust account. On XX/XX/XXXX I received a call from XXXX at Americor who asked why I had not made my scheduled monthly deposit into my trust account ; I informed her I had cancelled and was waiting on the refund of my trust account balance. She acknowledged this and the call was ended.

We are submitting a complaint regarding the handling of a disputed account by Synchrony Bank related to a financed purchase of multiple home appliances from third-party retailer, XXXX XXXX . 

This matter involves a failed transaction ( wrong and defective goods delivered ), the merchants refusal to remedy, and serious concerns regarding Synchrony Banks investigation process and billing practices during an active dispute. 

In XX/XX/XXXX, I was guided by salesperson XXXX to purchase appliances over the phone from XXXX XXXX and finance them through a Synchrony Bank credit card account. The purchase was made through guided telephone sales assistance where I relied on representations made by the salesperson XXXX regarding product suitability and inventory availability. The purchase was not made independently through an online self-service process for example. 

I explained to XXXX that I was looking for specific models not available at XXXX XXXX, Lowes, or XXXX XXXX that were flush mount and had no visible vents. He claimed that the models I was looking for were in stock and available for immediate delivery. He then encouraged me to take advantage of the Synchrony Bank credit card financing option offering 15 months 0 % APR. I opened an account and paid for the XXXX order of {$8300.00} in full. 

Although the appliances were ordered in XX/XX/XXXX, they were not shipped until XX/XX/XXXX - through no fault of our own. XXXX XXXX repeatedly notified us about shipping delays, and refused to send one appliance at a time instead forcing the entire order to be delayed and delivered at the same date and time. Despite the delivery delays, monthly payments started several months before receiving the appliances. We had begun payment on damaged and wrong appliances months before we were able to approve them. 

Upon delivery, the process was rushed by the delivery personnel. They delivered four ( 4 ) large appliances within XXXX minutes ( please see delivery slip with notated delivery times from XXXXXXXX XXXXXXXX to XXXXXXXX XXXX attached as Exhibit 1 ) and did not allow any time for inspection. They simply said a signature was required as acknowledgement of delivery only. It was only later we discovered that : Two appliances were the wrong products ( a wrong model of XXXX dishwasher was delivered with a visible vent on the front panel which I did not approve and the wrong XXXX oven that did not fit flush to my kitchen cabinets like my previous XXXX model ) ; One appliance arrived damaged ( the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX ) ; and One appliance ( refrigerator ) had structural issues ( drawers did not function properly ) and subsequent cooling failure after a repair person damaged the internal structure. 

Only once the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX was opened and the other appliances installed were the issues discovered. Attempts were then made within 24 hours of delivery to return the damaged XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and within 1-2 days of delivery to return or resolve the issues with the remaining appliances. 

While XXXX XXXX accepted the return and refund of one damaged appliance ( the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ), the process was made unreasonably difficult requiring us to provide a wooden pallet and rope for return. We were also charged an exorbitant return fee despite XXXX XXXX stated 30 day return policy. 

Attached as Exhibit 2 is a series of email communications detailing the negotiation process between my husband and I with XXXX XXXX Customer Service Representative XXXX. The details of the emails are as follows : XXXX with XXXX XXXX initially wanted to charge us a return fee of {$750.00} ; We countered with a return fee of 10 % of our total XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( price {$2000.00} ) of {$200.00} ; XXXX then stated she would charge a return fee of {$390.00} as long as we provided a wooden pallet and rope for the return ; and XXXX ultimately charged us a return fee of {$270.00}, a fee much higher than the 10 % fee we were comfortable paying and was listed on the XXXX XXXX  invoice. 

Additionally, the consumers ( my husband and I ) are older individuals ( seniors ) who were expected to immediately unbox, inspect, maneuver, and potentially repackage multiple ( four ) large and heavy appliances within an extremely limited delivery window. Despite these practical limitations, we still acted promptly and successfully arranged the return of one of the items within 24 hours ( the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ), only to incur substantial return and restocking fees, and substantial negotiation delays. These circumstances further demonstrate the unreasonable nature of the merchants handling and return process as well as the bait and switch nature of this purchase. 

Upon installation of the XXXX refrigerator, we recognized right away that the drawers and shelves within the appliance were not able to slide properly on the tracks or be readjusted. 

Due to this, XXXX was notified and scheduled a series of repair appointments from a separate and independent repair company called XXXX XXXX XXXX . Many of the appointments were cancelled by XXXX XXXX XXXX resulting in measurable losses, including wage loss for time off work. 

During the repairs on the refrigerator, the following was determined : The drawers were confirmed to be defective, new drawers were ordered on many occasions - none of which fit or worked within this model of refrigerator ; Repair technician XXXX XXXX stated that because the drawers were defective, a new refrigerator would need to be ordered. He failed to do so. Instead ; On the last repair appointment, repair technician XXXX XXXX, in an attempt to provide a makeshift repair for the drawer tracks, removed the refrigerator backing, bent and repositioned the cooling/electrical coils, and cut out large amounts of insulation from the refrigerator. I have the insulation pieces that were cut out as well as the several extra drawers that were ordered and did not fit, and would be happy to provide pictures of them. XXXX XXXX DID NOT ask for approval from myself, my husband, or XXXX before materially changing the refrigerator from factory standards. 

As a result, the XXXX refrigerator drawers and shelves were never repaired and the refrigerator subsequently began experiencing cooling issues that had not previously existed. And XXXX XXXX and XXXX left us without repair or replacement while allowing the warranty to expire despite our consistent attempts at grievances. 
In emails back and forth with XXXX XXXX customer service representative XXXX, the damage done by the XXXX XXXX repair technician was completely disregarded. Please see Exhibit 12 of the certified mailed physical copy of our Formal Escalation for complete attachments including detailed emails, documentation of failed repair attempts, and no solution reached by XXXX XXXX or XXXX for the wrong and damaged goods they provided us. 

XXXX XXXX refused to accept returns for the remaining XXXX appliances and directed the matter to the manufacturer ( XXXX ) , resulting in multiple unsuccessful repair attempts. Despite extensive efforts ( including over 100 pages of documented email communications, service visits, and attempted repairs ), the issues were never resolved, and the warranty period expired without remedy.

An initial Formal Grievance was filed with Synchrony Bank on XX/XX/XXXX ( attached as Exhibit 3 ), which was ultimately denied. 

The first denial dated XX/XX/XXXX ( attached as Exhibit 4 ) appears to have been determined by an unidentifiable written statement attributed to XXXX XXXX that : Was unsigned ; Was not on company letterhead ; Was provided by an unknown individual that the consumer never interacted with ( XXXX XXXX ) ; Provided no contact information like a phone number or email ; and Omitted substantial portions of the documentation timelines and evidence.

Synchrony Bank did not appear to meaningfully consider the extensive documentation provided by the consumer, including photographs, service records, and email communications demonstrating good faith efforts to resolve the issue.

This raises serious concerns regarding the adequacy and fairness of the investigation.

After the denial of our Original Formal Grievance, we reopened the claim as instructed in the denial letter by submitting a Formal Escalation to Synchrony Bank, dated XX/XX/XXXX ( attached as Exhibit 5 - due to the CFPB portal submission limit, only the letter is attached to the online submission. A complete copy with all attachments has been sent to the CFPB in a physical certified mail copy ). 

On XX/XX/XXXX, Synchrony Bank received the Formal Escalation ( dated XX/XX/XXXX ) confirmed via USPS delivery tracking attached as Exhibit 6. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, Synchrony issued a written acknowledgment ( attached as Exhibit 7 ) stating : The dispute was under active review ; and Interest charges would NOT accrue on the disputed charges during the investigation. 

Additionally, on XX/XX/XXXX, we received a voicemail confirming receipt of Formal Escalation ( attached as Exhibit 8 ). 

However, on XX/XX/XXXX, I received my XX/XX/XXXX statement ( attached as Exhibit 9 ) which shows that - while the dispute remained open and unresolved - Synchrony Bank : Assessed {$2000.00} in deferred interest ; and Issued a statement treating the full balance as due.

This directly contradicts Synchronys written representation that interest would not accrue during the review process. 

The assessment of interest during an active investigation materially prejudices the consumer by inflating the disputed balance before the dispute has been resolved. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, we received a second denial letter from Synchrony Bank ( attached as Exhibit 11 ). The reason provided is simply Synchrony is unable to validate that there was a quality defect. This reason is materially implausible. 

Synchrony Bank, XXXX and XXXX XXXX have been passing the blame between each entity. No single entity will comply with appropriate investigative and resolution practices. As a result, XXXX has allowed the manufacturers warranty on the appliances to run out by the expiration date of XX/XX/XXXX. Despite submitting by certified mail Formal Grievances and Formal Escalations to each entity, no resolution has been reached- this account has remained in continuous active dispute since the appliances have been delivered.

My husband and I, the consumers, have made substantial efforts to accommodate service scheduling, troubleshooting, and repair access, yet the matter ultimately has remained unresolved. The prolonged insufficient handling of the matter and repeated unsuccessful repair attempts raise serious concerns regarding lack of meaningful warranty remedies provided by XXXX ( and XXXX XXXX  ), consistent with obligations under the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

Despite submission of substantial additional documentation during the second Formal Escalation - including extensive written communications, documentation of repeated failed repair attempts, and evidence that one damaged appliance was successfully returned- the second denial issued by Synchrony Bank relied on the same unsupported merchant narrative previously used in the first denial. No new investigation was performed and Synchrony Bank did not meaningfully address or reconcile the substantial evidence provided by us, the consumers. 

XXXX XXXX has implied that they have a 30-Day Return Policy, when they do not. They actually are operating under an All Sales Final policy without informing their customers. Salesperson XXXX never informed me during my guided phone purchase that damaged appliances could not be returned however in the unsigned, non-letterhead written statement attributed to a purported XXXX XXXX representative XXXX XXXX that was supplied as evidence for denial from Synchrony Bank states that XXXX XXXX XXXX does not return installed appliances. This statement was never disclosed prior to purchase and would have caused me to not purchase appliance through XXXX XXXX had I been informed. 

Instead, large appliance retailers like XXXX XXXX provide free, 30-day returns. Why would anyone purchase from XXXX XXXX when they operate under an all sales final approach and do not disclose it to customers? 

Lastly, XXXX XXXX has relinquished any responsibility associated with the wrong and damaged appliances sold to us under an undisclosed all sales final policy. Instead, theyve shifted all responsibility to the manufacturer XXXX . Despite this, Synchrony Bank has failed to properly implicate XXXX in its investigations and simply claims there is no evidence of quality defect when the evidence is abundant - detailed documentation of which have been provided by certified mail to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, and Synchrony Bank. 

This case reflects not only a failed transaction but also a breakdown in dispute handling and billing practices. The consumers made extensive good faith efforts to resolve the issue, yet have been left with defective goods and a significantly inflated balance during an unresolved dispute.

Again, this account has remained in continuous dispute since the appliances have been delivered.

Accordingly, we respectfully request that the CFPB requires Synchrony Bank to : Remove all interest charges assessed during the dispute period, including the full {$2000.00} charge ; Fully refund the charge incurred of all appliances, including exorbitant shipping fees, associated with returning the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to XXXX XXXX ; Fully refund the installation costs for installing wrong and/or damaged appliances ( totaling {$670.00}. Invoices attached as Exhibit 10 ) ; Reimbursement of financial losses for a total of {$1400.00} incurred while awaiting unreliable delivery and repair appointments ( XXXX XXXXXXXX 7 Days ) ( please see EXTENSIVE details regarding the repeated delivery and repair cancellations and reschedules caused solely by XXXX XXXX on Exhibit 12 ) ; Reimbursement of {$60.00} for the wooden pallet and rope requested by XXXX XXXX for the return of the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( please see EXTENSIVE details regarding XXXX XXXX  absurd return practices and financial losses caused by them in Exhibit 12 ) ; and Written confirmation ( not verbal ) that no negative credit reporting or adverse impact to my credit score has occurred or will occur as a result of this grievance or any other billing dispute pursuant to applicable California law .

In support of the details herein, attached please find the following : Exhibit 1 : Updike Delivery Slip ; Exhibit 2 : Series of email communications detailing the return fee negotiation process between consumers and XXXX XXXX Customer service Representative XXXX for the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ; Exhibit 3 : Formal Grievance to Synchrony Bank dated XX/XX/XXXX ; Exhibit 4 : First Synchrony Bank Denial dated XX/XX/XXXX ; Exhibit 5 : Formal Escalation to Synchrony Bank dated XX/XX/XXXX ; Exhibit 6 : USPS Delivery Confirmation of Formal Grievance dated XX/XX/XXXX : Exhibit 7 : XX/XX/XXXX letter from Synchrony Bank acknowledging receipt of Formal Escalation and confirming that interest charges would not occur during the investigation period ; Exhibit 8 : Transcription of XX/XX/XXXX voicemail from Synchrony Bank confirming receipt of Formal Escalation ; Exhibit 9 : Synchrony BankXXXX XXXX Account Statement displaying a {$2000.00} interest charge despite Synchrony confirming interest would not be charged during an open investigation period ; Exhibit 10 : Two ( 2 ) receipts detailing the installation costs associated with the installation of wrong and/or damaged appliances - one {$320.00} installation fee and another fee for {$350.00} totaling {$670.00} ; Exhibit 11 : Second Synchrony Bank Denial dated XX/XX/XXXX ; and Exhibit 12 : Complete Formal Escalation package dated XX/XX/XXXX ( Due to the CFPB portal submission limit, only the letter is attached to the online submission. During a foreclosure mediation on XX/XX/year>, I participated by phone without legal representation due to my personal circumstances, including my son being XXXX  at the time. Although the mediation concluded without a formal written resolution, specific reinstatement options and approximate payoff figures were clearly discussed during that session. 

Following the mediation, I was instructed to work with a Single Point of Contact ( SPOC ) to finalize the exact reinstatement amount and proceed with payment. I made multiple attempts to contact the assigned SPOC by phone and email to obtain a detailed written breakdown of the reinstatement amount, including all fees and charges.

Although I was verbally provided with a payoff figure, I specifically requested a written itemization to verify the accuracy of the amount before submitting payment. Given the size of the amount, this request was both reasonable and necessary. I was prepared and willing to pay the required amount by XX/XX/year>, but I could not responsibly proceed without confirmation and documentation of the figures. 

Despite my repeated efforts, the SPOC failed to provide the requested written breakdown or respond in a timely and meaningful manner. Instead of providing the requested documentation, the servicer escalated the matter and instructed their attorney to move forward with foreclosure proceedings while my request for clarification remained outstanding. 

I have also been informed that the servicer is taking the position that, because there was no formal written agreement resulting from the mediation, the discussions and figures presented during the mediation can not be relied upon. However, I do not agree with this position, particularly since the servicers attorney has referenced and relied upon information discussed during that same mediation. 

When I was finally able to speak with the SPOC in XX/XX/year>, I was quoted a reinstatement amount that was significantly higher than the approximate figures discussed during mediation. This increase was substantial and unexpected. I believe this inflated amount is a direct result of delays, added fees, and the servicers failure to provide timely communication when I was actively attempting to resolve the matter. 

As a result, I am requesting the opportunity to reinstate my loan based on the approximate amount that was quoted during the XX/XX/year>XXXX  mediation, rather than the significantly increased amount that I was later quoted after the servicer failed to respond to my requests. 

As a result of the servicers failure to communicate and provide required information, I was deprived of a fair and reasonable opportunity to reinstate my loan and avoid foreclosure. I believe this reflects a serious breakdown in servicing obligations and may constitute unfair or deceptive practices.

Additional Concern : This is my third complaint submitted regarding this same matter. In my prior complaints, the servicers responses did not resolve the core issue, which remains their failure to provide a clear, written breakdown of the reinstatement amount in a timely manner despite my repeated requests and readiness to pay. 

I am concerned that my previous complaints may have been closed based solely on the servicer providing a response, rather than actually resolving the issue. The underlying problem remains unresolved and has now resulted in continued foreclosure activity.

I respectfully request that this complaint be escalated for further review and not closed without a thorough evaluation of the servicers actions and their direct impact on my ability to reinstate my loan. 

I have attached email correspondence from the lenders attorney sharing they are moving forward with foreclosure and I have attached a document from the lender showing they need time to provide me with my request. Both documents are dated the same date. XX/XX/year>XXXX  I made every effort in good faith to resolve this matter and had the financial ability to do so by the XX/XX/year>XXXX  deadline. The servicers lack of responsiveness directly prevented me from completing the reinstatement process.

This discrepancy is preventing my loan discharge and appears to be the result of a failure to properly apply IDR adjustment payment counts across repayment plans. 

This is not an eligibility issue. It is a processing failure between the Department of Education and my loan servicer. 

Despite multiple inquiries, I have been told only to wait, while interest continues to accrue and my account remains in limbo. 

-- - Requested Resolution : I am requesting : 1. Immediate review of my account at the Department of Education level 2. Correction and alignment of qualifying payment counts across all IDR plans 3. Removal or correction of any adverse account status resulting from this delay -- - Additional Information : I have attached documentation confirming : * Servicer acknowledgment of eligibility for IDR forgiveness * Federal Student Aid data showing over 300 qualifying payments * Ongoing discrepancy in qualifying payment counts under my current plan This issue reflects a systemic processing failure and requires escalation beyond standard customer service channels.

text:
I. Statement of Facts On XX/XX/year>, I filed a dispute regarding unauthorized electronic fund transfers associated with my Crypto.com prepaid debit card. 

On XX/XX/year>, Foris DAX, Inc. issued written notice that my account had been provisionally credited for disputed amounts. The written notice explicitly stated : These temporary credits are being provided while we investigate your claim You will have full use of these funds while we complete our investigation. 

Subsequently, my virtual card was restricted. I was informed via chat support that : A routine review had been performed. 
I would no longer be able to perform card purchases or apply for a new card. 
The restriction applied to card functionality. 
I must wait until the investigation is completed. 
The matter had been escalated internally. 
No written explanation was provided specifying the legal or contractual basis for the restriction. 

As a result of this restriction : I can not use my card for purchases. 
I can not apply for a replacement card. 
I can not access the provisionally credited funds through the only instrument authorized for such access. 
I was unable to use my funds during an emergency. 

The company has provided provisional credit but has simultaneously XXXX access to the only mechanism by which the funds may be used.

II. Regulatory Framework Implicated A. Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) 15 U.S.C. 1693f The EFTA requires that when a consumer reports an unauthorized electronic fund transfer, the financial institution must : 1. Conduct a good faith investigation ; 2. Provisionally credit the consumers account within 10 business days if the investigation can not be completed ; 3. Permit the consumer to use the funds during the investigation.

Denying practical access to provisionally credited funds undermines the statutory purpose of the provisional credit requirement.

B. Regulation E 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ) ( 2 ) ( i ) When provisional credit is provided, the financial institution must : Provisionally credit the consumers account for the amount of the alleged error, including interest where applicable. 

Official Interpretations clarify that provisional credit must allow the consumer meaningful access to the funds pending investigation. 

Issuing provisional credit while simultaneously disabling card functionality prevents meaningful access and defeats the purpose of provisional credit protections.

C. Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ) 12 U.S.C. 5531 Unfair Acts or Practices An act or practice is unfair if it : 1. Causes or is likely to cause substantial injury ; 2. The injury is not reasonably avoidable ; and 3. The injury is not outweighed by countervailing benefits.

Providing provisional credit while freezing the instrument required to access those funds : Causes substantial financial injury, Is not reasonably avoidable by the consumer, Provides no apparent countervailing consumer benefit, Particularly where the institution has expressly represented in writing that the consumer will have full use of the funds.

D. Potential Adverse Action / Account Restriction Concerns The company has restricted card privileges without providing : A written explanation of the specific basis for restriction, Notice of adverse action, if applicable, Clear disclosure of whether this restriction is tied to fraud review, compliance review, or dispute activity.

The lack of transparency raises additional compliance concerns.

III. Core Compliance Issue The central issue is this : Foris DAX , Inc. explicitly stated in writing that I would have full use of provisionally credited funds during the investigation. 

However, they simultaneously restricted card functionality and prevented access to those funds. 
This action renders the provisional credit functionally inaccessible and inconsistent with the protections provided under Regulation E and the Electronic Fund Transfer Act.

IV. Harm Experienced Inability to access funds during an emergency Financial hardship due to inability to use credited funds Lack of clear written explanation Ongoing uncertainty regarding access to funds
label: Prepaid card

text:
I am filing this complaint regarding PayPals continued restriction of my account and withholding of funds in a manner that appears inconsistent with its own User Agreement and stated policies. 

At the time of restriction, my account reflected approximately {$18000.00} in my PayPal personal balance and approximately {$9300.00} in PayPal Savings. Currently, my PayPal balance reflects {$16000.00}, with {$9300.00} still held in PayPal Savings.

These funds include legitimate income, including proceeds originating from an IRS tax refund. 

In early XX/XX/year>, I received multiple payments from a single sender over a short period of time. Beginning in XX/XX/year>, multiple disputes and chargebacks were initiated, all tied to this same sender. The total dispute exposure is estimated to be in the range of approximately {$3000.00} to {$3500.00}. 

Despite this, PayPal applied a blanket restriction across my entire account and all funds.

According to PayPals User Agreement, limitations and reserves may be applied to protect PayPal and the network and may be based on anticipated risk or liability. The agreement also indicates that funds not subject to restriction or reserve should remain available for withdrawal. 

However, in my case : - The identified risk is limited to a defined set of transactions tied to a single sender - The total exposure is approximately {$3000.00} to {$3500.00} - PayPal is currently withholding over {$16000.00} in PayPal balance, in addition to {$9300.00} in PayPal Savings This appears disproportionate to any reasonable or anticipated liability.

Additionally, PayPals agreement references the use of funds as a reserve or security for potential liabilities. However, the amount currently being withheld significantly
exceeds any known or reasonably anticipated chargeback exposure.

If PayPal is relying on a risk-based or protective justification, I request a clear explanation of how holding funds far exceeding the actual dispute amount is necessary to protect PayPal or its network.

Furthermore, PayPal has not provided : - A transaction-level explanation of the restriction - An itemized breakdown of disputed transactions- Clear identification of which funds are considered restricted versus unrestricted Without this transparency, it is not possible to determine whether PayPal is applying its policies in a reasonable and consistent manner.

Additionally, the pattern of disputes originating from a single sender within a defined timeframe suggests potential unauthorized use or abuse of the dispute system. Under a reasonable risk-based framework, this should have triggered a targeted fraud investigation into the source of the transactions, rather than a blanket restriction of unrelated funds.

PayPal performs functions similar to a financial institution, including holding customer funds, accepting direct deposits, and receiving tax refunds. As such, it should be held to reasonable standards of fairness, proportionality, and transparency in how it applies restrictions to customer funds.

Based on the above, PayPals actions appear : - Disproportionate relative to the identified risk - Inconsistent with its stated purpose of applying limitations for protection - Lacking sufficient transparency and justification I am requesting : 1. Immediate release of all funds not directly tied to disputed transactions 2. A complete itemized breakdown of all disputed transactions and associated amounts 3. A clear written explanation of the basis for any continued restriction 4. Clarification of how PayPal determined the amount of funds being held as a reserve 5. Review and removal of any improper dispute-related fees

text:
I am submitting this complaint regarding a timeshare purchase I made after a sales presentation conducted by representatives of XXXX including inducement into a loan I didnt realize I was taking. The sale involved high-pressure tactics, misleading statements about the cost and benefits of the program, and a lack of clear disclosure about the financing and my cancellation rights. 

On XX/XX/year>, my fianc and I traveled to New York City to see the XXXX XXXX as a XXXX gift from my mother. We stayed at XXXX that evening. While sitting in the bar that night, an individual approached our table and casually started a conversation. He asked if we would be interested in hearing about easier vacation options and offered a free cruise incentive if we attended a presentation. We agreed to attend a meeting the following day. 

On XX/XX/year>, we took an XXXX to a separate location for the timeshare presentation. When we arrived, we rang a doorbell and were admitted by a man who asked for our identification and the pamphlet we had received the night before. We were given name tags and taken up an elevator where we were checked in again and placed in a waiting room with several other couples. I believe we received a cruise voucher at that time. 

We were then moved to another room where they played a video that was very emotional and focused on the importance of family vacations. During the video, man spoke about how he had immigrated from another country and how owning a XXXX timeshare allowed him to spend meaningful time with his family. 

After the video, we were introduced to a person named XXXX who us on a tour across XXXX XXXX to a hotel that she said was used exclusively by XXXX timeshare members. During the tour she asked about our employment, our financial situation, and how we typically vacation. While we were touring the property, we encountered an older couple in the elevator who told us that they loved their timeshare. This interaction appeared to reinforce the positive message about the program. 

After the tour we returned to the original building where XXXX began discussing different packages and the XXXX points system. She explained that points could be used for vacations and flights with major airlines. At that point, a XXXX named XXXX began hovering near the conversation and eventually took over the presentation. 

XXXX began presenting multiple pricing options and repeatedly stated that the numbers looked good. The explanation of the points system was confusing and involved a large amount of information presented very quickly. XXXX said that the points could be used for travel anywhere and even for first-class airline tickets. He also said that we could use the program whenever we wanted and that booking would generally only require a few weeks or months of advance notice. 

We told XXXX several times that we needed time to think about the decision. At that point another woman entered the room and talked about how much she loved the program. She told a story about a friend who had died and how she was able to immediately book travel to attend the funeral because she owned the XXXX program. 

XXXX then returned and continued presenting numbers. He told us that the package he was offering had originally been purchased by another family for approximately {$120000.00} but that XXXX had taken it back and would sell it to us that day for {$60000.00}. He emphasized that this was a special opportunity available only that day. We were also offered other benefits that were only available on a first visit. 

XXXX asked about our typical vacation habits and stated that based on our travel patterns we would likely spend approximately {$60000.00} on vacations over the next XXXX years. He said that if we purchased the timeshare we would essentially be investing that same amount into XXXX and, after the loan was paid off, we would only need to pay the monthly maintenance fee. He specifically represented that the maintenance fee, which he said was approximately {$300.00} per month, would be locked in and would not increase. 

At no point during the sales discussion was it clearly explained that the true cost of the purchase would exceed {$110000.00} when interest and a separate loan was included. They also gave me a credit card I didnt ask for. I have also found out that the maintenance fee will absolutely increase. 

XXXX initially asked us to provide a {$15000.00} deposit. When we said that we could not afford that amount, he lowered the deposit to {$10000.00} and stated that we did not need to pay it that day. This is where XXXX came in. We did not fully understand at that time that a separate loan was being created for this deposit. Although both me and my fianc are on the XXXX contract, only I was made responsible for the loan and I subsequently found out that the interest rate is 34.49 %. 

The sales process continued for approximately XXXX and a half hours. We repeatedly expressed hesitation and said that the purchase did not seem right for us, but the representatives continued to present new numbers, incentives, and assurances. We didnt feel like we could leave and eventually we felt worn down and agreed. 

We were then taken to another room with a different representative who had a computer displaying electronic documents. He rapidly scrolled through multiple pages and directed us to sign in several places. The documents were not carefully explained and were moving very quickly on the screen. We were simply told where to sign. 

At no time during this process were we informed that we had the right to cancel the contract within XXXX business days. 

After the signing process concluded, printed copies of some documents were provided to us. Later that evening, XXXX left a voicemail message for me stating that she was checking to make sure we arrived home safely and that she was entering our names in a drawing for a free trip. 

The following day we began to feel that we XXXX have made a mistake. We were embarrassed and initially did not tell my mother about the purchase. When we eventually did tell her, she contacted XXXX on our behalf to inquire about canceling the contract. At that point we were told that the rescission period had expired XXXX days before and they just kept saying that the contract would not be canceled. 

After my mother reviewed the documents more carefully, we realized that the financial obligations were far greater than explained during the presentation and that a separate loan had been created for the deposit. We also learned that we had agreed to receive hundreds of pages of documents related to the timeshare structure and multiple programs ( with extra fees ) offered by XXXX. They were supposedly sent via XXXX. I had no idea that I was receiving additional documents via XXXX. 

We believe this sale involved misleading statements about the cost of the program, the nature of the financing, and the stability of the maintenance fees. We also believe the presentation relied heavily on pressure tactics designed to wear down potential buyers during a long meeting. We did not feel like we could just get up and leave, and there was no way to exit. 

XXXX and the lender it services XXXX DR Bank, are a fundamental part of the sales process. By pushing the loan, XXXX gets thousands of dollars upfront and if the customer later objects to the sale process, the customer is left to deal with a third party servicer/lender that claims to have no part in the timeshare sale. This is also part of the scam. I am disputing the validity of the timeshare contract and the loan that would not exist but for the unfair and deceptive sales practices.

As of today, XX/XX/XXXX, I have not heard from them. I also have not heard XXXX DR Bank.
