A blanket " determined to be incomplete '' does not satisfy that requirement. 

Most significantly, the XX/XX/XXXX letter contains a written admission by Onity that it conducts the very dual-track servicing prohibited by Regulation XXXX Onity XXXX XXXX XXXX : " With respect to account servicing and credit reporting, even when an account is under consideration for loss mitigation or enrolled in a trial or forbearance plan, servicing continues in accordance with the terms of the Note. Both positions conflict with 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( f ) and ( g ), which prohibit the servicer from making the first notice or filing for any judicial or non-judicial foreclosure process, or from moving for foreclosure judgment or order of sale, while a complete loss mitigation application is pending for evaluation. 

The XX/XX/XXXX letter also confirmed that Onity will continue reporting me as delinquent to XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX, stating, " we are unable to remove valid past due reporting. '' It is not accurate to report this account as standard delinquent. I have been in an approved Temporary Hardship Forbearance Plan since XX/XX/XXXX, and I have had a loss mitigation application on file and under review for the entire period. Reporting a borrower in approved forbearance as standard delinquent, while a complete loss mitigation application is pending, violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, and CFPB furnisher-accuracy guidance. This complaint constitutes a formal dispute of the inaccurate furnished information under the FCRA. 

I am also actively working to sell the property. It is currently listed for sale at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX with XXXX XXXX of XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ). text:
FORMAL CFPB COMPLAINT REGULATION CC VIOLATIONS, FAILURE TO ACCOUNT FOR FUNDS, MISREPRESENTATION, AND ARBITRARY ACCOUNT CLOSURE I am submitting this complaint against Bank of America for multiple violations involving improper funds handling, failure to provide required disclosures, contradictory transaction reporting, and arbitrary account closure following my attempts to obtain lawful information. 

I. MATERIAL FACTS AND DOCUMENTED EVIDENCE On XX/XX/year>, I deposited XXXX checks in the amount of {$6000.00} each into my checking account. At the time of deposit, I was explicitly informed that no hold would be placed. This representation was relied upon and materially influenced my decision to proceed with the transaction. 

Later that same day, holds were applied retroactively and inconsistently, accompanied only by vague explanations including pending funds verification and refer to maker. At no point was I provided with a specific, factual basis identifying any defect, insufficiency, alteration, or fraud indicator associated with the checks. 

I independently confirmed with XXXX XXXX, the paying bank, that the funds were debited and the checks cleared without issue. This was further verified directly with the maker of the checks, whose account was charged the same day the checks were issued. I possess documentary evidence, including screenshots, confirming that the funds were available, debited, and not subject to return for insufficient funds or stop payment. 

Despite this, Bank of America later asserted that the checks were returned unpaid with a Refer to Maker designation. However, no documentary evidence has been provided to support this claim, including : No return transaction record No interbank return trace No return settlement confirmation No evidence that funds were transmitted back to the issuing bank This creates a direct contradiction between financial institutions and establishes a failure by Bank of America to properly account for the disposition of deposited funds.

II. REGULATION CC VIOLATIONS Under Regulation CC 229.13 ( e ), a bank may invoke an exception hold only where it has reasonable cause to believe a check is uncollectible, and such determination must be based on specific, articulable facts.

Bank of America failed to provide any such facts.

Further, 229.13 ( g ) requires that when an exception hold is applied, the bank must provide a clear and specific statement of the reason for the delay, sufficient to allow the customer to understand the basis for the action taken.

Statements such as pending verification and refer to maker are conclusory and do not meet the specificity requirement mandated by regulation.

Additionally, 229.16 ( c ) requires that disclosures be clear, conspicuous, and meaningful. The explanations provided were vague, non-informative, and prevented any meaningful understanding or verification of the banks actions.

III. FAILURE TO ACCOUNT FOR FUNDS / TRANSACTION DISCREPANCY Bank of America has asserted that the checks were returned unpaid while the issuing bank has confirmed no such return occurred. This contradiction, combined with the absence of any trace documentation, establishes a failure to properly reconcile or account for the funds.

A banks obligation is not satisfied by assertion alone. It must be supported by verifiable transaction records. The failure to produce such documentation raises serious concerns regarding internal controls, reconciliation accuracy, and the handling of customer deposits.

IV. MISREPRESENTATION AND UNFAIR PRACTICES At the time of deposit, I was informed that no hold would be placed. This statement was later contradicted by subsequent actions. This constitutes a material misrepresentation.

Further, the use of vague, non-specific explanations, combined with contradictory statements regarding the status of the funds, constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice that prevented me from understanding or protecting my financial position.

V. DENIAL OF INFORMATION AND OBSTRUCTION During multiple attempts to resolve this matter : Representatives refused to provide specific information Stated no additional details were available Refused escalation to a supervisor Terminated calls when escalation was requested Refused to provide identifying information This conduct interfered with my ability to obtain information regarding my funds and demonstrates a failure to provide reasonable access to account-related information.

VI. ARBITRARY AND POTENTIALLY RETALIATORY ACCOUNT CLOSURE Following my repeated attempts to obtain information and escalate the issue, my account was closed with the sole explanation that my account activity put the bank at risk, with no factual basis provided.

While banks may close accounts, the timing and circumstances of this closureimmediately following my efforts to question and escalateraise serious concerns that the action was arbitrary and potentially retaliatory in nature.

The refusal to provide any explanation further compounds concerns regarding transparency and fairness. 

VII. DISPARATE AND UNPROFESSIONAL TREATMENT On XX/XX/year>, at a branch in XXXXXXXX XXXX, I was treated in a dismissive and demeaning manner by a branch manager who explicitly stated she did not have to answer my questions. During the same visit, I observed other customers receiving polite and cooperative assistance. 

Additionally, during a subsequent call, a representative identified as XXXX refused to provide identification, laughed when I requested escalation, and terminated the call. 

This pattern reflects inconsistent treatment and a failure to uphold professional standards. 

VIII. DEMAND FOR REGULATORY ACTION Based on the foregoing, I am requesting : Immediate investigation into the handling and disposition of my deposited funds Production of all transaction records, including any alleged return documentation A formal check trace and reconciliation review Determination of compliance with Regulation CC Review of internal controls and decisioning processes Correction of any inaccurate reporting or account records Accountability for failure to provide required disclosures CONCLUSION This matter involves more than a routine deposit dispute. It reflects a systemic failure to provide required disclosures, properly account for funds, and maintain transparency in customer transactions. 

The inability to reconcile contradictory statements between banks, combined with the absence of documentary proof and the refusal to provide information, raises serious concerns that warrant immediate regulatory intervention. 

I respectfully request that this matter be reviewed with urgency and that corrective action be taken.

text:
Complaint Narrative TransUnion Product : Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports Issue : Incorrect information on credit report Sub-issue : Account age / length of credit history I am submitting this complaint regarding TransUnions inaccurate and inconsistent reporting of credit aging metrics, including Average Age of Accounts and Oldest Account Age, in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ). 
Summary of the issue TransUnion is reporting credit age figures that materially differ from those reported by other national consumer reporting agencies ( including Experian and Equifax ), despite all agencies drawing from the same underlying credit history. These discrepancies demonstrate that TransUnion is either : Including accounts that should not be included in aging calculations, Excluding accounts that should be included, or Relying on inaccurate or unverified date opened data furnished by one or more data providers.

Credit age is a mathematical derivative of fixed historical account dates. It is not subjective. Different aging outcomes across bureaus indicate that TransUnions procedures are not ensuring accuracy. 
FCRA violations implicated This conduct implicates, at minimum : 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) Failure to conduct a lawful reinvestigation of disputed information 15 U.S.C. 1681g ( a ) Failure to clearly and accurately disclose information used in credit scoring factors When credit aging metrics differ across agencies, at least one bureau must be reporting inaccurately. Continued publication of internally inconsistent aging data constitutes misleading credit reporting.

Harm caused This inaccurate credit aging information has caused and continues to cause : Artificial suppression of credit scores Increased perceived credit risk unrelated to actual payment performance Adverse impact on lending, housing, and credit access decisions Because credit age is a high-impact scoring factor, even small inaccuracies cause outsized harm. 

Requested resolution I am requesting that TransUnion : Conduct a documented reinvestigation of all account date opened data used in its credit aging calculations ; Remove or exclude any account data that can not be verified with complete and consistent historical records ; and Correct or suppress credit aging metrics that can not be calculated with maximum possible accuracy. 
If TransUnion can not ensure accurate and consistent credit age calculations, continued reporting of those metrics should cease. 
Supporting documentation demonstrating discrepancies across consumer reporting agencies.
label: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports

text:
XX/XX/XXXX Subject : CFPB Complaint ID : XXXX, XXXX Wells Fargo Case Number : XXXX CFPB Complaint Update Concerns Regarding Wells Fargo Safe Deposit Box Investigation Process , Repeated Case Closures, Claimed Authorization Issue, and Credit Card Cancellation Dear CFPB Representative , We respectfully submit this update regarding our ongoing complaint involving missing contents from my XXXX mothers Wells Fargo safe deposit box. 

Our family remains deeply concerned that Wells Fargo has not provided a meaningful, transparent, or independent review of this matter. Instead, Wells Fargo appears to have repeatedly closed or limited complaint reviews, issued boilerplate responses, and redirected responsibility back to the same XXXX branch involved in the events. 

The missing contents were discovered on XX/XX/XXXX, shortly after a visit to the Wells Fargo XXXX branch to retrieve valuables from the safe deposit box. The matter was reported to the XXXX branch the same day, and a police report was promptly filed. Since then, our family has submitted extensive documentation, including inventories, affidavits, photographs, receipts, serial numbers, Power of Attorney documents, and supporting explanations. 

One of our major concerns is Wells Fargos repeated position that it did not have permission to share information with the CFPB. My Power of Attorney authorizes me to handle my mothers financial matters and communicate with Wells Fargo on her behalf. In addition, our family filed complaints with the CFPB specifically to request the involvement of the government agency responsible for oversight of consumer financial matters involving banks. 

We understand that Wells Fargo may have internal requirements for authorization. However, Wells Fargo has not clearly identified what specific separate form, signature, or authorization it claims is missing. Instead, the banks repeated closure or limitation of complaint reviews on this basis has the effect of preventing the CFPB from obtaining meaningful information, while leaving our family without substantive answers. 

We respectfully ask the CFPB to require Wells Fargo to clearly identify any specific authorization it claims is needed, rather than allowing Wells Fargo to rely on a vague no permission explanation while avoiding a substantive response. 

Our concern is that Wells Fargos handling has not addressed the substance of the complaint. Specifically : 1. Wells Fargo has repeatedly closed or limited complaint reviews while stating that it did not have permission to share information with the CFPB ; 2. Our family has submitted Power of Attorney documents and has attempted to cooperate fully ; 3. Our family filed CFPB complaints to request government oversight and involvement ; 4. Wells Fargo has not clearly identified what exact additional document, form, or signature is supposedly needed ; 5. The repeated closures have the effect of preventing the CFPB from obtaining information from Wells Fargo ; 6. Wells Fargo continues to direct safe deposit box questions back to the Houston XXXX XXXX, while the branch has not provided any investigation updates to our family. 

We are also concerned that the investigation does not appear sufficiently independent. The alleged loss occurred in connection with a safe deposit box at the branch, yet Wells Fargo continues to indicate that the branch is handling the claim directly. We respectfully believe that a matter involving alleged missing contents from a bank-controlled safe deposit environment should receive independent review by personnel or departments outside the branch directly involved. 

Another serious concern is Wells Fargos slow and incomplete cooperation with law enforcement. The branch provided safe deposit box vault entry records to our family and the police but has not provided any surveillance videos and names of the staff members who assisted us with vault access during relevant visits. Wells Fargo should have records identifying which employees serviced customers at the vault. In a police investigation involving alleged missing safe deposit box contents, those records are highly relevant. 

In addition to the safe deposit box matter, Wells Fargo later cancelled my mothers credit card. The cancellation letter listed reasons that appear inconsistent with my mothers actual financial and payment history. My mother had an excellent credit score at the time of card cancellation ; she also has sufficient equity, income, and savings to pay her debts. She has always paid on time. Her monthly payments on her Wells Fargo credit cards were many times above the minimum payment, if not paid in full. The particular Wells Fargo credit card that was cancelled reportedly carried no balance since XX/XX/XXXX. Therefore, Wells Fargos statement that her payments were too low relative to the Wells Fargo balance appears unreasonable and troubling. 

We understand Wells Fargo may deny that the credit card cancellation had any connection to the safe deposit box dispute, police report, or CFPB complaint. However, the timing of the cancellation, during an unresolved safe deposit box investigation and active complaint process, creates a reasonable concern of possible adverse treatment after my mothers family raised serious concerns against Wells Fargo. We are not claiming proof of retaliation at this time, but we respectfully believe the timing and circumstances should be reviewed carefully and independently. 

The credit card cancellation significantly affected my mothers credit profile and added additional emotional distress during an already difficult unresolved dispute with Wells Fargo. 

Our concerns are not limited solely to my mothers financial loss. This matter raises broader consumer protection concerns for elderly and vulnerable customers, including senior XXXX customers who may face language or cultural barriers and may not know how to defend themselves when valuables go missing from a safe deposit box they believed was protected by a major financial institution. 

We respectfully request that the CFPB ask Wells Fargo to : 1. Explain why the complaint has been repeatedly closed or limited without meaningful findings ; 2. Identify exactly what authorization Wells Fargo claims is missing, if any, for communication with the CFPB ; 3. Confirm whether an independent department outside the branch is reviewing the safe deposit box matter ; 4. Preserve all relevant records, vault access logs, surveillance materials, employee handling records, and safe deposit procedures ; 5. Cooperate fully and promptly with law enforcement, including providing relevant staff names and requested evidence ; 6. Provide a clear explanation for the credit card cancellation in light of my mothers payment history and zero balance on the cancelled card since XX/XX/XXXX ; 7. Confirm whether the safe deposit box dispute, police report, CFPB complaint, or related internal complaint activity had any role in the credit card cancellation decision ; 8. Provide a substantive response addressing the facts and evidence submitted, rather than repeated boilerplate letters. 

Our family remains willing to cooperate fully. We respectfully ask that this complaint not be closed until Wells Fargo provides a meaningful explanation of its investigation, its handling of law enforcement requests, its claimed authorization issue regarding CFPB communication, and its credit card cancellation decision. 

Thank you for your attention and assistance.

text:
I am filing a complaint regarding a fraud claim with Wells Fargo involving {$14000.00}. 
I was a victim of impersonation fraud. I was contacted by an individual who was posing as Wells Fargo and who had knowledge of my account information. I believed I was speaking with the bank and was instructed to take immediate action to 'protect ' my funds. 
Following those instructions, I went into a Wells Fargo branch and withdrew cash from my account. Although I did not write a check, the transaction appears to have been processed internally as a withdrawal with a check number. 
I was then instructed to deposit the funds using what I was told was a secure method. This involved a digital debit card that appeared temporarily on my phone. That digital card is not associated with my account, is not in my name, and is no longer accessible to me. 
The Funds were deposited and then immediately removed. Wells Fargo has stated that they do not see a digital card associated with my account, which is exactly the issue. The account or card used to receive the funds was not mine and not under my control. This supports that the transaction was part of a fraudulent scheme and not a legitimate or authorized transfer. 
I reported the fraud and initially filed a claim. That claim was denied. However Wells Fargo then reopened the matter under a new claim number and transferred it to their check fraud department, focusing on the withdrawal itself rather than the fraudulent circumstances that caused it. 
This reclassification is the core issue. The withdrawal was not a normal or voluntary transaction, it was performed under deception by someone impersonating the bank. 
The entire sequence of events, including the withdrawal and subsequent deposit, was part of a coordinated fraud. 
Despite reporting this promptly and fully cooperating, I have not received provisional credit. I was informed that an expedited request has been submitted, but I have already waited the standard XXXX business days typically associated with fraud investigations. 
I am concerned that my claim is being improperly evaluated as a check or withdrawal issue rather than as impersonation fraud involving unauthorized activity. The focus on how the withdrawal was processed is ignoring the fact that I was deceived into making that transaction. 
I am requesting that this case be reviewed as fraud involving impersonation and unauthorized activity, and that provisional credit be issued while the investigation continues. 
I am also requesting a full review of how this claim has been handled, including the denial of the original claim number, and the failure to provide timely provisional credit. 
This situation has caused significant financial hardship and stress, and I am seeking a fair resolution consistent with consumer protection standards. 

XXXX XXXX

text:
I am filing this complaint due to ongoing unresolved issues and PennyMac Loan Services, LLCs continued failure to comply with its servicing obligations and prior acknowledgments regarding funds owed to me. 

This matter is not isolated. I have filed multiple complaints through the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau regarding similar issues with this servicer. 

For reference, my most recent complaint ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ), submitted on XX/XX/year>, is part of a series of complaints I have filed since XX/XX/year>. In total, I have submitted five complaints regarding the same unresolved issues. 

Despite these repeated complaints, the company has consistently failed to provide a clear, complete, and actionable resolution. Instead, they have responded with vague, indirect, and incomplete explanations that do not address the core issues raised. 

This repeated need to escalate demonstrates a pattern of deficient servicing practices, lack of transparency, and negligent handling of my funds. 

In prior correspondence DATED XX/XX/year> PennyMac acknowledged that the following amounts are owed to me : {$300.00} related to a State Farm insurance payment that I paid out of pocket, which should have been covered through escrow. 

{$750.00}, which was separately identified and acknowledged as an outstanding balance owed to me. 

I explicitly requested that both amounts be issued via paper check mailed directly to my address for proper documentation and traceability. 
However, PennyMac has failed to comply.

In its response da, the company introduced a new and inconsistent position regarding the {$750.00}, claiming that the funds were credited to my escrow account and/or that a payment had been issued and subsequently returned.

I do not accept this claim.

I have never received any such payment. My address on file is correct, and there is no valid reason for any alleged return. PennyMac has failed to provide any supporting documentation, including proof of mailing, tracking information, delivery confirmation, or evidence of return.

Without such documentation, this claim is unsubstantiated and does not constitute fulfillment of their obligation. If a payment was in fact issued and returned, the company must provide verifiable evidence and immediately reissue the payment.

Furthermore, even if a check had been issued and returned, PennyMacs unilateral decision to apply those funds to my escrow account is unacceptable and improper.

Once the company has acknowledged that the funds are owed directly to me, those funds must be disbursed to me, not retained, redirected, or internally reallocated at the companys discretion. Any alleged return of a mailed check does not extinguish their obligation to pay me directly. Instead, they are required to promptly reissue the payment.

Crediting funds to an escrow account does not constitute a disbursement to the borrower and does not satisfy the obligation owed to me.

Under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ), 12 U.S.C. 2605, and its implementing regulation, Regulation X ( 12 C.F.R. Part 1024 ), mortgage servicers are required to properly manage escrow accounts, accurately account for borrower funds, and promptly return any surplus or funds owed directly to the borrower.

PennyMacs actionscrediting funds internally to escrow instead of issuing payment, failing to provide clear disbursement details, and offering inconsistent explanationsare inconsistent with these obligations and may constitute improper handling of escrow funds.

With respect to the {$300.00}, PennyMac has also failed to provide any clear commitment to reimburse me. Their response merely references the underlying insurance payment but does not confirm payment to me, does not provide a disbursement date, and does not specify any method of reimbursement.

This is unacceptable.

These funds were paid directly out of my personal pocket due to a servicing failure. They must be reimbursed to me directly and must not be treated as an escrow adjustment, internal credit, or any form of indirect accounting entry.

Additionally, PennyMac continues to attempt to require that I contact them by phone in order to request payment. I will not do so.

This submission is intended to provide : a complete factual timeline, clarification regarding disputed transaction inconsistencies, supporting evidence related to the impersonation event that led to discovery of the fraud, and concerns regarding the completeness and reliability of the prior claim investigations and denials. 

BACKGROUND AND ACCOUNT HISTORY The Wells Fargo account involved was not used as a primary day-to-day spending account during the time of the fraudulent charges ( XX/XX/XXXX - XX/XX/XXXX XXXX ). UNAUTHORIZED TRANSACTION ACTIVITY Beginning XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, multiple unauthorized debit card transactions occurred on the account. 

These transactions were all card-not-present/online transactions. 

The transaction behavior reflected an escalating fraud pattern beginning with smaller validation and test charges and progressing into significantly larger transactions over time. 

Examples of the unauthorized transaction pattern included : repeated small authorization/test charges, escalating purchase amounts, electric vehicle charging-related charges despite my not owning or operating an electric vehicle, travel and rental-related transactions inconsistent with my account history, and merchant activity inconsistent with the purpose and ordinary use of the account. 

The disputed transactions included the following : XX/XX/XXXX {$340.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$320.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$440.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$38.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$260.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$110.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$210.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$25.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$16.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$20.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$48.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$86.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$950.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$3700.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$110.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$1700.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$2200.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$69.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$1600.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$2200.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$130.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$29.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$420.00} XX/XX/XXXX {$360.00} Additional disputed amount {$210.00} The total disputed amount exceeded {$15000.00}. 

XX/XX/XXXX FRAUD DISCOVERY AND IMPERSONATION EVENT On XX/XX/XXXX at approximately XXXX AM PST, I received a text message stating : Wells Fargo XXXX : Did you make a {$430.00} purchase at Target card ending XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX? Reply YES or NO. To opt out of alerts, reply STOP.

XX/XX/XXXX INITIAL FRAUD REPORT TO WELLS FARGO At approximately XXXX AM PST on XX/XX/XXXX, I independently contacted Wells Fargo directly at ( XXXX ) XXXX to report the incident and unauthorized transactions.

XX/XX/XXXX CONTINUED TRANSACTION DISCREPANCIES On XX/XX/XXXX at approximately XXXX AM PST, I received another inbound call from a Wells Fargo XXXX department representative.

INVESTIGATION TIMELINE CONCERNS Although the fraud was initially reported on XX/XX/XXXX, the effective business-day investigation period appears to have run only from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX.

XX/XX/XXXX REOPENED CLAIM DENIAL On Monday, XX/XX/XXXX at approximately XXXX AM PST, I received another inbound call from Wells Fargo regarding the reopened fraud claim. 

I returned the call later that day and was informed that the reopened claim had again been denied. 

During the conversation : I requested clarification regarding how the reinvestigation could reasonably have been completed within such a limited timeframe, particularly because the prior representative had advised on XX/XX/XXXX that supporting evidence could be submitted within approximately XXXX hours. 

I was informed that the claim reopening occurred on Friday, XX/XX/XXXX at approximately XXXX PM XXXX. 

However, by Monday morning, XX/XX/XXXX, the claim had already again been denied despite no meaningful business-day investigation period appearing to have occurred between reopening and denial. 

During the XX/XX/XXXX discussion : the representative referenced approximately XXXX disputed transactions, further conflicting with the prior internal transaction counts of approximately XXXX and approximately XXXX transactions previously referenced by Wells Fargo XXXX and representatives. 

Additional inconsistencies became apparent regarding : transaction totals, transaction groupings, digital card analysis, and prior transaction history interpretations. 

The representative additionally stated that some disputed transactions were allegedly associated with a digital card number. 

However, given that the impersonation caller already possessed : my name, address, email address, full debit card number, expiration date, and CVV/security code, it is entirely plausible that unauthorized individuals also obtained access to digital wallet or digital card information associated with the compromised account. 

The representative additionally referenced alleged prior XXXX transaction history as support for denial reasoning. 

However : I do not maintain a XXXX account, disputed XXXX transactions themselves had previously been inconsistently grouped across Wells Fargo XXXX, and prior claim records omitted certain disputed XXXX transactions entirely. 

As a result, transaction activity that should have been grouped together as part of the same disputed fraud activity instead appeared fragmented across differing claim records, creating the inaccurate appearance of unrelated prior usage history. 

During the XX/XX/XXXX discussion, I was additionally provided XXXX Escalation reference number XXXX associated with the continued review and escalation of the matter. 

CONCLUSION AND REQUEST The repeated inconsistencies involving : transaction totals, transaction groupings, differing internal transaction counts, claim visibility, omitted disputed transactions, additional unexplained transactions, fragmented records, digital card analysis, denial timing, and the absence of meaningful evidence review prior to denial raise substantial concerns regarding whether the prior investigation process was : complete, internally consistent, procedurally reliable, and based upon accurate consolidated claim information.

This evidence further supports that the account information had been compromised and that the disputed transactions were unauthorized. 

Given the inconsistencies identified during the prior handling of the claim, I respectfully request : a full and comprehensive reinvestigation, review of all supporting evidence, review utilizing the corrected and reconciled transaction records, and written clarification regarding the basis for prior denials and fragmented claim handling.

COMPLAINT REGARDING INACCURATE CREDIT REPORTING DURING APPROVED FORBEARANCE AND TRIAL LOAN MODIFICATION I am filing this complaint against Freedom Mortgage for inaccurately reporting my mortgage payments as late to the credit bureaus during an approved forbearance period and a servicer-offered trial payment plan, causing severe and ongoing financial harm. 

BACKGROUND In XXXX of XXXX, I entered into an approved forbearance agreement with Freedom Mortgage on my mortgage loan ( Account # XXXX ). The forbearance was approved by the servicer and lasted approximately XXXX months. 

At the conclusion of the forbearance, Freedom Mortgage offered me a trial payment plan as a pathway to a permanent loan modification. The servicer presented this plan as a preview of what my new modified loan terms would look like, contingent on my completing three consecutive on-time payments at the reduced trial amount. I accepted the trial plan in good faith. 

During the trial period, I made all three payments on time and in the exact amounts specified by the servicer. Critically, when I logged into my mortgage account on Freedom Mortgage 's online portal during this period, the reduced trial payment amount was displayed as my " payment due. '' There was no indication on the portal that a different, higher amount was expected, nor any warning that making the trial payments as instructed could result in negative credit reporting. 

I successfully completed the trial period, and my permanent loan modification was finalized. I have been current on my modified mortgage payments since the modification was completed. 

THE PROBLEM Despite the fact that I was on an approved forbearance and then made every trial payment on time and as instructed, Freedom Mortgage reported multiple late payments to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX during both the forbearance period and the trial modification period. The servicer 's justification is that because the trial payments were less than the full original mortgage payment amount which they claim was " technically still valid '' until the permanent modification was executed the payments qualified as partial and therefore late. 

This reporting is misleading and harmful for the following reasons : 1. The servicer approved the forbearance and offered the trial plan. I did not unilaterally reduce my payments I followed the servicer 's own program. 

2. The servicer 's online portal displayed the reduced trial amount as my payment due during the trial period. A reasonable consumer logging into their account would conclude that paying the amount shown as due constitutes an on-time payment. 

3. At no point did the servicer clearly disclose in the trial plan offer, on the portal, or in any communication I received that making the trial payments as instructed would result in late payment reporting to the credit bureaus. 

4. The trial plan was presented as a pathway to modification, not as a period during which my credit would be damaged. Had I understood the credit reporting consequences, I would have sought alternative arrangements. 

DISPUTE HISTORY Upon discovering the late payment entries on my credit reports, I filed a dispute directly with the servicer. They denied my dispute, claiming the reporting was " accurate '' because the original loan terms technically remained in effect until the modification was finalized. I believe this response fails to account for the misleading nature of the trial plan offer and the portal display, and does not reflect a reasonable investigation of my dispute as required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. 

FINANCIAL HARM The inaccurate late payment reporting has had severe, concrete financial consequences : - My credit score has dropped significantly. My current score is approximately XXXX, whereas prior to the forbearance and trial period it was substantially higher. 

- I have been denied a home equity line of credit ( HELOC ) specifically due to the reported forbearance and late payments, despite having significant equity in my home and strong income ( {$140000.00} annual salary plus approximately $ XXXX in rental income ). 

- As a direct result of being unable to access home equity lending, I remain unable to consolidate approximately {$50000.00} in credit card debt that I took on because of unexpected medical issues, much of which is accruing interest at rates exceeding 25 %. Had I been approved for a HELOC at typical rates of XXXX %, I would be saving thousands of dollars per year in interest charges. 

- The damaged credit profile is limiting my financial options and prolonging a debt situation that my income would otherwise allow me to resolve efficiently.

text:
TransUnion has enough information to impersonate any of us and the information it sells decides where we can work, who we can borrow from, what we can borrow, and the interest rates at which we borrow. TransUnion credit scores are pretty much a quantitative value of how " good and trustworthy '' of a person you and I are. 

One would expect such an important company to be held against the highest ethical, accuracy, and transparency standards... But clearly, Transunion is nowhere near the bar. 

Between XX/XX/2023 and XX/XX/2023, my TransUnion credit score ( as seen through my XXXX bank app ) dropped by XXXX from XXXX to XXXX. My XXXX Credit score dropped by a similar number as well, but this complaint is focused on TransUnion. It is funny because my revolving utilization was lower than previous months and I didn't do anything to lower my credit score. 

The only thing that comes to my mind is that I requested a credit line increase from my XXXX bank. But XXXX uses soft inquiry and should not have lowered my credit score. In fact, it should have increased my score because it reduced my utilization. 

I need to understand why my credit score decreased, so I called XXXX Customer support. XXXX customer support confirmed their soft inquiry shouldn't have harmed my credit score and advised me to call TransUnion ( where they get my credit score ) and gave me their phone number : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

I called TransUnion. The call felt like a scam. They asked for my Zip Code, full social security number, and date of birth. I checked the phone number during the call and managed to confirm through XXXX XXXX that it was a legitimate number, so I answered the questions. I was forwarded to TransUnion Customer support without issue. 

The first thing the customer support agent asked was " where did I get my credit score from? '' I answered " XXXX. '' She went quiet for a couple of minutes and didn't respond no matter how much I asked if " she was there? '' She then hanged up on me... 

I made another call. But I didn't feel safe sharing my SSN again and I don't feel I should share it like that. This is sensitive information and they " record the phone call for quality control purpose. '' So, I'm not convinced my information is appropriately collected or stored. 

I tried getting my credit score from www.annualcreditreport.com. I couldn't get my XXXX and XXXX credit reports at the time ( they said to try on a business day, so I will do that later ), but I got the TransUnion report ( they didn't give me access to my credit score, though ). I didn't see a possible reason for my score to have dropped. 

Here are my complaints. 
- I have a right to freely get all the information that TransUnion reports on me. That includes my report, my score, and why my score changed. It is suspicious to me that TransUnion and other credit bureaus ' Credit Score algorithms are not publicly disclosed and it is even worse that TransUnion customer support doesn't bother answering my questions and hangs up on me. 
- For a company that is trusted with our identities, I don't think it is okay for their phone calls to sound so much like a scam or to ask for PII like SSN on a phone call. What I provided them just on that call is enough to steal my identity and I felt like the customer support agent was probably in XXXX, so the information probably didn't even stay in the US. It feels like PII is unscrupulously collected, shared, and stored. Clearly no action was made to ensure their calls stand out from scams. They could have confirmed my identity by sending me a text message with a temporary code instead of asking for extremely sensitive and hard to change PII like SSN. 
- It seems like my experience is a common one, looking at XXXX XXXX 's and other websites ' reviews. I don't understand why a company so unscrupulous with PII and disrespectful of consumer 's right to know their financial records is one of three trusted sources of our financial trustworthiness. In the long term, I don't want TransUnion to be used to assess my financial trustworthiness anymore. It frustrates me that I have no control on that.

Financial entities, regardless of their operational model, owe a duty of care to their customers and the broader financial ecosystem. Traditional financial institutions are legally required to exercise the skill and diligence of a competent and vigilant financial entity, adhering to international best practices in fraud detection, anti-money laundering ( AML ), and consumer protection. 

In this case, Coinbase had a duty to identify, assess, and act upon red flags that indicated a high probability of fraud. A financial service provider can not simply turn a blind eye to objective warning signs that a transaction is associated with illicit activity. This standard applies universallywhether through Know Your Customer ( KYC ) obligations, risk assessment protocols, fraud prevention mechanisms, or transaction monitoring systems.

While interpretations of reasonableness may vary, the core principle remains the same : the obligation to apply reasonable care in all circumstances, not merely to follow industry norms at their lowest threshold. The fact that many institutions may routinely overlook risks does not justify negligence. A responsible entity must proactively prevent foreseeable harm rather than react only after financial losses occur.

Given the patterns of fraud that have emerged in similar cases, it is imperative that institutions learn from past failures and refine their protective measures. The evidence in this case strongly suggests that Coinbase failed to exercise reasonable foresight, disregarding key warning signs and failing to intervene despite the clear risks involved.

Coinbases Position & RESPONSE Coinbase contends that the circumstances of this case do not establish a genuine obligation to protect victims from fraudulent schemes. In its response, Coinbase implicitly suggests that unwritten obligations, reasonable judgment, practical safeguards, and lessons from past incidents should be disregarded in favor of a rigid legalistic approach. Given their size, influence, and vast technological resources, they were far better positioned than an individual consumer to identify risks and intervene where necessary, particularly in relation to high-risk, out-of-pattern transactions. Moreover, Coinbase has avoided directly engaging with the key arguments raised in this complaint. Instead, their response appears crafted to protect their own interests rather than to uphold their duty of care. This approach is not only inadequate but also contradicts regulatory expectations, which emphasize that financial service providers should proactively implement safeguards to prevent fraudulent exploitation of their platforms. 

It is neither fair nor sustainable to shield financial entities behind self-serving technicalities while vulnerable victims suffer severe financial consequences. text:
I am submitting this complaint regarding the way myFlexPay structures and communicates repayment of earned wage access ( EWA ) transfers, which resulted in unexpected and financially harmful payroll deductions. 

The core issue is not that the system malfunctioned, but that the repayment mechanism is not clearly or adequately disclosed to users, leading to a reasonable misunderstanding that directly caused financial harm. 

Summary of Events I used the myFlexPay service to access earned wages prior to payday. Based on how the platform presents work weeks ( Sunday through Saturday ), I reasonably understood that transfers made in different weeks would be repaid separately across different paychecks. 

I made the following transfers : XX/XX/year> {$650.00} + {$3.00} fee XX/XX/year> {$340.00} + {$3.00} fee XX/XX/year> {$380.00} + {$3.00} fee These were settled as follows : XX/XX/year> paycheck {$650.00} deducted ( partial settlement of XX/XX/XXXX transfer ) XX/XX/year> paycheck {$730.00} deducted ( remaining balance plus both XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX transfers and fees ) As a result, I received paychecks of {$0.00} and approximately {$26.00}, creating immediate financial hardship and impacting my ability to meet essential obligations, including rent. 

How the System Actually Works ( Per Company Explanation ) After contacting support, I was informed that repayment is not based on the displayed weekly work periods or when transfers are made. 

Instead, repayment is governed by a lock date system : Transfers made before the lock date are settled on that paycheck Transfers made after the lock date are settled on the next paycheck In my case : Pay period : XX/XX/XXXX to XX/XX/year> Lock date : XX/XX/year> Both the XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX transfers occurred before the XX/XX/XXXX lock date, which caused them to be combined into a single paycheck deduction. 

Disclosure and Design Issue The problem is that this lock date mechanism is not clearly presented in a way that a reasonable user can rely on when making financial decisions.

1. Terms of Service focus on payroll cycles, not lock dates The Terms of Service describe the service in relation to : Available Earnings before the employer runs payroll Earnings accrued since the last payroll run Access before the next payroll run Deductions from the end of pay-cycle salary payment This language frames the service around payroll cycles and pay periods. 

However, the Terms I reviewed do not clearly define or prominently disclose that a separate lock date determines which paycheck is actually debited. 

2. App presentation reinforces a weekly structure The platform displays work weeks as Sunday through Saturday, which reasonably suggests that repayment aligns with those periods.

There is no clear, prominent indication at the point of transfer that : -displayed work weeks do not control repayment timing -multiple transfers across different displayed weeks may still be combined into one paycheck -a lock date is the actual controlling factor 3. Company acknowledgment of the issue In their final response to my complaint ( Reference XXXX ), the company acknowledged : That the Sunday-to-Saturday work week display could reasonably lead someone to expect repayment would align with those periods That the lock date mechanism isn't clearly visible at the point of making a transfer Despite acknowledging both the potential for reasonable misunderstanding and the lack of visibility at the decision point, the company denied any reimbursement or adjustment. 

Why This Matters This is a disclosure and transparency issue. 

A financial product that : allows early access to wages automatically deducts repayment from paychecks uses a non-obvious internal mechanism ( lock date ) to determine repayment timing must clearly and prominently disclose how and when deductions will occur. 

In this case, the system : presents one structure ( weekly work periods ) operates on another ( lock date cutoff ) does not clearly connect the two at the point of user decision-making This creates a materially misleading experience and exposes users to significant and unexpected wage depletion. 

Financial Impact Due to this lack of clear disclosure : Multiple transfers were combined into a single paycheck deduction I received paychecks of {$0.00} and approximately {$26.00} This caused immediate financial hardship, including difficulty meeting rent obligations

text:
What happened : This matter centers on Wells Fargos failure to evaluate the controlling evidence in a billing dispute : the transaction-dated sales documentation. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, jewelry containing blue diamonds was purchased from XXXX XXXX  for approximately {$25000.00} using a Wells Fargo XXXX XXXX credit account. 

The only reliable and verifiable record of what was disclosed at the time of sale is the transaction documentation provided at purchase, including the sales receipt, jewelry tags, and merchant appraisal. These documents do not contain any written disclosure that the blue diamonds were color-enhanced or treated. 

After the sale, an independent XXXX gemological report, obtained at my expense, confirmed that the diamonds are color-enhanced/ treated. This did not create the issue ; it revealed that a material characteristic affecting value existed but was not disclosed in the transaction documentation. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, a billing dispute was opened with Wells Fargo for goods not as described. 

Between XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo denied the dispute and multiple appeals. On XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, three separate complaints were filed with the CFPB due to the companys failure to address the absence of written disclosure. 

Across all disputes and complaints, Wells Fargo did not identify any transaction-dated document showing that gemstone treatment was disclosed in writing at the time of sale. 

Instead of evaluating the actual sales documentation, Wells Fargo relied on merchant statements obtained after the transaction, interpretations of product descriptions, and appraisal-based arguments. These sources are not equivalent to the transaction record and do not establish what was disclosed at the time of purchase. 

This is the central failure. 

Regulatory standards exist specifically to prevent this type of situation and to ensure consumer protection through verifiable documentation. These include : - Regulation Z ( 12 CFR 1026.13 ), requiring a reasonable investigation based on the transaction record - The Fair Credit Billing Act, requiring evaluation of whether goods were accurately described based on what was provided at the time of sale - FTC Jewelry Guides ( 16 CFR Part 23 ), requiring disclosure of gemstone treatments that materially affect value clearly and conspicuously at the time of sale These standards require that disclosure be made in writing at the time of the transaction so that it can be verified. They do not rely on recollection, interpretation, or statements made after the fact. 

In this case : - The diamonds were confirmed to be treated by an independent XXXX report obtained after purchase - Treatment materially affects value - The transaction-dated sales documentation contains no written disclosure of treatment - Wells Fargo has not produced any document showing that such disclosure exists Wells Fargo also stated it could not determine what was discussed at the time of sale, yet still concluded the goods were properly described. When disclosure is required to be in writing, the transaction documentation is the controlling evidence. If the documentation does not contain the disclosure, then it was not disclosed. 

A reasonable investigation requires verification of disclosure within the transaction documentation. That did not occur. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo issued a final response maintaining its denial without identifying any transaction-dated document showing disclosure of gemstone treatment. 

To date, across all internal disputes, appeals, and CFPB complaints, Wells Fargo has not produced any evidence demonstrating that the required disclosure occurred in the sales documentation. 

The central issue remains unresolved : - A material characteristic affecting value ( treatment ) exists - Required written disclosure is absent from the transaction documentation - The investigation did not evaluate or resolve that absence By relying on post-sale statements instead of the documented transaction record, the investigation did not address the controlling evidence. 

Given that the required disclosure must be verifiable in the transaction documentation and no such documentation has been identified, the determination appears unsupported by the record and raises concerns that the investigation did not meet the standards required under Regulation Z and the Fair Credit Billing Act for resolving billing disputes involving goods not as described.
label: Credit card

This complaint concerns the continued reporting and attempted enforcement of an alleged debt originally issued by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and subsequently associated with Security Credit Services. 

My consumer disclosure reflects that the account was charged off in the approximate amount of {$19000.00} and later transferred or sold to another entity. 

Despite formal dispute and evidentiary notice, this account continues to be reported and/or represented without competent documentary substantiation. 

This raises material violations under both Regulation V ( XXXX CFR Part XXXX ) and Regulation XXXX  ( XXXX CFR Part XXXX ). 

-- - REGULATION V VIOLATIONS ( FURNISHER AND REPORTING OBLIGATIONS ) Under XXXX CFR XXXX ( b ), furnishers are required to conduct a reasonable investigation upon receipt of a dispute and review all relevant information. 

No documentation has been provided demonstrating : The original executed agreement The complete transactional ledger The methodology used to calculate the reported balance The factual basis for the charge-off determination Under XXXX CFR XXXX, furnishers must maintain reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy and integrity of furnished information. 

Because the account is reported as charged off and transferred, accuracy requires verifiable proof of : The original obligation The complete balance calculation The identity of the current owner The legal authority of any entity continuing to report the account Without such documentation, the information is materially unverifiable. 

-- - REGULATION XXXX  VIOLATIONS ( DEBT COLLECTION CONDUCT ) Security Credit Services, as a third-party debt collector, is subject to Regulation XXXX. 

Under XXXX CFR XXXX, a debt collector must provide accurate validation information, including : The amount of the debt The identity of the creditor Sufficient information to allow the consumer to evaluate the debt No such validation has been provided. 

Under XXXX CFR XXXX, a debt collector must properly investigate disputes and respond with substantiated findings. 

No competent documentation has been produced in response to dispute. 

Under XXXX CFR XXXX ( d ), a debt collector is prohibited from making false, deceptive, or misleading representations regarding : The amount of the debt The ownership of the debt The legal status of the obligation Continued reporting or representation of this account without documentary substantiation raises material concerns under this provision. 

-- - CHAIN OF TITLE AND AUTHORITY DEFECTS The account is reported as sold or transferred. 

Accordingly, lawful reporting and collection require documentary proof of : Complete assignment chain from the original creditor Date and terms of transfer Identity of the current legal owner Authority of any entity reporting or attempting to collect Absent assignment-chain documentation, no party can establish lawful authority to report or enforce the alleged obligation. 

-- - WILLFUL NONCOMPLIANCE FRAMEWORK A formal evidentiary dispute notice has already been issued demanding full documentary verification. 

Continued reporting after actual notice of material defects, without production of underlying documentation, constitutes reckless disregard for statutory obligations. 

See : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX A party can not continue to publish adverse financial information affecting a consumer while lacking the evidentiary basis necessary to support that publication. 

-- - REQUESTED RESOLUTION I request that the parties involved : XXXX. Provide full documentary verification, including : Original executed agreement Complete transactional ledger Itemized balance calculation Charge-off documentation Full assignment chain and ownership records XXXX. Identify the current legal owner of the account and the basis for continued reporting. 

XXXX. Cease any collection or reporting activity unless and until such documentation is produced. 

XXXX. Delete the account from all consumer reporting agencies if competent documentation can not be provided. 


NOTICE Any continued reporting, reinsertion, or representation of this account without documentary substantiation after formal dispute and evidentiary notice will be treated as knowing and willful noncompliance. 

This complaint is submitted for regulatory review and enforcement action.

Mr. Cooper, the nations largest nonbank servicer of mortgage loans, will refund customers nearly {$90.00} million and pay a civil penalty of more than {$6.00} million to settle a lawsuit claiming it violated the rights of over XXXX customers, some of whom it had illegally foreclosed on. 

When Mr. Cooper then known as Nationstar bought thousands of mortgages through XXXX bulk purchases, it frequently failed to identify loans with existing modifications, according to the lawsuit, which was filed by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Those modifications allowed the borrower to make trial payments, which would then require the servicer to permanently modify the loans. 

But Mr. Cooper often didnt take those mods into account, and then foreclosed on thousands of those borrowers, damaging their finances and credit, the CFPB and state attorneys generals for 53 states and territories said on Monday. Mortgage servicers are entrusted with handling significant financial transactions for millions of Americans, including struggling homeowners, said CFPB Director XXXX XXXX in a statement. [ Mr. Cooper ] broke that trust by engaging in unfair and deceptive practices prohibited by the Consumer Financial Protection Act of XXXX as well as violations of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act and the Homeowners Protection Act. 
Specifically, the CFPB alleged that between XXXX XXXX  and XXXX XXXX XXXX, Nationstar : Failed to identify loans on its systems that had pending loss-mitigation applications or trial-modification plans, and as a result failed to honor borrowers loan modification agreements. 
Foreclosed on borrowers to whom it had promised it would not foreclose while their loss mitigation applications were pending Improperly increased borrowers permanent, modified monthly loan payments, mispresented to borrowers when they would be eligible to have their private mortgage insurance premiums canceled, and failed to timely remove private mortgage insurance from borrowers accounts. 
Failed to timely disburse borrowers tax payments from their escrow accounts and failed to properly conduct escrow analyses for borrowers during their XXXX XXXX bankruptcy proceedings. 
According to the release, if entered by the court, Mr. Cooper would be required to immediately set aside about {$15.00} million to pay borrowers it has not remediated prior to the orders effective date and to certify that it has already paid approximately {$57.00} million in redress to other borrowers affected by the conduct alleged in the complaint. 

We are holding Nationstar accountable for harming homeowners by improperly servicing their mortgage loans, said Delaware Attorney General XXXX XXXX. The new servicing standards in this settlement will help ensure Nationstar does not repeat this conduct. 

The consent judgment also requires Mr. Cooper to follow a detailed set of rules or servicing standards related to how it handles certain mortgage loans. These servicing standards are more comprehensive than existing law and will be in place for three years starting on XXXX XXXX XXXX 

Mr. Cooper has negotiated several multi-million dollar settlements in the past for violations of state financial laws, including the California Department of Business Oversight in XXXX  for overcharging borrowers and failing to properly investigate consumer complaints and unfair and deceptive business practices filed by the New York Department of Financial Services in XXXX 

In a statement following the news of the settlement, Mr. Coopers Chairman and CEO XXXX XXXX said the company was pleased to resolve the matter. When these issues were identified several years ago, we immediately made restitution to our impacted customers and invested in process improvements to prevent reoccurrence, he said in a prepared statement. Since then, we have continued to invest in technology, people, and leadership to ensure that our compliance and risk management programs not only meet our regulators expectations but also support sustainable growth and maintain our position as an industry leader.

I recently discovered that Aargon Agency is reporting a collection account on my credit report that I do not recognize, did not authorize, and do not own. Upon discovering this account, I immediately took action to investigate and protect myself from potential identity theft. I reviewed my credit reports carefully and confirmed that this account does not belong to me. I did not open this account, I did not authorize any transactions associated with it, and I have never had any business relationship with Aargon Agency.

Because of the seriousness of this issue, I filed an Identity Theft Report with the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ). Filing this report was a necessary step to protect my identity and to ensure that fraudulent activity is properly documented and addressed.

In addition to filing the FTC identity theft report, I also disputed this account directly with the credit reporting agencies, including XXXX XXXX and XXXX. In my disputes, I clearly stated that this account does not belong to me and that it is the result of identity theft. I requested that the account be investigated and removed from my credit report.

It is important to note that the presence of personal identifying information such as my name, address, or Social Security number on an account does not prove ownership. This information can be obtained and misused by unauthorized third parties, which is exactly what appears to have occurred in this case.

The continued reporting of this account is causing significant harm to me. It is negatively impacting my credit score and affecting my ability to obtain credit, housing, and other financial opportunities. This harm is ongoing and will continue as long as the account remains on my credit report.

Additionally, I have identified inconsistencies and concerns regarding how this account is being reported. The information reported by Aargon Agency has not been properly verified, and there is no evidence that a reasonable investigation has been conducted.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), both credit reporting agencies and data furnishers such as Aargon Agency are required to maintain maximum possible accuracy when reporting consumer information. They are also required to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation when a consumer disputes information.

In this case, those obligations have not been met.

Aargon Agency appears to be relying on unverified or incomplete information rather than conducting a thorough investigation. This raises serious concerns about the accuracy of the information being reported and the procedures being used to verify it.

Furthermore, under FCRA 605B, when a consumer provides an identity theft report and identifies fraudulent accounts, the credit reporting agencies are required to block the reporting of those accounts. I have provided this documentation, yet the account continues to be reported.

This situation highlights a broader issue with how identity theft and consumer disputes are handled. Companies are often relying on automated systems or superficial verification processes that do not adequately address the complexities of identity theft.

The burden of proof should not be placed on me to prove that I did not open this account. Instead, Aargon Agency must prove that I did. Without such proof, the account can not be considered valid.

At this point, it is clear that the account has not been properly validated and should not be reported on my credit file. The failure to remove this account is a violation of my rights under the FCRA and is causing ongoing harm.

In summary, I discovered an account reported by Aargon Agency that I do not recognize and do not own. I took immediate action by filing disputes and an identity theft report. Despite this, the account remains on my credit report, and Aargon Agency has failed to provide sufficient documentation to support their claim.

Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) by Bank of America. 

This complaint supersedes CFPB Case No. XXXX, which was closed without substantive review of the Bank Secrecy Act ( BSA ) and Consent Order compliance issues raised herein. New evidence includes : ( 1 ) OCC inquiry to Bank of America ( XX/XX/XXXX ) ; ( 2 ) recorded admission that XXXX XXXX was " banned by Social Security Number '' post-loss ; ( 3 ) OCC Consent Order XXXX adjudicating systemic deficiencies. 
Statement of Facts In early XXXX, Bank of America processed {$30000.00} in transfers from my account to XXXX XXXX / XXXX XXXX XXXX, a publicly documented fraudster ( SEC Litigation Release No. XXXX ). On a recorded call, a Bank of America Fraud Department representative admitted that XXXX XXXX was subsequently " banned by Social Security Number '' to prevent further fraud. This confirms the bank had the technical capacity and knowledge to identify and block XXXX as a threat but failed to do so before my loss occurred. 
The Timing Proves Violation Either Way If the SSN ban was before my transfers ( XXXX XXXX ) : Bank of Americas transaction monitoring failed to block a blacklisted recipient, violating OCC Consent Order Article II, Section 4 ( systemic failure to ensure appropriate thresholds ).

If the SSN ban was after my transfers : The bank failed to risk-rate a publicly-documented fraudster ( SEC XXXX ; Bankruptcy XXXX ) until a victim reported him, violating 31 C.F.R. 1010.230 ( CDD ) and Consent Order Article II, Section 5.

Either scenario proves systemic regulatory violations that caused my loss.

UDAAP Violations ( 12 U.S.C. 5536 ) Unfair Practice : Bank of America facilitated transfers to a known fraudster due to deficient monitoring and Customer Due Diligence systems, as adjudicated in OCC Consent Order XXXX ( Article XXXX, XXXX ). My injury was not reasonably avoidable because the banks failed controls, not authorization are the root cause. Federal BSA/AML duties run to the financial system, not just the customer. 
Deceptive Practice : Bank of America misrepresented to the CFPB that I had not provided a police report ( XXXX XXXX Report # XXXX number was provided ) and falsely categorized a documented fraud as a private investment dispute to evade regulatory scrutiny and the mandatory Article IX Look-Back review. 
Abusive Practice : Bank of America took advantage of my lack of understanding regarding the recipients banned SSN status and the banks systemic monitoring failures to coerce me into signing Scam Victim Acknowledgments. This materially interfered with my ability to understand the risks and exercise my rights under UCC 4A-202, because the banks procedures were not commercially reasonable ( as adjudicated by the Consent Order ).

text:
I am filing this complaint against LendingPoint LLC ( servicer ) and XXXX XXXX Bank ( original lender ) regarding a consumer installment loan for XXXX XXXX, Loan No. XXXX, originated XX/XX/XXXX, in the amount of {$14000.00}. 
BACKGROUND When I took out this loan to pay for XXXX XXXX, I was offered a " Same As Cash '' XXXX promotional term. I was told that if I paid the full {$14000.00} balance within XXXX  months, no interest would be charged. If I did not pay in full, interest would be charged back to the original loan date at a disclosed APR of 23.4899 %. 
I was not able to pay the loan in full within 12 months. The promotional period expired XX/XX/XXXX. At that point, I began to fall behind on payments. I contacted LendingPoint and was offered a XXXX XXXX XXXX, which I signed on XX/XX/XXXX. 
ISSUE XXXX : I WAS NOT TOLD HOW MUCH RETROACTIVE INTEREST WOULD BE ADDED When the promotional period ended, LendingPoint added retroactive interest back to the original loan date. However, at no point before or during the promotional period did LendingPoint clearly disclose to me in plain language what the total dollar amount of that retroactive interest would be. I was never shown a specific dollar figure showing what would be added to my balance if I failed to pay in full by XX/XX/XXXX. The contract used all-caps legal language that was not adequate to help me understand the actual financial impact. 
Federal regulations ( Regulation XXXX, XXXX C.F.R. XXXX ( h ) ) require that lenders offering deferred interest products clearly disclose that interest will be charged from the purchase date if the balance is not paid in full within the promotional period. I believe this disclosure was inadequate. 
ISSUE XXXX : THE LOAN MODIFICATION DID NOT INCLUDE REQUIRED DISCLOSURES The XX/XX/XXXX Modification Agreement changed my loan terms significantly it reduced my rate to 18.49 % APR, extended my loan term to 59 months, and set a new monthly payment of {$400.00}. However, the Modification Agreement did not include a XXXX in XXXX disclosure box showing the new APR, new finance charge, new total of payments, or amount financed. The original loan disclosed a 23.4899 % APR and total payments of {$21000.00}. The modification changed these figures materially without re-disclosing them. 
ISSUE XXXX : INTEREST WAS ADDED ON TOP OF INTEREST ( CAPITALIZATION ) The Modification Agreement states that as of XX/XX/XXXX, my balance was {$12000.00}, made up of {$12000.00} in unpaid principal and {$500.00} in " accrued unpaid interest. '' Under the modification, I am now paying 18.49 % interest on that combined amount meaning I am paying interest on interest that was previously accrued. This practice ( called interest capitalization ) was never clearly disclosed to me, and I did not knowingly agree to it. 
ISSUE XXXX : DEFAULT REMEDIES APPLIED TO AN ACCOUNT NEVER XXXX DAYS LATE Although some of my payments have been made late, I have never been XXXX or more days past due on this account. Despite this, LendingPoint 's modification contract contains a clause ( Section XXXX ) stating that if I miss any payment, they can immediately reinstate the original 23.4899 % APR without any prior notice to me. This " hair trigger '' default provision which can be activated without notice on an account that has never reached a reportable delinquency threshold is unfair and deceptive. 
ISSUE XXXX : I CAN NOT GET A COMPLETE ACCOUNTING OF MY BALANCE I have not been provided with a complete, itemized breakdown of : ( a ) all payments I have made since XX/XX/XXXX and how each was applied ; ( b ) the exact calculation of retroactive interest that was added when the promotional period expired ; ( c ) how the balance of {$12000.00} in the modification was calculated ; and ( d ) all fees that have been assessed. As of XX/XX/XXXX, my balance is {$7000.00}. I am unable to verify whether this balance is accurate without this information. 
WHAT I AM ASKING THE CFPB TO DO I am asking the CFPB to : XXXX. Require LendingPoint to provide a complete, certified payment history from XX/XX/XXXX through the present, showing how every payment was applied. 
XXXX. Require LendingPoint to provide a full calculation of the retroactive interest assessed when the promotional period expired, including the date assessed, the amount, and the method of calculation. 
XXXX. Investigate whether LendingPoint 's " Same As Cash '' promotional disclosures comply with federal Regulation XXXX  requirements for deferred interest products. 
XXXX. Investigate whether the XXXX XXXX XXXX was required to include XXXX in XXXX re-disclosures. 
XXXX. Investigate whether LendingPoint XXXX no-notice default rate reinstatement clause ( Modification Agreement, Section XXXX ) constitutes an unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice under XXXX U.S.C. XXXX. 
XXXX. Confirm that no adverse credit reporting has been or will be made based on the disputed balance while this matter is under review. 
I am attaching copies of the original signed Loan Agreement ( dated XX/XX/XXXX ) and the signed Loan Modification Agreement ( dated XX/XX/XXXX ) as supporting documentation. 
I have also sent a formal written Notice of Dispute and Demand for Accounting to LendingPoint LLC via XXXX mail, and a Preservation of Evidence notice. I am prepared to escalate to the DC XXXX of the Attorney General and to pursue civil remedies if this matter is not resolved.

text:
On XX/XX/year>, I was the victim of a sophisticated fraud scheme involving direct impersonation of Navy Federal Credit Union. I received a phone call that appeared to originate from Navy Federals official phone number, the same number listed on the back of my card. The caller accurately identified me, referenced a prior fraud case, and guided me through what appeared to be standard fraud prevention procedures, including canceling my card and updating my account credentials. 

During this interaction, a {$1500.00} credit appeared in my account, and I received legitimate emails from Navy Federal, further reinforcing the credibility of the situation. I was then instructed to transfer the funds via XXXX to what was described as a secure back-office account as part of the fraud mitigation process. Given the verified caller ID, the accurate account details, and the supporting activity on my account, I reasonably believed I was acting under the direction of Navy Federals fraud department and complied in good faith. 

Shortly thereafter, I realized I had been defrauded and immediately reported the incident to Navy Federal. At that time, I was led to believe that the matter would be resolved and was not informed that I could be held liable for the loss. 

Despite the clear indicators of third-party fraud and impersonation, Navy Federals subsequent investigation concluded with a denial of my claim and an implication that I was responsible for, or involved in, the transaction. I strongly dispute this determination. The level of sophistication used in this scam, including spoofing Navy Federals official phone number, leveraging legitimate communications, and demonstrating detailed knowledge of my account, would have reasonably misled any consumer. 

Furthermore, the integrity of Navy Federals investigation is called into question due to factual inaccuracies. During the appeal process, I discovered that Navy Federal had incorrectly identified my savings account as the account involved in the fraudulent activity, when in fact the transaction occurred on my checking account. When I brought this discrepancy to their attention, I did not receive a clear or satisfactory explanation. This raises serious concerns about the thoroughness and accuracy of the investigation used to deny my claim. 

I submitted a formal appeal outlining these issues ; however, Navy Federal denied the appeal without adequately addressing the evidence of impersonation, the procedural errors, or the deficiencies in their investigation. 

This situation represents a clear case of bank impersonation fraud and social engineering, not customer negligence or misconduct. Holding me financially responsible under these circumstances is both unreasonable and inconsistent with consumer protection standards. 

I am therefore requesting a full and independent review of this matter, including : -A reassessment of the fraud claim based on the documented evidence of impersonation and deception -A review of the investigative errors, including the misidentification of the affected account -A reversal of the claim denial and reimbursement of the {$1500.00} loss Given the facts, I believe Navy Federal has failed to properly investigate this claim and has inappropriately assigned liability.
