To Whom It May Concern : I am writing to address an unfortunate situation involving my lender, US Bank. In XX/XX/year>, I lost my job and immediately contacted US Bank to discuss forbearance options, as I was not earning any income at the time. I was informed that, if I qualified, I could enter forbearance, after which I would need to either pay back the deferred amount in full or add it to the end of my mortgage term. I made it clear several times that, since I had no income during the forbearance period, paying a lump sum at the end was not feasible. This concern was raised repeatedly throughout the process, and I was assured it would not be a problem. 
The agreement required me to call in each month with an update on my status. I always felt confident in the process, and everyone I spoke with seemed helpful. There was never any indication that something would go wrong. I specifically asked many times whether participating in forbearance would impact my credit score, and each time, I was reassured that it would not. This wasnt just mentioned once or twiceI brought it up frequently because I was worried about the potential effects. 
Throughout this period, I received letters mentioning late payments. When I inquired about these, I was told they were automatically generated by another department, and I shouldnt worry since I was in forbearance. The mobile app reflected late payments as well, and when I resumed payments in late fall according to my agreement, the app still wouldnt allow me to make payments, nor did it show them as registered. I was told that once the forbearance was finalized, the app would update accordingly. However, even after four to five months, the app remained unusable ; I continued calling monthly to make payments and check in but kept being told not to worry since the forbearance was still being closed out.

Recently, I checked my FICO score and noticed a significant drop. Worried, I planned to discuss this with my US Bank loan officer and considered the possibility of fraud, but soon realized the issue was tied to the conclusion of my forbearance. I called the same number for the team I dealt with during this process and spoke with someone named XXXX, who was not particularly helpful. She told me that US Bank never offered a program where you could pause payments without affecting your creditwhich contradicted everything I had been told throughout the process. 
When I asked to escalate the issue, I was transferred to XXXX, a supervisor, who showed no interest in resolving my problem. As a customer blindsided by this situation, I was panicked and received no sympathy from this supervisor. When I requested to speak to someone else, I was told that was not possible, but I could file a complaint and wait for a written response. 
With assistance from someone in another department at US Bankwho was also unsure about the situationI sought further help. After two weeks, I received a response from XXXX, who was polite but seemed unable to do much beyond delivering disappointing news. If anyone had listened to my calls, they would have clearly heard me ask several times whether the decision would affect my credit. I was given the impression that adding payments to the end of the mortgage was acceptable. US Bank receives their payment regardless, and refinancing could have been an option. There needs to be action taken. The forbearance team is responsible for ensuring customers understand the consequences, yet I was told to call in regularly and was instructed to keep them updated. I did this, and again when I asked, I was told not to worry. These representatives are referred to as relationship managers ; however, I was never able to speak directly with the one assigned to me, so no real relationship was established. All I could do was repeatedly explain my situation to whoever answered the phone. 
Additionally, I asked if I could refinance my mortgage, which would resolve much of this issuebut was told that due to the drop in my credit score, I could not. Ironically, the very institution that was supposed to help me will not refinance my existing mortgage because I sought their assistance and trusted their process. I am devastated and feel that despite doing everything right, the situation unraveled against me. US Bank told me I had to live with it and closed my complaintthat was it.

Hello, I am submitting a complaint regarding inaccurate credit reporting by Mazda Financial Services related to an alleged delinquent final auto loan payment. 

I had my auto loan set up on autopay for the duration of the loan. My understanding and expectation was that autopay would cover all scheduled payments through payoff. At no point was I clearly notified that the final payment would not be processed via autopay or required separate manual action. 

As a result, the final payment was not processed, and Mazda Financial Services has reported this as a delinquency to the credit bureaus. This does not reflect my payment intent or behavior, as I had automatic payments in place specifically to avoid missed payments, and I had never missed a payment for the life of the loan. 

I have since paid the final payment and attempted to resolve this issue directly with Mazda Financial Services, including submitting a goodwill request. Despite my consistent payment history and the circumstances involving autopay setup, they have refused to remove or correct the negative reporting. 

I am requesting : 1. A full investigation into the accuracy of this reported delinquency 2. Verification of how autopay was structured and whether it reasonably covered the final payment 3. Removal of the delinquency from all credit reporting agencies due to the misleading or unclear autopay handling This issue stems from a breakdown in payment processing expectations rather than willful nonpayment. The continued reporting of this delinquency is unfair and damaging to my credit profile. 

Thank you for your time and review.

text:
This rebuttal is submitted to formally correct the record and respond to materially inaccurate, misleading, and incomplete statements made by NewRez Mortgage Company.

NewRezs response relies on half-truths, retroactive rationalizations, and the omission of material facts. The attached documentary evidence establishes that the delays in closing were caused by NewRezs own servicing failures, ineffective internal coordination, and deficient communicationsnot by any failure, delay, or lack of cooperation on my part.

Further, the facts described below raise serious concerns regarding NewRezs compliance with its mortgage servicing obligations, its duty of good faith and fair dealing, and the prohibition against unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) under applicable federal consumer protection laws.

________________________________________ 1. Shifting Documentation Requirements and Servicing Failures NewRez improperly attributes delays to alleged documentation deficiencies by the borrower. Each time documentation was requested, I complied promptly and in good faith. However, weeks after submission, NewRez repeatedly rejected previously submitted documents based on new or undisclosed requirements that had not been communicated at the time of the original request.

This pattern reflects deficient servicing practices, including inadequate intake controls, poor document review standards, and ineffective borrower communications, all of which are inconsistent with reasonable servicing expectations.

I had a previous loan from NewRez, loan number XXXX, for my condo. The loan process went smoothly and closed very quickly. So naturally, I thought very highly of the company and decided to get another one. This time, in XXXX, I entered into a nightmare. I had to fill out 2 applications for this condo loan, plus go through 2 closings. The first application, I started in XX/XX/XXXX. I worked with XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX. I submitted all documentation as asked. I increased the Flood Insurance amount as requested. I paid for pictures as instructed. Then I was told I should close around XXXX. 
I was totally confused when XXXX XXXX said I had to start a new application. I had to pay for more pictures and increase the flood insurance on my Condo. WHY? Because the XXXX XXXX did not approve of the application. I do not know the reason they did not approve of it. I do not even know what or who this organization is. 
I contacted the Insurance company once again with a new flood insurance number. I told NewRez that every time I change information, XXXX XXXX charges me a freaking fee. 
I sent in all documentation to NewRez as instructed. However, I was later informed weeks later on XX/XX/XXXX that all pages of bank statementsincluding blank pageswere required. This requirement was not disclosed initially. A mortgage servicer can not reasonably impose retroactive documentation standards and then attribute resulting delays to the borrower. For example, the XXXX information is just one example. It was sent on XX/XX/XXXX, but I had to go back and resend it because I got instructions from XXXX to redo all bank statements. So any and all previous bank statements had to be redone. This was a lot of work. 
I started the loan process in XX/XX/XXXX and closed approximately 5 months later in XX/XX/XXXX. 


________________________________________ 2. Defective Document Submission Infrastructure NewRez further attempts to attribute the delay to document submission issues while ignoring its own system failures. I made repeated, good-faith attempts to upload documentation through NewRezs online portal. On numerous occasions, the portal failed to function properly, loading indefinitely for 15 minutes or more without completing uploads.

I told NewRez several times that their portal was not functioning correctly. I kept getting error messages. I would close it down and reboot, but it still messed up. I even sent a screenshot to XXXX to show that I tried to upload the documents that she needed. I said the portal is not working again. It keeps going around in a circle for over 15 mins. She later told me she could not get the statements needed from a screenshot. DUH, no kidding, XXXX. A screenshot ( or screen grab ) is just a digital image of the current display on a computer screen, acting as a " photo '' of what you see. 
A servicers failure to maintain a reliable document submission system can not lawfully be shifted onto the borrower. Systemic portal failures constitute an internal servicing deficiency, not borrower inaction. 
________________________________________ 3. Material Misrepresentation Regarding IRS Payoff Letter Responsibility NewRezs claim that the delay resulted from my alleged failure to obtain an IRS payoff letter is materially false and misleading. 
Email correspondence attached to this rebuttal proves that for approximately XXXX month and a half, NewRez affirmatively represented that it would obtain the IRS payoff letter directly. During this period, I was repeatedly advised that NewRez was coordinating with XXXX XXXX of Mortgage Connection to secure the required documentation. I had to fill out forms for XXXX XXXX permitting him to get the payoff letter. See XX/XX/XXXX email. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX asks me for a formal IRS letter. 
Representing that NewRez would obtain the payoff letter while later blaming the borrower for delay constitutes a misrepresentation of servicing responsibilities and raises concerns under UDAAP prohibitions against deceptive acts or practices.

________________________________________ 4. Borrower Cooperation Disregarded At the request of XXXX XXXX, I completed authorization forms specifically intended to facilitate NewRezs efforts to obtain the IRS payoff letter. I complied fully, promptly, and without qualification. Despite this cooperation, NewRez failed to obtain the payoff letter and finally told me that I had to get it. Time consumed during this period resulted solely from NewRezs ineffective execution and inter-party coordinationnot borrower conduct. Attempting to recharacterize this period as borrower delay is false and unsupported by the record.

________________________________________ 5. Late Disclosure of Borrower Obligation and Unavoidable IRS Constraints It was not until XX/XX/XXXX, that NewRez first informed me that I was personally required to obtain the IRS payoff letter. Upon receipt of this instruction, I acted immediately. 
NewRez is presumed to understand that the Internal Revenue Service requires in-person appointments for issuance of payoff letters and that appointment availability is strictly controlled by the IRS. I have no authority over IRS scheduling or processing timelines. Nevertheless, I obtained the payoff letter at the earliest appointment made available.

Blaming the borrower for delays caused by known and unavoidable government processing constraints further reflects a lack of good-faith servicing.

________________________________________ 6. UDAAP, Servicing, and Good-Faith Concerns The conduct described above raises significant regulatory concerns, including but not limited to : Deceptive practices, by representing that NewRez would obtain the IRS payoff letter while later attributing delay to borrower inaction Unfair practices, by imposing undisclosed or shifting documentation standards and penalizing the borrower for noncompliance with unstated requirements Servicing deficiencies, including faulty systems, ineffective document review, and poor inter-party coordination Violation of the duty of good faith and fair dealing, by attempting to reassign responsibility for NewRezs internal failures after the fact. Collectively, these actions exhibit a pattern inconsistent with reasonable mortgage servicing standards and consumer protection obligations.

________________________________________ Conclusion As I previously notified NewRez Mortgage Company , the pattern, duration, and effect of the delays in my loan closing support a reasonable conclusion that these delays were not incidental, but the product of NewRezs servicing failures and internal breakdowns. NewRez Mortgage Company delayed my loan closing, which caused the IRS payoff amount to increase. This increased the total payoff NewRez required and raised my closing costs, causing me financial harm.

The documentary record establishes that the delays in closing were the direct result of NewRezs internal failures, miscommunications, and servicing breakdowns. At no point did I fail to act when provided with clear, accurate, and complete instructions.

Attempts by NewRez to shift blame to the borrower are contradicted by contemporaneous written evidence and appear to be a post hoc effort to deflect accountability. I respectfully request that this rebuttal and supporting documentation be given full consideration and that NewRezs prior statements be evaluated in light of the complete factual record and applicable regulatory standards.
label: Mortgage

I have been on an income-based repayment plan for my federal student loans since XXXX, prior to the SAVE plan. In XX/XX/XXXX, as soon as I learned that the SAVE plans 0.0 % interest forbearance was ending, I promptly applied to recertify my income-driven repayment plan so that my loans could return to an appropriate and affordable income-based payment amount. 
Instead of timely processing my request, MOHELA immediately began charging interest on my loans in XX/XX/XXXX, even though the SAVE 0.0 % interest forbearance remained active through the end of XXXX. I then waited month after month for my application to be processed. It was not until XX/XX/XXXX that I finally received notice that I had been approved for income-based repayment. 
However, the approval notice I received is deeply troubling and appears plainly erroneous. It states that my new monthly payment amount is {$3900.00}, with a first scheduled due date of XX/XX/XXXX. That monthly payment amount is more than my monthly income and is not remotely affordable. It is also completely inconsistent with my long history of income-based repayment, inconsistent with what I have previously paid, and inconsistent with the payment estimates provided through the federal StudentAid.gov system when I submitted my applications. 
When I submitted my recertification in XX/XX/XXXX, the estimated monthly payment shown was approximately {$420.00}. When I resubmitted in XX/XX/XXXX, the estimated monthly payment shown was approximately {$430.00}. The StudentAid.gov repayment calculator also states that under the Income-Based Repayment plan, payments are generally limited to 15 % of discretionary income and will never be more than the 10-year Standard Plan amount. A payment amount of {$3900.00} is not consistent with those terms and appears to reflect a serious servicing or calculation error. 
There is also a separate and equally serious problem with the timing of repayment. MOHELAs notice indicates that payments will not resume until late XXXX. That is unacceptable. I do not want to remain in a prolonged status in which I am prevented from making reasonable income-based payments and prevented from making progress toward applicable loan forgiveness. I want to begin making the correct, affordable income-based payments now. 
I anticipate that MOHELA may respond by noting that, when I applied for recertification, I selected the option to remain in forbearance rather than begin payments immediately. I selected that option for a very specific reason : I was concerned that MOHELA might miscalculate my payment amount and place me into an unaffordable payment status before the amount was correctly determined. Unfortunately, that is exactly what appears to have happened. My decision to remain in forbearance pending proper processing was not consent to an incorrect payment calculation, not consent to a multiyear delay in repayment, and not a waiver of my right to have my account accurately and timely serviced.

FH Cann & Associates is reporting a collection account on my credit report in the amount of {$5000.00} claiming the original creditor is XXXX University. This account was opened by FH Cann & Associates on XX/XX/year> and is currently reporting on XXXX  only it does not appear on my XXXX  or XXXX  credit reports. 
I have never received any written validation notice from FH Cann & Associates regarding this alleged debt as required under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g. This is my first formal contact disputing this account. 
This alleged debt originates from an educational institution and may involve the Return of Title IV Federal Financial Aid funds. When a student withdraws or stops attending a Title IV participating institution, federal regulations require the institution to calculate the amount of federal financial aid that must be returned using a specific federally mandated formula under 34 C.F.R. 668.22. The resulting institutional charge owed by the student if any must be calculated accurately and in full compliance with federal law. Any error in this calculation would make the reported balance inaccurate and unverifiable. 
FH Cann & Associates has not provided any of the following documentation required to validate this debt : Proof that FH Cann & Associates is licensed to collect debts in the State of Texas Complete documentation of my enrollment dates and official or unofficial withdrawal date as recorded by XXXX University The complete Return of Title IV calculation performed by XXXX University showing exactly how any institutional charge was determined Documentation showing how the alleged balance of {$5000.00} was calculated Any refund or credit applied to my account A copy of any original enrollment agreement or financial responsibility agreement signed by me Proof that the amount being collected is accurate and legally owed by me The exact date of first delinquency with the original creditor Without this complete documentation this debt can not be considered validated under the FDCPA or the FCRA. Educational institution debt involving federal financial aid is particularly complex and collectors almost never retain the complete federal calculation documentation necessary to fully validate such a debt. 
Additionally this account is currently reporting on XXXX  only and does not appear on my XXXX  or XXXX credit reports. This inconsistent reporting across the three major credit bureaus indicates that this information can not be fully and accurately verified and constitutes inaccurate reporting under the FCRA.

Despite failing to validate this debt FH Cann & Associates is currently reporting this unverified collection account on my XXXX  credit report which is negatively impacting my credit score and financial opportunities.

Under the FCRA 15 U.S.C. 1681 information reported to credit bureaus must be accurate complete and verifiable. An unvalidated debt does not meet this standard and should not be reporting on my credit file. 
I am requesting that the CFPB formally investigate this matter and require FH Cann & Associates to either provide complete and accurate debt validation within 30 days including all federal Title IV return of funds calculations or immediately remove this account permanently from my XXXX  credit report.

I am writing to formally document a series of regulatory violations that occurred both today and yesterday at Bank of America financial XXXX  # XXXX. As a business owner and the spouse of a 100 % XXXX veteran, I rely on the predictable liquidity of government funds. Bank of America has been our chosen financial institution for nearly XXXX  years. Today, Bank of America failed to meet its statutory obligations under the Expedited Funds Availability Act ( EFA Act ).

Statement of Facts : On XX/XX/year> at XXXX XXXX, I attempted to cash a state government warrant in the amount of {$2000.00}. I was informed that I may not cash the check but that I could deposit the check into my account and the funds would be available the following morning. An hour later I received a notice from my banking app that the check from the State Comptroller 's office which I had just deposited was now on a seven day hold. I immediately called customer service and was advised that the check was still processing and that they could only push the hold through if I called back the following day once the check had been processed. I waited until the following morning ( today ) and the check was still on hold. I attempted to speak with an associate on live chat through the official banking app with no success. I then visited branch # XXXX in person and requested the branch manager. Despite the check being a low-risk government item and well below the large-deposit threshold, the branch manager placed a multi-day hold on the funds. I remained in the branch for over 90 minutes seeking a resolution, which was summarily denied.

Regulatory Violations : Violation of Mandatory Next-Day Availability ( 12 CFR 229.10 ( c ) ) : Under Federal Law, state government checks deposited in person to a staffed teller station must be made available for withdrawal not later than the business day after the banking day on which the funds are deposited. The branch 's refusal to provide next-day access is a direct breach of this mandate.

Failure to Provide Statutory Notice of Exception ( 12 CFR 229.13 ( g ) ) : When a bank invokes an exception hold, it is legally required to provide the customer with a written notice at the time of deposit ( or by the next business day via mail ) stating the specific " Reasonable Cause '' for the hold. The branch manager explicitly refused my repeated requests for this documentation, stating incorrectly that general deposit disclosures were sufficient.

Refusal to Verify Funds Requirement : I provided the bank with the Texas Comptrollers Warrant Status Inquiry System to verify the checks validity. The bank explicitly refused to perform this verification or acknowledge the proof of validity, claiming that they have internet Proxy Blockers on their computers and Private Branch Exchange telephone lines. I offered to call the State Comptrollers office on my personal telephone and they rejected my offer stating they could not verify the validity of the office Im calling.

Misapplication of " Matching Funds '' Requirement : Branch staff informed me that the check would not be cashed because my account did not already contain the equivalent funds. Please be advised that Regulation CC contains no matching funds or recourse provision that overrides the mandatory availability of government warrants.

Failure of Administrative Oversight : The branch refused to exercise its delegated authority to perform a manual override, citing an inability to reach internal departments, thereby penalizing the consumer for the banks internal operational failures.

I opened the Best Buy credit card to purchase appliances approximately four years ago because I was told at the store that I would have no interest for 24 months. Based on that explanation, I understood that I would simply need to make my payments over the two-year period without being charged interest.

At no point was it clearly explained to me that if the full promotional balance was not completely paid off by the end of the 24 months, I would be charged retroactive interest on the entire original balance going back to day one. If I had been clearly informed of that, I would never have opened the account or agreed to those terms.

After the promotional period ended, I was hit with extremely high interest charges that caused my balance to increase significantly. Instead of being close to paying off the account, the deferred interest and additional fees pushed the balance over the credit limit. I feel this was misleading and unfair because the financing terms were not properly explained to me at the time of purchase.

I am requesting a full review of the account, a detailed explanation of all deferred interest charges, and consideration for removing or significantly reducing these charges due to the misleading way the financing was presented. I entered this agreement in good faith based on what I was told in the store, and I would like a fair resolution.

I am writing to file a formal complaint against XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX regarding a collection account ( Account XXXX. XXXX on XXXX, XXXX XXXXXXXX on XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  on XXXX  ) that XXXX is reporting on all three of my credit reports. This account, with a reported balance of {$5100.00}, is allegedly based on a debt from Westlake Financial Services. I dispute the accuracy and validity of this collection for multiple reasons documented below, supported by credit reports and dispute results from all three bureaus spanning from XXXX through XXXX. 

Issue 1 : Double-Reporting / Dual Tradeline Westlake Financial Services continues to report a charge-off of {$5100.00} on my credit reports as a closed account with " {$5100.00} written off. '' Simultaneously, XXXX XXXX XXXX reports a {$5100.00} collection for the same underlying debt. This means my credit reports show {$10000.00} in negative items for what is actually a single {$5100.00} obligation. Westlake 's account shows a {$0.00} balance as of XX/XX/XXXX, confirming the debt was transferred yet both tradelines remain on my credit reports, artificially inflating my reported delinquent debt. This violates FCRA Section 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), which requires furnishers to report accurate information, and FDCPA Section 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ), which prohibits false representation of the character, amount, or legal status of a debt.

Issue 2 : Unauthorized Hard Inquiries Before Account Assignment XXXX records show that XXXX XXXX XXXX made hard inquiries on my credit file on the following dates : XX/XX/XXXX ; XX/XX/XXXX ; and XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX 's own reported account opening and assignment date is XX/XX/XXXX. This means XXXX pulled my credit three times before the debt was even assigned to them. Hard inquiries require permissible purpose under FCRA Section 1681b ( a ) ( XXXX ) ( A ). XXXX had no permissible purpose to access my credit file before the debt was assigned. A fourth inquiry was made on XX/XX/XXXX. These unauthorized inquiries damaged my credit score and constitute willful violations of FCRA Section 1681b. 

Issue 3 : Sham Verifications Across Multiple Bureaus I have disputed this account multiple times across multiple credit bureaus, and each time the result has been a rubber-stamp verification with no meaningful investigation. My first XXXX  dispute, dated XX/XX/XXXX ( Report XXXX. XXXX ), resulted in " Remains '' XXXX certified the information as accurate with no changes. My second XXXX  dispute, dated XX/XX/XXXX ( Report XXXX. XXXX ), produced the identical outcome : " Remains, '' with the same certification. My XXXX  dispute, dated XX/XX/XXXX ( Confirmation No. XXXX ), resulted in " Verified and Updated '' but the only fields modified were " Additional Information, '' " Balance Date, '' and " Status Date. '' No substantive investigation was conducted into the accuracy of the underlying debt amount, the legitimacy of the collection assignment, or the double-reporting issue. These are textbook sham verifications. XXXX certified accuracy three times across two bureaus without addressing any of the substantive issues I raised : the double-reporting, the unauthorized inquiries, or the contradictory underlying Westlake data . 

Issue 4 : Underlying Debt Amount Was Never Properly Verified The {$5100.00} collection amount is based on Westlake Financial 's reported charge-off, but Westlake 's own data changed five times across six disputes. On XX/XX/XXXX, the balance was reported as {$7300.00} with a recent payment of {$590.00}. On XX/XX/XXXX, the balance changed to {$7100.00} with a recent payment of {$570.00}. On XX/XX/XXXX, the balance was reported as {$7300.00}, and the status changed to " Repossession. '' On XX/XX/XXXX, the balance dropped to {$5100.00}, the status changed to " Charge-Off, '' and the recent payment changed to {$570.00}. On XX/XX/XXXX, the balance was reported as {$0.00}, with a status of " Closed. {$5100.00} written off, '' and the recent payment inexplicably changed to {$2800.00}. XXXX is collecting {$5100.00} based on data from an original creditor whose own records were never stable or verified. When I disputed XXXX 's account, they simply re-certified the {$5100.00} figure without independently verifying it against Westlake 's contradictory records.

Issue 5 : Conflicting Information Across Bureaus The data XXXX furnishes differs across the three major credit bureaus in material ways. Removal dates differ : XXXX  reports " On Record Until XX/XX/XXXX '' while XXXX  reports " Estimated month and year this item will be removed XX/XX/XXXX '' a two-month discrepancy. There is also an address discrepancy : the XXXX  dispute result ( Confirmation No. XXXX ) lists XXXX  's address as " XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, NY XXXX '' with phone number ( XXXX ) XXXX, while the XXXX  credit report dated XX/XX/XXXX, and the XXXX  credit report list " XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, CT XXXX '' with phone number ( XXXX ) XXXX. The date of first delinquency is reported by XXXX  as XX/XX/XXXX this date should be consistent across all bureaus but varies in how it is reflected in the removal date calculations. These inconsistencies demonstrate that the bureaus are not conducting meaningful reinvestigations and that XXXX is furnishing inconsistent data to different bureaus. 

Issue 6 : FDCPA Violations XXXX is a " debt collector '' as defined by 15 U.S.C. Section 1692a ( 6 ) they purchased or were assigned this debt from Westlake Financial after the account was charged off. Reporting a collection amount based on unverified, contradictory original creditor data constitutes a false representation of the amount of a debt in violation of Section 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ). Continuing to report after disputes without conducting a meaningful investigation violates Section 1692e ( 8 ) communicating credit information known or which should be known to be false. The double-reporting, whereby both Westlake 's charge-off and XXXX 's collection appear simultaneously, constitutes an unfair practice under Section 1692f by artificially inflating reported delinquent debt. XXXX 's unauthorized hard inquiries constitute unfair practices under Section 1692f ( 1 ).

I have disputed this account multiple times across multiple bureaus. Each time, XXXX has certified its accuracy without conducting a genuine investigation. The double-reporting, the unauthorized credit pulls before the debt was even assigned, the contradictory underlying data from Westlake, and the inconsistencies across bureaus all demonstrate that XXXX is not reporting accurate information and is not complying with its obligations under federal law. Complaint : I am filing a complaint regarding a private student loan issued by Ascent Funding for enrollment at Devslopes, an online education provider that permanently closed during my enrollment period. 

I enrolled in XXXX in XX/XX/year> and took out a loan through Ascent Funding with the expectation of completing the program and improving my earning potential. In XX/XX/year>, XXXX ceased operations before the program was completed. As a result, I was unable to complete the education or receive the full value of the services for which the loan was issued. 

Despite the schools closure and the incomplete delivery of educational services, I remain responsible for repayment of this loan.

I have acted in good faith throughout this process : I have remained current on all payments I promptly notified Ascent of the school closure I formally disputed the loan and requested relief I cooperated fully with their review process Ascent acknowledged the school closure and placed my account in temporary forbearance at 0 % interest. They also confirmed that their executive and legal teams reviewed the situation.

However, Ascent has denied full relief and instead offered a 50 % balance reduction as a courtesy, while maintaining that they are not responsible for the schools closure. They have since stated that no further relief, adjustments, or discharge options are available.

This outcome leaves me responsible for a significant remaining balance tied to an education that I was unable to complete due to circumstances entirely outside of my control.

Additionally, this situation has created financial hardship for my household. I am supporting a young child, and my partners ability to work is limited due to childcare responsibilities and health constraints. While I have continued to make payments to protect my credit, the remaining balance represents a substantial burden given the lack of educational value received.

I am requesting that Ascent Funding : Reconsider full discharge of the remaining balance due to failure of consideration Alternatively, provide additional balance reduction beyond the current 50 % offer Remove any interest accrued after the date of the schools closure Confirm that my account will not be negatively reported while this matter is under review I believe it is unfair to require repayment of a loan for educational services that were not fully delivered due to the schools closure. I am seeking a fair and reasonable resolution.
